News.title: SAS veterans of Troubles must be spared endless threat of legal repercussions, warns former Armed Forces minister
News.content:
SAS veterans who fought the IRA must not be left facing “endless legal jeopardy” decades after the Troubles, former Armed Forces Minister Al Carns has warned.

The ex-Royal Marine backed a new report warning ageing troops risk fresh investigations and possible prosecution under Labour’s Troubles Bill.



The Tories’ 2023 Legacy Act offered conditional immunity from prosecution to people accused of Troubles offences if they co-operated with the independent body investigating legacy cases.

Labour’s legislation would scrap that immunity and allow some civil claims and inquests to resume.



Mr Carns said: “No soldier should be above the law. Equally, no soldier should face endless legal jeopardy.

“Accountability is not the same as perpetual investigation. Justice is not served when the process itself becomes the punishment.



“That is why this paper matters. It gives voice to men who were there, making decisions almost impossible to recreate 40 or 50 years later.”

Policy Exchange is demanding ministers scrap the draft legislation, block new inquests and inquiries and be prepared to face down Strasbourg.

But speaking in Belfast last week, Andy Burnham said the Bill would be brought back to Parliament in the autumn.

A Government spokesperson said: “There was no equivalence between the lawful service of our veterans and the sickening deliberate actions of the terrorists.



“We will make that clear in the Bill, and introduce a package of new, effective and lawful protections for our former service personnel.”

News.title: Cops open fire on ‘woman with a knife’ in Times Square in front of terrified tourists
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

GUN HORROR Cops open fire on ‘woman with a knife’ in Times Square in front of terrified tourists

POLICE have opened fire on a woman who allegedly stabbed two in Times Square, New York.

Shots were fired in the packed tourist hotspot during a reported knifepoint robbery at 4:27pm.



Cops gunned down the blade-carrying fiend between Seventh Avenue West and 42nd and 43rd Streets.

Eyewitnesses said she had been threatening people with two knives – before allegedly stabbing two.



The woman – who cops have described as “emotionally disturbed” – then fled the scene and raced north towards the NYPD substation.

Confronted by cops at the station, the woman refused to lay down her knives, police say.

Following the shooting, the woman has been rushed to hospital in “critical condition”, reported NBC Connecticut.

It is unclear precisely what injuries have been sustained by the suspect.

Horrifying videos circulating online show the woman – in jeans – lying on the ground as police officers swarm around her – appearing to give CPR.

Streets in the surrounding area have been cordonned off following the dramatic showdown.



Police sources have not yet confirmed the condition of the two people who were stabbed.

The attacks are not being treated as a terror incident.

Breaking news…More to follow…

News.title: Burnham must learn how to make strong decisions and stick to them or he’s in for a very bumpy autumn
News.content:
Get real, PM

SUMMER is at an end and with it our new Prime Minister’s honeymoon.

So far Andy Burnham has enjoyed the cushiest of rides in Downing Street.



Since taking the reins he has splashed YOUR cash including billions on a £45 cut to energy bills and capping bus fares at two quid.

He’s also been out and about on a tour of the country which brought only one real announcement: an unnecessary crackdown on heavily regulated High Street bookies which he bizarrely compared to money-laundering vape shops.



To paraphrase another Northern comedian, Eric Morecambe, guitar-botherer Burnham has been desperate to show that he is playing all the right notes, just not necessarily in the same order as his predecessor Keir Starmer.

Today, though, the music stops.



As Labour MPs return to Westminster, they will be looking to him to deliver on Britain’s REAL problems: defence, welfare and a flatlining economy.

So far the signs have not been good.

Burnham has also got himself into a huge mess over Labour’s early prisoner release scheme — unnecessarily causing immense worry and heartache for the family of PC Andrew Harper before finally keeping his killers behind bars.

In doing so, he is also about to free hundreds of highly dangerous prisoners serving indeterminate sentences.



Of the 2,271 still on them, 1,415 already had to be recalled after offending on release.

They include Joseph McCann, who was freed in 2019 but went on to commit 37 offences — including the abduction and rape of 11 women and children.

Is that really the kind of gamble with public safety that any PM should take?

Cavalier Burnham has already shown he has a track record of overpromising then caving in to pressure.

He is already rowing back from committing to spending three per cent of GDP on defence.



And despite paying lip service to the idea, he still has no serious plans to slash welfare.

Endless U-turns ruined Keir Starmer’s premiership and left Britain stuck in the grip of decline.

If Burnham can’t make strong decisions and stick to them, he is in for a very bumpy autumn.

Team to shine

NO ONE can deny Kemi Badenoch has transformed her fortunes as party leader.

Now she is setting about building a team around her who can give the Tories a chance at the next election.



New Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith has more business experience than Labour’s entire Cabinet — and wants to cut taxes.

Ex-Army officer Tom Tugendhat, now Shadow Foreign Secretary, knows all about Chinese and Russian aggression.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kemi knows she has to win back the trust of former Conservative voters.

Offering proper solutions to fix Britain’s stuttering economy will go a long way towards that.

News.title: Labour is so obsessed with attacking Israel it doesn’t realise a trade ban will cost PALESTINIAN jobs
News.content:
IMAGINE Britain had an ally whose intelligence know-how was so vital to our safety that the head of MI5 said the ally had “disrupted a huge quantity of terror activity inside the UK” and “saved many, many lives on British soil”.

Imagine the same ally’s military equipment had saved the lives of British soldiers in Iraq and Afghanistan.



Then imagine the ally was also a huge market for British trade, buying £3.2billion of British products a year and so backing huge numbers of British jobs.

That ally doesn’t need to be imagined. It’s Israel.



More than 1.7million of us work for firms exporting to Israel.

One in eight of the drugs dispensed by the NHS comes from Israeli companies.



Israel ranks eighth per capita among countries investing in the UK.

Almost anyone using a mobile phone is using Israeli tech.

There has long been a lobby within Labour that regards Israel not as an ally to be cherished but an enemy to be attacked.

The Labour Government has spent the past two years doing just that.



Now PM Andy Burnham is poised to go a stage further by banning the import of any goods produced in the West Bank — the disputed region which the Palestinians claim as their own but on which Israel has been building settlements for many years.

The ostensible reason for the sanctions is that Israel is planning to build homes in an area of the West Bank known as E1.

Labour says this will destroy all hope of a two-state settlement.

Yet in every peace plan for the region, from Oslo to Camp David and beyond, E1 has been marked as remaining under Israeli sovereignty.

There is no conceivable peace plan in which it would be part of a Palestinian state.

The truth is that this is just an excuse.



For a huge number of Labour MPs, attacking Israel has become core to their world view.

They are so consumed by “Palestinianism” — the ideology and mindset that puts the campaign for a Palestinian state above everything else — that they will not rest until Israel is brought to heel.

Burnham is now doing their bidding.



One of the first things he did on his return to Parliament was to apologise for “Labour’s initial response to the treatment of Gaza”.

He said: “We got it wrong and I am sorry for that.”

But there is also another factor at work. The emergence of a sectarian Muslim vote has changed politics on the Left.

In the last General Election, so-called Independent Gaza candidates won four seats and came very close in others.

The Muslim population is over 20 per cent in 37 constituencies, and there are another 73 seats where the Muslim population is between ten and 20 per cent.



Labour MPs are terrified they will be booted out at the next election.

Everything Labour does with regard to Israel should be seen in that context.

It is all about showing the sectarian Muslim vote that Labour is their party.

The sanctions have nothing to do with helping Palestinians because they will be hit the hardest.

Roughly 30,000 Palestinians work in the settlement economy, earning several times what Palestinian employers pay elsewhere.



A goods ban would cut their income without shifting Israeli policy at all.

As for the impact here, it’s physically impossible to separate all goods produced on the West Bank from other goods.

There is no overall labelling system when they are exported from Israel. So this is really a bar on the import of all Israeli goods.



If Burnham thinks the Israelis are just going to sit back and accept such treatment, he must be even more out of his depth than he already seems.

As I’ve explained, we need Israel’s technological, military and intelligence expertise far more than they need us.

When the Israelis respond, we will be the ones who suffer.

Just look at Ireland. In 2024, Micheal Martin, the then-defence minister and now Irish PM, ordered the removal of an Israeli-made navigation system from Ireland’s new official jet because it would have required a deal with Elbit Systems, an Israeli defence firm.

That jet is now unable to land in fog or rough weather.



Perhaps Burnham thinks it is a good idea to ensure that the RAF won’t be able to fly its planes because they depend on Israeli technology.

(And, by the way, Israel is the UK’s second largest defence supplier — and doesn’t buy British weapons. This is one-way traffic.)

When Israel alone is singled out for boycotts — there is nothing over the Western Sahara, Northern Cyprus, China or any other conflict except Ukraine — it also changes the atmosphere at home.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

At a time when antisemitism is on the rampage, it is British Jews who will bear the brunt of the impact.

Next time you hear Burnham or any Labour minister say they deplore anti-semitism, remember they are shameless hypocrites.

News.title: Fury as lags who ‘behave themselves’ at UK’s most violent jail can get a bigger TV in their cell in ‘bit of a p**s take’
News.content:
INMATES who “behave themselves” at Britain’s most violent prison can get a bigger TV in their cell, a report reveals.

Bosses at 500-capacity HMP Brinsford, Staffs, decide if inmates have a standard 15in TV or are upgraded to a screen of 24in or more, based on behaviour.



Over 12 months, 527 assaults were recorded at the jail, which is also a young offenders’ institute, the HM Prisons Inspectorate report said.

But prisons’ chief inspector Charlie Taylor said he had “optimism things will improve”.



A report from Charlie Taylor, the Chief Inspector of Prisons, praised the jail – the most violent in the UK – for rewarding well-behaved cons and encouraging ‘positive behaviour’.

He said: “Well-behaved prisoners had access to some benefits, such as bigger televisions and additional association time.”

He added that inmates on the basic level of privileges struggled to progress, adding: “There was limited support to help prisoners on the lowest level of the scheme to progress.”

The report also revealed the staggering level of violence at the jail, with 527 assaults in the most recent 12-month period.

Mr Taylor said: “Levels of violence were very high. The rate of violent incidents was the highest in the adult male estate.

“Rates of violence against staff had more than doubled, (and) violence (against other prisoners) was often driven by interpersonal issues and bullying.”



But an insider said: “TVs in cells do keep offenders occupied — but giving them bigger tellies just because they’ve not kicked off recently is a bit of a p**s take.”

News.title: I was raped by 50 men after grooming gang targeted me at 14 – ordeal broke me but abusers STILL threaten me from jail
News.content:
BRUTALLY abused by a grooming gang from the age of 14, brave Fiona Goddard battled years of trauma to rebuild her life and protect her own children.

But news that one of her attackers, Mohammed Usman, was last week freed early from prison has left the mum-of-six’s world “falling apart”.



Fiona, 33 — who has waived her right to anonymity — is now in a safe house with her young kids, aged between one and 12, terrified that her court testimony which helped nail nine of her abusers in 2019 will bring devastating repercussions.

She has already received threats to firebomb her home from her attackers’ acquaintances.



Vile Usman served only half of his 15-year stretch for abusing Fiona because he was sentenced before a change to the law in 2020, which now requires some serious offenders to do two-thirds of their time behind bars.

Speaking exclusively to The Sun, Fiona — who was raped and beaten by at least 50 men after a grooming gang first targeted her in 2008 while she lived in a Bradford children’s home — said: “The whole ordeal has left me feeling broken.



“Since news of Usman’s release, I’ve had countless threats on social media that my home would be set on fire with me and my children inside and my abusers would come to deliver ‘real justice’ when they get out of prison.

“I feel terrified. I have been accused of making up my abuse and told that the perpetrators are victimised, innocent men.



“How is it fair that my children and I are still living in fear after all I’ve been through?”

Her story comes as Prime Minister Andy Burnham bowed to a million-strong petition backed by The Sun this weekend and announced yet more changes to the early release scheme aimed at easing prison overcrowding.

While this means perpetrators of unlawful killing and historical sex offences will now be barred from early release, it doesn’t apply to Fiona’s case.



However, she said: “I’m still glad for other survivors.

“It’s common sense that the worst crimes like rape, child sexual abuse and murder are all excluded from early release.

“I went through a lot to make sure those men went to prison.



“When I heard the sentence Mohammed Usman was originally given of at least 17 years, I felt relieved.

“But then it was reduced to 15 on appeal, and then, after just seven-and-a-half years, he has been released.

“It’s unreal. I live in fear. Where’s the justice in that?”

Growing up, Fiona was extremely vulnerable due to a difficult childhood, making her easy prey.

She said: “I was exposed to domestic violence in my childhood and my mother suffered her own mental health issues. This led to instability and I was placed in care.



“I just wanted love and attention.”

The abuse started after Fiona ran away from the home with a friend.

She encountered an associate of a gang of highly dangerous, drug-dealing criminals who ensnared girls for their own sexual pleasure, as well as “renting them out” to business associates and other relatives.

‘Scheme deeply unfair to victims’ DURING the 40-plus years I have been campaigning to end men’s violence against women and girls, I have rarely heard a story as harrowing as Fiona’s. Don’t get me wrong, all of the cases I have written about are truly terrible – child sexual abuse within the home; rape by a man wielding a weapon; sustained domestic violence; and coercive control stripping the victim of any sense of worth. I have sat in murder trials, holding back tears on the press bench as details of dreadful sex murders are recounted. But interviewing Fiona has had a huge impact on me. Desperate for love and attention, she was targeted and groomed by wicked men. The fact she survived and went on to advocate for so many other victims of these vile gangs is commendable. I am sickened at her abuse, but extremely privileged to know Fiona and to campaign alongside her. It is terrible that she is now reliving this nightmare. This early release scheme is deeply unfair to victims. We owe Fiona, and all girls put through this type of hell, a commitment to listen and ensure men who ruin lives get locked up for a long time – and serve their full term.

At 16, she gave birth to her first baby, a girl, but while she was still being abused, social services removed her daughter, who was later adopted.

“No one helped me during that time,” said Fiona. “The abusers got away with it.”



At 17, she finally escaped the gang’s clutches after moving area. But life after the abuse was difficult and she suffered with agoraphobia for years.

She also became addicted to substances and ended up in an abusive relationship.

Fiona explained: “I suffered nightmares. Then, in 2013, the police turned up asking questions about an investigation into grooming gang crimes. I realised I could not move forward with my life until I faced what had happened.”

In 2019, Fiona’s determination to testify in court meant nine of her abusers — Usman, Basharat Khaliq, Saeed Akhtar, Naveed Akhtar, Parvaze Ahmed, Zeeshan Ali, Fahim Iqbal, Izar Hussain and Kieran Harris — were sent to jail, with sentences ranging from 18 months to 20 years.

While relieved to have secured justice of sorts, Fiona said: “This was the tip of the iceberg.



“At least 50 men raped and abused me during this time.

“Some weren’t prosecuted because the police couldn’t trace them.

“When people believe they are unlikely to be caught or face meaningful consequences, it can create a dangerous sense that they can act without fear of repercussions.”

Just seven years on, all but one of those locked up have become eligible for early release.

To make matters worse, Fiona says she has been harassed online since February by people she believes are associates of grooming gang members. Last week, it got so bad she was moved to the safe house.



She says: “I was reported to anti-terrorism police for being a far-right radical, and to social services. Thankfully, they didn’t take it seriously.

“I’ve been called a s**g and also had people laughing about me being gang raped. It’s sickening.

“My children don’t realise yet what’s happening, but they can’t even play outside without me watching them constantly. My oldest daughter is so upset, missing her best friend.”

Fiona says she reported the harassment to police after receiving “countless” messages from anonymous accounts telling her she was being watched, and her mental health suffered.

She added: “My doctor saw the state I was in, so prescribed me anti-anxiety and depression pills.”



Despite everything, Fiona continues to travel the country campaigning and advocating for survivors.

But she says that inside, she is “falling apart”, adding: “Your home should be your safe space and that’s been taken from me. I’m in fight or flight all the time.”

Of her home move, she added: “I felt like that little girl again . . . I was in danger if I stayed in the house where the abusers could find me.

“At least I know my kids are safe and I can go to sleep without thinking anyone’s going to come through the door.”

Fiona wonders why victims have to “fight and fight” for justice and to feel protected, while evil Usman managed to get his original sentence reduced on appeal by saying he did charity work in Pakistan while on the run from rape charges.



She is understandably angry about the way the Government has failed to take decisive action over early release.

Referring to their latest U-turn, which excludes perpetrators of unlawful killing and historical sex offences, she says: “A government that can’t stick by its own decisions, whether right or wrong, shows weakness.

“I’m in temporary accommodation and I don’t believe people in parliament have any idea of the real-life implications of some of the legislation that they pass.

“We need legislation to make sure that licence conditions are much stricter and to make sure they face the consequences if they step out of line.”

Last month, asylum seekers arriving in the UK were handed booklets warning them that sex with children is illegal, and that men and women are equal under UK law.



The nine-page document, published by the Home Office, also told migrants they understood “laws and customs here may be different from your home country”.

Now, Fiona is once again trying to move on for the sake of her family.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “I am trying to rebuild my life. I won’t stop campaigning until systems are put in place to make sure that these dangerous men are taken off the streets and kept in custody until they are no longer a danger.

“We deserve justice and they deserve punishment.”

News.title: Cops arrest 315 on final day of iconic Notting Hill Carnival as police probe knife crimes and licence breaches
News.content:
POLICE have arrested 351 people on Notting Hill Carnival’s final day as the party comes to a close after millions flocked to the streets.

The arrests were related to several offences including possession of a handgun and sexual offender licence breaches.



This brings the total number of arrests over the celebration to 560.

The annual west London carnival is Europe’s biggest street party and billed by organisers as “the greatest community-led event on the planet”.



It attracts an estimated two million people every year.

However, a large celebration can sometimes bring chaos, as police reveal the number of arrests made at the celebration’s closing day.

Cops claim that 48 of the arrests were down to live facial recognition.

Cameras also allowed police to track down 43 sexual offenders to ensure they were complying with license conditions.



The Met Police claim arrests may increase as the evening goes on.

Tragically, one man lost his life entering a canal during the celebration.

It is understood the individual, believed to be in his 20s, fled from police on foot at around 3pm.

Not long after he entered the water where officers and paramedics pulled him out.

Despite the best efforts of emergency services, the man later died in hospital.



Earlier this week, the force said more than 7,000 officers would be deployed to west London over the bank holiday weekend.

The carnival includes parades, live music, street food and sound stages and is celebrating its 60th anniversary this year.

But while officers responded to a number of incidents, they said “the mood has been overwhelmingly positive and celebratory”.

Yesterday’s opening celebration saw a total of 243 arrests, including drugs and sexual offences, and two knife attacks.

In 2025, the Met said it made 528 arrests across the two main days of the carnival, including 167 for drug offences, 50 for possession of an offensive weapon, 21 for sexual offences, four for violence with injury and 49 for other violence.



In 2024, there were eight stabbings, including the murder of 32-year-old mother Cher Maximen, with the same number the previous year, and seven including a murder in 2022.

The festival, which first took place in 1966, got off to a colourful start yesterday as partygoers filled the streets.

Things kicked off with J’ouvert, the tradition of throwing paint to welcome in the morning on the first day of the carnival.

The opening day, also known as Family Day, saw thousands of revellers celebrating the event’s 60th anniversary.

A spokesperson for Notting Hill Carnival Limited said: “Notting Hill Carnival 2026 has been a fantastic celebration of the 60th anniversary of an iconic event. Tens of thousands of performers have lit up the streets of London and made us all proud, while honouring the pioneers of this incredible legacy.



“Carnival is constantly evolving and as we continue to take further responsibility for crowd and wider event management, we are pleased that the success of the operation allows our partners to concentrate on their core purpose.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Often the number of arrests at Carnival is a focus and it should be understood that this is a tiny proportion of the up to 2 million attendees a year.

“Notting Hill Carnival is a victim of crime too, it does not cause it and we thank our partners for their vital work in making sure the overwhelming majority can revel in the joy of our great event.”

News.title: Travellers’ Bank Hol ‘land grab’ on wildlife haven near Rod Stewart’s mansion BLOCKED by cops to relief of fuming locals
News.content:
DEFIANT villagers celebrated after a 24-hour vigil to stop a land grab by travellers ended with police turfing workers off the site.

Up to 100 locals watched over the wildlife area — less than a mile from Sir Rod Stewart’s £4.65million mansion — after diggers turned up at the weekend.



Workers began putting in fences and hardcore and laying pipes on the wetland and nature reserve in Sawbridgeworth, Herts.

The travellers, who recently bought three fields in the area, ignored a temporary stop notice from East Herts District Council on Saturday and also refused access to Environment Agency officials concerned by the effect of pipework on the nearby River Stort.



Residents monitored the site through Sunday night as the council sought an injunction — and when the workers returned at 8am yesterday, police quickly arrived.

Locals said officers threatened the travellers with arrest if work continued — thanks to a sweeping High Court injunction obtained early yesterday that has banned further development and caravans or mobile homes being occupied.

One resident said: “It was a festival atmosphere overnight.

“We were warned not to interfere when the travellers came back, just to let them start working but tell the police as soon as the injunction was broken.



“They came and turfed them out quickly and they say they will now keep guard.”

A bare-chested, tattooed security guard stayed on the site and said: “I’m here to stop anybody coming on to this land who might try to remove or destroy the machinery.”

One local called Laura, 45, said: “I love to walk here with my son but now there’s nothing left of it.



“They’ve destroyed the habitat for the wildlife.”

Another High Court hearing is due on September 15.

News.title: 'No parent should lie awake worrying about uniform costs or breakfast when help is there'
News.content:
'No parent should lie awake worrying about uniform costs or breakfast when help is there'

EXCLUSIVE: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says many parents are missing out on cost-saving help for school simply because they do not know they have a right to more support

View 2 Images Parents can save hundreds of pounds with back to school help

The start of the school year for children across the country is full of excitement: reuniting with friends, meeting new teachers and, for many, exploring a new school.

‌



For us parents, however, September can bring a sense of dread as the back-to-school bills come flooding in. School uniforms, lunches and childcare all need to be organised and paid for on top of everyday household bills.

‌



That's why I want every parent to get the support they are entitled to. From the start of term, families across the country can benefit from more support with back-to-school costs through thousands of free breakfast clubs across the country, childcare support, cheaper school uniforms and importantly our historic expansion of free school meals to three million children.

‌



Thousands of students celebrate GCSE results day - but regional divide widens READ MORE :

View 2 Images Education Secretary Lucy Powell said measures will offer breathing room to struggling families (Image: Getty Images)

But I know that many parents are missing out simply because they do not know they have a right to more support. Some of this is down to perception. We assume that help is only for those in the toughest circumstances. While those families absolutely benefit, we have expanded support to help many more families manage back-to-school costs.

As a parent, I know that our focus is on seeing our children happy, confident and thriving at school. But too often, the pressure of household bills can distract us from that.

‌



And research shows that around a third are cutting back on treats and snacks or are turning to batch cooking to make their budgets stretch further during term time, while one in ten have relied on a food bank or community service for support.

The variety of support now on offer for families could have a huge impact. Families benefiting from free school meals, free breakfast clubs and cheaper uniforms could save up to £1,200 per child. Eligible working parents using government-funded childcare could save up to £8,000 a year per child.

No parent should be lying awake at night worrying about uniform costs or breakfast when help is available. I urge every family, as we head back to school and nursery, to check whether they are eligible for support.

‌



This is significant support that can give families greater financial breathing space, allowing them to spend less time worrying about how everything will add up. It means they can focus on supporting their child's learning, encouraging their ambitions and helping them make the most of school life.

And while we're helping families with the pressures they face at home, we're equally determined to ensure every child gets the brilliant education they deserve.

As families settle back into the routine of a new school year, we'll be focused on raising standards, widening opportunity and delivering an education system that gives every young person a clear route to success.

Article continues below

Because September should be about children looking ahead to the future with confidence, not parents worrying about how they're going to pay for it.

News.title: Small boat crossings drop to seven-year low over summer despite hot weather
News.content:
Small boat crossings drop to seven-year low over summer despite hot weather

Latest figures show a sharp drop in small boat crossings in June, July and August - but Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood admitted there is more to do

View 2 Images Small boat arrivals fell dramatically over the summer, figures show (Image: PA)

Small boat crossings were at their lowest in seven years this summer despite the hot weather, new figures show.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood welcomed a dramatic fall in the number of people making the dangerous journey, but said there is more to be done. Arrivals dropped by 46% in June, July and August compared to last year.

Data released by the Home Office show the lowest total crossings since 2019 and the lowest number of people reaching the UK since 2020. There were 7,416 arrivals between June 1 and August 30 - compared to 15,458 over the same period in 2022 and 12,421 in 2022 under the Tories.

Ms Mahmood said: “This Government is committed to restoring order at our border. This work is beginning to bear fruit, with June, July and August recording the lowest number of small boat crossings in seven years.

Early prison release scheme - how it works and what has changed under Andy Burnham READ MORE :

View 2 Images Shabana Mahmood said there is more to be done (Image: Dan Kitwood/PA Wire)

"But we know there is more to do. We will be relentless in targeting the criminal gangs behind these crossings, and we will continue to remove the incentives that draw people here on unsafe and illegal routes."

Earlier this year Ms Mahmood signed a new agreement with France to ramp up police enforcement on French beaches by 40%. In the first three months 185 small boat crossings were prevented - 61% of the dangerous journeys in that time.

The government faces pressure to tackle crossings, with a record 230 people packed onto a single boat raising the alarm last month. Ms Mahmood is pushing through a raft of measures, including a streamlined appeals process and a new charge of around £10,000 for successful asylum seekers to pay for the support while they waited for a decision.

But many Labour MPs are concerned about the proposals, while campaign groups have called on the government to instead focus on ramping up safe routes to end the reliance on smuggling gangs.

Since the general election in 2024, more than 48,000 crossing attempts have been prevented, the Home Office said. More than 1,100 boats and engings have been seized by the National Crime Agency, and returns are at their highest level in a decade.

The number of people in asylum hotels has been halved in a year, and the asylum backlog fell by 56% in the year to June 30.

This week Andy Burnham is set to meet French President Emmanuel Macron in Downing Street. Tackling small boat crossings and strengthening border security cooperation will be at the top of the agenda.

It comes after Reform UK announced plans to dispatch the Royal Navy in the Channel, only for the proposal to swiftly collapse. France said Nigel Farage's proposal would violate French sovereignty as it torpedoed the headline-grabbing idea.

News.title: Times Square shooting horror as police open fire during New York 'knifepoint robbery'
News.content:
Times Square shooting horror as police open fire during New York 'knifepoint robbery'

The New York Police Department (NYPC) said shots were fired at a woman in Times Square after two people were stabbed and rushed to hospital with life-threatening injuries

View 2 Images A 'police-involved' shooting has shaken Times Square (Image: Twitter/X/austen_tv)

Police have shot a woman in New York City's Times Square following a reported knifepoint robbery during which two people were stabbed.

‌



The New York Police Department (NYPD) said shots were fired at 4:27pm local time (9:27pm UK time) between Seventh Avenue West and 42nd and 43rd Streets.

‌



According to police sources, a woman who appeared to be emotionally disturbed began threatening people with two knives, reports ABC7.

‌



At 4:26pm, the New York City Fire Department (FDNY) arrived at the scene following a report of a stabbing.

Police said the woman had stabbed two people, a man and a woman, then fled north toward the NYPD substation where police confronted her.

‌



View 2 Images A person has been shot in New York City's Times Square (Image: Twitter/X/austen_tv)

When approached, the woman refused to put the knives down, police said. The woman, along with the two victims who were stabbed, were rushed to the hospital with life-threatening injuries.

Dozens of emergency vehicles swarmed the busy intersection, with streets closed down to allow police to carry out an investigation of the scene.

Article continues below

Officers have urged the public to avoid West 43rd Street and Seventh Avenue, an area usually packed with tourists taking in Time Square's iconic glowing billboards.

The condition of the woman is unknown at this time.
