News.title: Mum and daughters, 16 and 20, killed in California crash with car going in wrong direction
News.content:
Mum and daughters, 16 and 20, killed in California crash with car going in wrong direction

Vanessa Wetmore, 41, and daughters Kylie, 20, and Kloie, 16, were driving home from a concert when they were hit by a car going in the wrong direction on a busy California highway

View 4 Images The family were hit by a vehicle travelling in the wrong direction (Image: Jam Press/GoFundMe)

A mum and her two daughters have been killed after their car was struck by a wrong-way driver before bursting into flames on a busy highway.

‌



Vanessa Wetmore, 41, Kylie, 20, and Kloie, 16, were heading home from a concert to celebrate Kloie's upcoming birthday when the tragedy unfolded. The teenager's birthday was just four days away, falling on the same day as her brother Seth, 16.

‌



The family were travelling along California's Highway 99 near Bakersfield shortly after midnight on Sunday, August 16, when a BMW travelling in the wrong direction collided with their Honda. They were all pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



Kylie was driving, with her mum and younger sister travelling as passengers. The California Highway Patrol said a 2019 BMW 530i was heading north in the southbound lanes, with the collision also involving a 2022 Chevrolet Colorado.

View 4 Images The family had travelling home from a concert in Fresno (Image: Jam Press/GoFundMe)

The Wetmore family's Honda became engulfed in flames before emergency services arrived at the scene, north of Seventh Standard Road, and pronounced them dead.

‌



The police patrol later identified the driver of the BMW as 44-year-old Jamie Rodriguez, of Tulare. He suffered serious injuries and was taken to hospital, while two people travelling in the Chevrolet sustained minor injuries.

Investigators are continuing to establish how the BMW ended up travelling against traffic, including where it entered the highway and whether drugs or alcohol played a role. No criminal charges have so far been filed in connection with the crash.

A GoFundMe launched to cover funeral expenses and support Seth has raised $87,084 (£64,500) from more than 960 donations.

‌



An update shared by organiser Dale Schoettler said the support would allow Seth to focus on grieving without worrying about his immediate future.

View 4 Images Vanessa (R), Kylie (L) and Kloie (C) Wetmore (Image: Jam Press/GoFundMe)

"We truly cannot put into words how grateful we are for the incredible amount of love and support that has been shown to our family," Dale wrote.

‌



"Because of all of you, Seth will be able to give his family the services they deserve and honor Vanessa, Kloie and Kylie in the way they deserve to be honoured.

"That alone takes an enormous weight off his shoulders during a time when he should not have to worry about anything other than grieving and being surrounded by the people who love him."

The family hope the fundraiser will give Seth some stability as he faces a future without his mum and sisters.

‌



Dale added: "There is no amount of money that can make any of this okay, but the support this community has given Seth and his family means more than we could ever explain."

View 4 Images Vanessa Wetmore died in the crash (Image: Jam Press/GoFundMe)

Vanessa, Kylie and Kloie had travelled to Fresno to see Thee Sacred Souls, La Lom and The Womack Sisters perform as an early celebration of Kloie's 17th birthday.

‌



The fundraiser said: "What should have been a weekend filled with memories and a celebration of Kloie turning 17 has instead left a family trying to comprehend the loss of a mother and her two daughters all at once.

"There are simply no words for the magnitude of this loss or for what this family is facing in the days, weeks, and months ahead."

It added: "Vanessa, Kloie, and Kylie were so much more than the three lives mentioned in a news story. They were a mom, daughters, sisters, family and friends who were deeply loved and who should have made it home that night."

Article continues below

Kloie was a senior at Centennial High School in Bakersfield and a member of its Golden Hawks softball team.

Paying tribute to the teenager following her death, the team said: "Her presence on and off the field will never be forgotten. Kloie will forever be a Golden Hawk."

News.title: Met Office maps show fresh heat surge in days as 15 areas face 24C or more - full list
News.content:
Met Office maps show fresh heat surge in days as 15 areas face 24C or more - full list

At least 15 counties could see highs of 24C or more as the Met Office warns 'very warm spells are possible' even as autumn edges closer

View 3 Images Warm temperatures are set to return to the Kent coast (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

Brits could be treated to another burst of summer sun after a spell of miserable rain and cooler weather, with temperatures set to rocket back into the mid-20s this week.

‌



At least 15 counties are set for highs of 24C or more by Sunday, September 6, with the south and southeast likely to enjoy the highest readings, according to Met Office charts.

‌



By 4pm that day, the mercury could hit 25C in a string of towns and cities, including London, Reading, Chelmsford, Worcester and Stratford-upon-Avon.

‌



Kent, Surrey and Cambridgeshire are all expected to enjoy highs of 24C, along with Bristol and Gloucester.

The warmth is also set to reach the coast, with Brighton and Dover both set for 22C, while Plymouth could climb to 23C.

View 3 Images Multiple areas are forecast to welcome warm weather this week (Image: Met Office )

‌



In Wales it is likely to be a little cooler, although much of the country could still see a pleasant 20C or 21C. Further north, the mercury is set to reach lower levels but Derby could reach 22C on Sunday, and Liverpool could hit 21C. Manchester, Sheffield and Newcastle are all forecast to reach 20C.

Scotland will be noticeably cooler, with Edinburgh and Glasgow both expected to reach around 17C, while the Highlands will see temperatures hovering between 15C and 17C.

The warm spell comes after 71% of England was officially declared in drought following a summer of exceptionally dry weather and a succession of heatwaves.

‌



The country has since welcomed bouts of much-needed rain and cooler conditions - although the deluges have brought their own problems.

Severe thunderstorms caused significant flooding in Birmingham last week, damaging dozens of properties near the Tame Valley Canal as torrential rain swept across the West Midlands.

View 3 Images A car sits on a flooded street in Birmingham (Image: Anita Maric / SWNS)

‌



Despite autumn edging closer, the Met Office says "very warm spells are possible, especially in the south" as we head into September.

In its outlook for September 5 to September 14, the forecaster said unsettled weather is likely in northern and western areas, but this could soon be followed by brief warm spells in the south.

"An unsettled period is likely, with many places seeing showers or longer spells of rain at times," the Met Office said.

Article continues below

"Rain is expected to be most frequent across northern and western areas, while the south and east are more likely to see longer, drier spells. There is also the potential for some strong and gusty winds, particularly in the northwest.

"Temperatures are likely to be near average, although brief warm or very warm spells are possible, especially in the south."

Counties set for 24C or more on September 6

News.title: 'Stolen' van crashes after going 'wrong way' down A20 to London before being rammed by cops
News.content:
'Stolen' van crashes after going 'wrong way' down A20 to London before being rammed by cops

A suspect, aged 23 from Swanley, was arrested on suspicion of aggravated vehicle taking, criminal damage, dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified and failing to stop for police

View 2 Images A large number of police vehicles rushed to the scene after the crash (Image: UKNIP)

A van crashed after it was allegedly taken without the owner's consent and driven the wrong way down a major road during a police chase before it was rammed by officers.

Police then chased down a 23-year-old suspect who fled on foot following the dramatic police pursuit, before he was caught and arrested.

Images from the scene show the van left with one wheel suspended in the air after police stopped it in Bromley, London. Reports on social media from eyewitnesses claim they saw multiple police cars slam into the vehicle in Mottingham Road before it finally came to a halt.

The van was chased for about 17 miles from Swanley into London, Kent Police said, after they spotted the vehicle, which had previously been reported stolen, at 6.45pm yesterday (Sunday).

View 2 Images The vehicle was left suspended after it was rammed by cops (Image: UKNIP)

The force said it was called to a report that a man had smashed a window and taken a van that did not belong to him from an address in Swanscombe at 2.55pm.

The owner of the property is known to the man, police said. After officers spotted the van, the driver allegedly refused to stop and instead headed for London down the wrong side of the A20, police said.

The police gave chase and were joined by officers from the Metropolitan Police. Officers from the London force detained the driver after making what they called "tactical contact" with the vehicle.

Article continues below

Pictures show at least eight police vehicles filling the road behind the white van at the conclusion of the chase. The suspect, aged 23 from Swanley, was arrested on suspicion of aggravated vehicle taking, criminal damage, dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified and failing to stop for police. He remains in custody as enquiries continue.

One Metropolitan Police officer suffered an injury to his hand during the incident and no other serious injuries were reported.

News.title: Fresh Middlesbrough arrests in organised crime crackdown after 'vehicle rammed'
News.content:
Fresh Middlesbrough arrests in organised crime crackdown after 'vehicle rammed'

Two men aged 19 and 24 have been arrested in Middlesbrough on suspicion of Possession of a firearm with intent to cause fear of violence

View Image More than 200 police been mobilised across Teesside (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

Police have made two arrests after a vehicle was allegedly rammed in Middlesbrough - eight days after a head-on collision which killed five young men and two police officers on the A66.

Cleveland Police said 27 people have now been arrested as part of their investigations since the horrific collision on the A66 on August 22.

In the latest incident, men aged 19 and 24 were arrested on suspicion of possession of a firearm with intent to cause fear of violence. The force said the arrests "come after" a vehicle rammed another on Derwentwater Road at around 11pm on Sunday.

The older man was arrested in Burns Road around half an hour later, while the teenager was arrested at a property in that street by officers conducting checks in the area. Both men remained in custody on Monday.

Cleveland Police also said an 18-year-old has appeared in court charged with dangerous driving after a car was spotted "being driven dangerously" in the town on Saturday afternoon. He appeared before Teesside Magistrates' Court on Monday and was remanded in custody, the force said.

Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said: "We have said previously Cleveland Police will not stop pursuing those involved in serious and organised crime, and I hope these arrests further demonstrate that. Our commitment to tackling criminal gangs whose intent is to harm people in our communities is, and will continue to be, a persistent focus for us.

"These latest developments now take the total number of arrests since we started investigating the incidents in the early hours of Saturday August 22 2026 to 27 and I can assure the public that they will not be the last.

"We are investigating around the clock and we thank the public not only for their support and patience while we conduct numerous inquiries, but also for the information we are receiving. We will always act on this information in our unwavering commitment to dismantle serious and organised crime in our area."

Around 200 police officers from outside Cleveland Police have been drafted in to help the force tackle organised crime following the crash on the A66.

Article continues below

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, were killed when their marked response vehicle was hit by a Volkswagen Passat heading the wrong way down the dual carriageway.

Cole Worthy, 17, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and 23-year-olds Michael Cahill and Jakub Matusiak were in the Passat and were also killed in the crash. Four of the five had criminal records and police have said there may be links to "serious and organised criminal activity".

On Sunday, PC Blades' sons led out Manchester United at Old Trafford for their game against Ipswich Town.

News.title: DARREN LEWIS: 'Notting Hill Carnival's biggest dangers are the liars out to divide us'
News.content:
The liars laying in to the Notting Hill Carnival are going to have to try again next year. The usual suspects were out in force even earlier than normal to claim the annual British-Caribbean jamboree – celebrating its 60th birthday this year – was a war zone waiting to happen.

If you’ve never been, ignore them and put it in your diary for next August. Saturday is generally the good-natured face-off day between the steel bands, Sunday is a designated family and ­children’s day and Monday is the main parade day.

Social media was awash with the tired old fibs, suggesting you were taking your life into your own hands if you went out to West London to get involved. Tell that to the people who’d been there, done that, and have posted the fun footage online to prove it.

Carnival’s biggest danger used to be the racists attacking Black and Brown people in the area. Now it is sections of the commentator class clutching their pearls and trying to divide us. They must be seething over their laptops that most sane, sensible people reject them.

‌



View 3 Images Carnival-goers during the Notting Hill Carnival in London (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

And as usual, to back up that pushback, some actual facts. The data over consecutive years – with the figures adjusted for crowd sizes –clearly shows the carnival’s arrest rate per person is comfortably lower than two other major UK music festivals ­Creamfields and Reading. I’ve had my teenagers at all three this weekend.

It sits only marginally above the UK’s other big festival, Glastonbury. Two million people attended last year’s carnival. There were 528 arrests. Percentage? 0.0264.

And that was a spike from previous years because of an effective, proactive policing strategy which included live facial recognition technology to identify troublemakers and suspects on watchlists. If anything, the tactics to keep people safe at the carnival are actually working.

‌



Reading has a history of campsite chaos on the final night, including ­incidents of tent burning resulting in dozens of people being thrown out – but not necessarily arrested. The disorder has led to the final night bring ­nicknamed “The Purge”, leading to the introduction of live facial recognition cameras at the gates.

Creamfields in Daresbury has a history of large groups of gatecrashers trying to overcome their lack of tickets by breaking through the perimeter fencing.

View 3 Images The facts remain that Notting Hill is among the safest of the UK’s carnivals. (Image: Vuk Valcic/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

Cheshire Police also deals with remarkable levels of planning by drugs gangs and dealers. This year they dug up massive stashes of ketamine and nitrous oxide canisters that had been buried months in advance to bypass security.

‌



Freedom of Information data reveals at least 24 rapes were reported at Leeds Festival between 2018 and 2024 – with eight rapes or penetration offences reported during the 2024 bank holiday weekend alone.

Have there been serious incidents at Notting Hill Carnival? Yes. Four people were stabbed last year. Down from eight, the year before. All of them were serious incidents, let’s not hide away from that. Our thoughts are with all of the victims.

But the critics rejecting Notting Hill’s annual celebration of cultural unity hate it when solid evidence puts even those numbers into perspective.

They hate it when you look at the detail and not just the professional agitators. They hate it when police officers see the negativity for what it is and positively engage with revellers, singing, dancing and being human.

‌



Last year, officers were actually ordered by London’s Met Police NOT to dance with people at the carnival. Seven years ago they were even threatened with a “dancing ban”.

How on earth are the critics going to worry the life out of potential attendees when law enforcement show the fear-mongering up to be a load of old nonsense?

And yet still the facts remain that Notting Hill is among the safest of the UK’s carnivals. You’ll struggle to find a large-scale outdoor festival anywhere that doesn’t have a minority of troublemakers who want to spoil it for everyone else.

But carnival continues, time and again, to capture the spirit of ­camaraderie that we need more than ever across the country.

News.title: Mel Stride and Priti Patel replaced in major Tory reshuffle
News.content:
Badenoch's reshuffle is intended to bring solutions to a number of problems.

First, she wants to retire those members of her top team that have had a relatively low profile, or who have not been delivering sufficient blows to both Labour and Reform UK.

Badenoch paid a warm tribute to Sir Mel but some recent polls suggested that Reform UK were more trusted on the economy than the Conservatives.

And that is something Kemi Badenoch felt needed to change.

Second, while familiar faces like Dame Priti were useful to have in the top team as they brought high-level government experience, they might also remind voters of the party they decisively rejected in 2024.

There has been a changing of the old guard, and Badenoch is now focusing on who can take the Conservatives into the next election - faced as she is by a new Labour leader and cabinet.

Third, she wants to focus on issues where Labour is perceived to be vulnerable.

One such area is defence spending and national security.

So as shadow foreign secretary she appointed Tom Tugendhat - a former security minister and current army reservist who served in Afghanistan and Iraq. He will work as part of a team with the shadow defence secretary.

Some opinion polls rate the economy as the most important issue for voters, above asylum and immigration, and again the Tory leader believes the government is vulnerable here, with sluggish growth.

So she has announced a new Conservative economic unit headed by Griffith, with his extensive business experience.

Coutinho as his deputy is seen as a rising Conservative star who has performed well in her previous role shadowing the former energy secretary Ed Miliband in the Commons, and as a potential future chancellor if the Conservatives were ever to recover electorally.

But the Tory leader has also included the former Conservative chairman and City Minister Richard Fuller in the unit, concentrating on fiscal responsibility and tax.

He will be deployed as an attack dog if - as she believes he will â the chancellor raises taxes in the Budget.

But the role will also underline that the Conservative leader is serious about making her sums add up, in contrast to her characterisation of Reform UK's plans as ill-thought out.

The question now though is whether Badenoch will change her own approach to political leadership.

While some of her top team may be seen as lacklustre, how much opportunity did they get to shine?

She tends to make the big announcements and is ubiquitous on the media.

If the Conservatives are to convince voters they are once again a government in waiting then the public will have to see that there is breadth and depth in the team that is shadowing current ministers.

News.title: Messi retires from international football with 'nothing left to give'
News.content:
In the race between athlete and time, there is only ever one winner.

Messi has pushed that defeat date back for a long, long time now. But I think maybe two things hastened it a little bit.

One is the recent death of his father and the other is - although it was 1-0 on the scoresheet - the World Cup final defeat by Spain. The distance between the two sides was so, so large.

You could see Messi, as he looked around the stadium almost thinking, "I don't think I can go through this again".

What memories he has given us. This little man has been a part of my life for 21 and a half years - but it had to end some time and that day is today.

Could Messi move back to Newell's Old Boys to finish his career? I think there are two problems there.

One is moving his family back to the city of Rosario. It is a little bit provincial, and there are problems with violence there. True, his old mate Angel di Maria has done it with Rosario Central without too many problems. But I think Messi would worry about taking his family back into a goldfish bowl.

The other is that the level of football might not attract him quite so much. It could happen for just a few games, as a kind of romantic end to his career. He has talked about it plenty of times in the past. But I imagine Inter Miami might be the end.

Who knows? He will stop playing when he feels like it. If he doesn't feel like going on until the end of 2028, he could knock it on the head before then.

We will have to see. Inter Miami fans are the lucky ones. They will get the last drops of this little man's genius.

News.title: Hundreds remember Heaton Park synagogue attack victims at memorial event
News.content:
The Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis and Communities Secretary Angela Rayner were among about 800 people who attended a memorial event for the victims and survivors of last year's Heaton Park synagogue attack.

Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed, and three others injured, as they tried to defend their place of worship from attacker Jihad al-Shamie on 2 October 2025.

Relatives of the bereaved and some of the survivors were among the speakers at Monday's service of remembrance at the synagogue in Manchester.

Prior to the event, Rabbi Daniel Walker said the Jewish community feels less safe now than it did immediately after the attack.

He said rising antisemitism, combined with a lack of action to "deal with core problems", had left many members of Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation â and British Jews more widely â feeling increasingly vulnerable.

Two seats remained empty for the service, bearing the names of Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby.

News.title: AI could cause global economic downturn, Bank of England chief warns
News.content:
The governor of the Bank of England has warned G20 finance ministers that artificial intelligence could cause a global economic downturn and pose a significant cyber security risk to financial systems.

Andrew Bailey said any collapse of growth in the AI sector could lead to a "future market correction" that spreads worldwide.

In an open letter to finance ministers in the US on Monday, he said companies around the world should prepare for security breaches "involving simultaneous disruption across multiple firms".

Earlier this month, a group of 100 firms, including Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI, urged countries and groups to beef up their cyber defences before AI grows powerful enough to override them.

Bailey told the G20 finance ministers that a combination of highly priced stock markets, increased borrowing by investors, and the growing concentration of money into a small number of major technology companies could amplify any future market correction.

"The issue is not simply that investors are borrowing more, but that leverage is interacting with high valuations and market concentration, in particular the increasing cross-investment between artificial intelligence (AI) companies and hyper scalers, in a way that could amplify a future market correction," he said.

Bailey has called on those in charge of financial security to develop "appropriate steps to support safe and responsible model release and deployment on a global basis".

Bailey, who was writing in his capacity as chairman of the Financial Stability Board international watchdog (FSB), expressed concern about the "volatility" prompted by the effect of energy supply shocks caused by the US-Iran war.

His warning comes several months after UK Chancellor John Healey announced a Â£100m fund aimed at backing British AI start-ups.

That is part of the government's efforts to grow the country's "sovereign AI" capacity, developing homegrown AI technology to ensure the UK is not dependent on services from abroad.

Ministers want to see companies compete for the funding to help tackle challenges like cutting waiting lists in the NHS and bolstering cybersecurity and defence.

A UK government spokesperson said its' new AI economics institute was working with international partners to build "a stronger shared understanding of how AI is transforming economies around the world."

"The institute is the first government-backed body of its kind focused on AI's economic impact, helping policymakers understand what AI means for growth, productivity, jobs and public services as the technology develops at pace," the spokesperson said.

But there is growing concern that AI companies are increasingly developing models that can easily override the safeguarding systems of banks and financial centres.

News.title: Victoria Beckham's company makes its first profit after 18 years
News.content:
Victoria Beckham's fashion and beauty business has made an operating profit for the first time since she founded it in 2008, the company has said.

Victoria Beckham Holdings Ltd, which is led by the former Spice Girl as creative director, made an operating profit of Â£7.3m in 2025, accounts show, after years of losses.

"We have all worked hard for a long time for this moment of profitability and growth," Lady Beckham told the Financial Times, external.

"We've been very transparent about the problems that we had in the business but have recovered and are now growing at a sensible pace. After 20 years, people don't look at my brand as a celebrity brand any more."

News.title: Notting Hill Carnival revels in 60th anniversary celebrations
News.content:
Notting Hill Carnival has celebrated its 60th anniversary with three days of revelry fuelled by drummers, dancers and colourful costumes.

Europe's biggest street party continued on Monday with the adults' parade, live bands, more than 30 static sound systems and the scent of jerk chicken floating through the air.

The carnival, which celebrates Caribbean culture and history, was first held in west London in 1966.

"We are the greatest when we come together as people," said Jackie, from Jay Dee's Catering, who has been trading at the event for 15 years with her family business.

News.title: Trump pushes Apple to change 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' on its maps
News.content:
Trump signed the executive order on Thursday seeking to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America, following the collapse of trade negotiations between Canada and the US.

The order directs Burgum to "take all appropriate actions" to rename the lake, including updating the Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), the official US government map database.

Google said in a statement on Saturday that its maps will display the Lake America name for US users to comply with the GNIS.

It added that those in Canada will continue to see Lake Ontario displayed. In the rest of the world, users will see the name displayed as: Lake Ontario (Lake America).

Not all map providers are changing the name. MapQuest, an American free web mapping service launched in 1996, said "we're not changing it" in a short Facebook post on Friday.

The platform also unveiled a tool that allows users to change the lake to any name they choose and share their creations.

After its announcement that it will not be changing the name of Lake Ontario, MapQuest rose to the top of the most-downloaded free applications as of Monday morning on the Apple App Store in Canada.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a large sign by the lakeshore on Saturday that read "Lake Ontario Now and Always" in both English and French, Canada's official languages.

"No one's going to call it Lake of America," Ford told American TV host George Stephanopoulos on Sunday. "It's been Lake Ontario for hundreds of years. It's going to continue being Lake Ontario."

The names of four of the Great Lakes - Ontario, Huron, Michigan and Erie - originate from indigenous words.

News.title: Kushner states regret over World Cup sell-off plan
News.content:
Kushner's comments come just days after Uefa asked a court in New York to approve subpoenas for testimony and documents from both the American billionaire and Thrive as it considers lodging a criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland.

European football's governing body Uefa has led the rebellion against the Fifa president, who is facing calls to stand down.

In a statement, Kushner said: "Money in football has historically been concentrated amongst a small group of countries.

"The idea behind FFE was to direct more capital and equity equally amongst all 211 member countries, providing significantly more investment to underdeveloped nations to nurture local talent, support grassroots football, enhance the fan experience, and ultimately grow the global game everywhere.

"It was an idea that every member association would vote on, not an obligation or determination.

"While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to. Thrive has a long track record of being a partner to all constituents. Had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved."

In late July, shortly before scrapping the plan, Fifa said, "Thrive Eternal...is expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE", claiming it would have seen the funding distributed to each national association for the 2027-2030 cycle increase from Â£5.9m to Â£14.7m.

As well as Kushner, Uefa has asked for the disclosure of documents from two Fifa businesses in the US and American financier Greg Maffei, who was a key adviser on the deal.

While Uefa says neither Kushner nor Maffei are anticipated defendants in any legal proceedings, it claims the pair first discussed the FFE concept in July 2025 and that Infantino had "been discussing the underlying concept with Kushner for nearly a year before the terms sheet was ultimately signed."

Its lawyers also argue the World Cup was deliberately undervalued at around Â£15bn, which it says is "a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer". It claims Infantino failed to consult Fifa's hierarchy over the plan.

Kushner has recently agreed a deal to buy basketball's Los Angeles Lakers for a record $12.5bn (Â£9.3bn).

News.title: Early release scheme could see dangerous criminals released, Conservatives warn
News.content:
On Monday Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones told the BBC: "We will do nothing that would risk the public or put the public at danger."

Under the early release scheme some 4,500 prisoners are now expected to start being released in tranches from October to ease overcrowding in jails.

The numbers due to be released has been reduced after the government said rapists, those found guilty of serious child sex offences and grooming offences and now those found guilty of manslaughter would be excluded from the scheme.

Given that fewer prisoners will now be released than initially expected this will have a knock-on effect on prison capacity.

Timothy said releasing prisoners serving indefinite sentences under imprisonment for public protection sentences posed its own risk.

Between 2005 and 2012 IPPs were given to some offenders in England and Wales where they were considered to pose a significant risk of causing serious harm to the public. Once they had served a minimum term they could only be released once the Parole Board was satisfied they no longer posed a risk to the public. Although IPPs are no longer imposed many people already serving sentences are stlll in prison.

Timothy told the BBC: "By definition, the people who are still in prison on those sentences are dangerous, because they've all been considered by independent expert assessors who have concluded that they are not safe to release and they would be a danger to the public."

He accepted not enough prisons had been built under the previous Conservative government.

Indefinite prison sentences have previously been handed out in several high-profile cases, including to Tracey Connelly, the mother of Baby P, who was jailed in 2009 after admitting causing or allowing the death of her one-year-old son Peter.

There were 2,271 people serving IPPs, according to Ministry of Justice (MoJ) data up to June this year.

Of those, 856 have never been released because the Parole Board thought it was not safe to do so. Ending indefinite sentences for those still serving them would require new legislation, meaning it could be years before space is freed up.

Davies-Jones told BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "The government's number one priority is to keep the public safe and in order to do that we need a functioning criminal justice system."

She defended the government's decision to look at indefinite sentences as part of ensuring there were enough prison spaces.

"We need to look at every case on its merits individually, and pass the appropriate legislation and we will do that responsibly and we will take our time to get it right," she added.

She said those released would still be monitored.

News.title: Man dies near Notting Hill Carnival after entering canal
News.content:
A man has died near Notting Hill Carnival in London on Monday afternoon, the Metropolitan Police have confirmed.

Police officers had attempted to stop the man, believed to be in his 20s, as he approached the event. He fled on foot with officers in pursuit, and entered the water in the vicinity of Meanwhile Gardens a short time later, the force said.

The man was taken to hospital by ambulance and was pronounced dead a short time later.

Cdr Claire Smart said: "This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are with the loved ones of the man who has lost his life."

The Met Police said officers had attempted to stop the man at about 15:19 BST near Harrow Road.

The man entered the water in the vicinity of Meanwhile Gardens, off Kensal Road.

Officers and members of the public went in after him and pulled him from the water, police said, and officers immediately started CPR.

Paramedics were called and continued treatment at the canal side before taking the man to a central London hospital. He was pronounced dead at 16:43 BST.

The Met Police said on Monday night that urgent enquiries were ongoing to locate and inform his next of kin.

Smart, gold commander for the Notting Hill Festival, said: "Any death following contact with the police is passed to the Independent Office for Police Conduct so the circumstances can be fully investigated.

"I would encourage everyone to avoid speculation while this work takes place."

She added: "I acknowledge the efforts of the officers and members of the public who entered the canal to rescue this man. I know they will be devastated that his life couldn't ultimately be saved."

The Met Police said the two days of the festival passed "largely without incident".

There were two assaults with knives - one stabbing and one slashing. Neither of which resulted in life threatening injuries.

On Monday evening, police said there had been 315 arrests that day, bringing the total number of arrests to 560.

Police said it is likely this number may rise slightly while latter arrests are processed.

News.title: Nursery fined after baby boy burned by bleach
News.content:
Defence advocate Barry Smith KC said the first priority of a nursery was the safety and wellbeing of the children there.

He added: "It is of the utmost regret from all involved - from the director and all staff - that this accident occurred and injury was caused to a young child."

In a statement released via law firm Digby Brown, the family said: "We've had to wait five years for Little Dreams Nursery to admit what happened to our son was their fault but we don't feel the severity of his injuries have been acknowledged.

"We trusted them to take care of him and for such an injury to happen to a 10-month-old baby is indefensible.

"In the months and years that followed, we had to watch our boy deal with the consequences of something that was never his fault. No parent should have to experience that, but we are thankful what happened hasn't had a more serious or longer-lasting impact."

The statement concluded: "Today we close the most horrific chapter of our lives and we want to thank everyone who has supported us during this time and now request our privacy as we move forward."

Little Dreams said the safety, wellbeing and care of every child entrusted to them was of the "highest priority".

"We deeply regret that this incident was able to occur and are profoundly sorry for the distress and impact it has had on the child and their family," the nursery said.

News.title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems
News.content:
Burnt out teachers urgently need better working hours and more support to stop them leaving the profession, the Liberal Democrats say, as the new term approaches.

Nearly half of the teachers surveyed by the party in England said they were planning to quit the classroom in the next five years, with many saying they felt overworked and stressed.

The Lib Dems are urging new Education Secretary Lucy Powell to fully fund teachers' pay, rather than raiding school budgets to cover increases, and to bring in limits on overtime.

The Department for Education said last year saw the lowest rate of teachers leaving the profession since 2010 but acknowledged there was "more to do".

The survey asked more than 900 teachers, headteachers and Special Educational Needs Coordinators (SENCOs) across England how long they planned to stay in teaching.

Almost half of those in post said they were considering leaving teaching in the next five years, while one in ten were planning to spend less than a year in the job.

More than three quarters of those surveyed, which included former teachers, said they had felt "frequently or constantly burnt out" while at work.

Respondents cited high workloads on marking, lesson preparation and other tasks, which they said gave them less time in the classroom.

The Liberal Democrats' schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said this pointed to a government that is "not listening" to the profession.

"We rely on teachers to educate our children, the least we can do is make sure they want to come back after the summer," she said.

Teacher retention is a challenge successive governments have had to grapple with.

The National Education Union (NEU) reported that 4 in 10 teachers were planning to quit over "huge workloads and excessive accountability" in 2019.

This latest survey was also conducted with the help of the NEU, as well as the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL).

"After over a decade of austerity and chronic underfunding in our schools the system is on its knees" said the NEU's general secretary Daniel Kebede.

"The new academic year is the perfect time for Andy Burnham to signal a fresh start for our schools" he added.

"That means fully funding the pay award and properly funding all our schools and colleges to stem the recruitment and retention crisis and give children the education they deserve."

"As Lucy Powell enters her first term as education secretary the Liberal Democrats are calling for her first act to be to introduce an emergency package of 'back to school' measures to face this crisis head on," Voaden said.

The Lib Dem proposals include the government fully funding teacher's pay, which will increase in England by 3.5% from September, with an additional 3% the year after.

Currently, half of the pay increase will come from existing school budgets.

The party is also calling for proper enforcement of teacher's legally mandated working hours, the introduction of reasonable limits on overtime, and for all schools to be required to introduce flexible working policies.

The party did not identify where funding might come from to pay for the policies.

An education department spokesperson said: "We know teachers do an incredible job and we're determined to make sure that dedication is matched with the right support.

"Last year saw one of the lowest rates of teachers leaving the profession since 2010, and a record number of teachers returning to the classroom, but we know there's more to do.

"We're taking action by announcing pay awards of almost 17% over two years, funding schools to improve maternity pay and offering targeted support to normalise flexible working and manageable workloads so that more teachers stay in our classrooms and thrive."

News.title: Business groups urge Swinney to scrap 'ineffective' food price cap plan
News.content:
The SRC said the policy also risked forcing small shops which are not covered by the proposed legislation to be uncompetitive.

"Scottish consumers benefit from the most affordable food prices in western Europe," MacDonald-Russell added.

"We know food price inflation is a problem, but the best model to deal with it is the one we have right now and price caps are going to make that worse.

"It is giving a false promise that it is going to be able to help with something.

"In reality, there is as good a chance it is going to make the overall cost of a shopping basket higher, because the cost of the scheme as well as the cap have to be absorbed by businesses."

It is thought the proposals would require changes to the UK Internal Markets Act of 2020, which was brought in after Brexit to prevent trade barriers and regulatory divergence between England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland as powers returned from the EU.

The Scottish government said helping people with the cost of living was a "top priority".

A spokesperson added: "Ministers have welcomed engagement with stakeholders, including retailers, food producers and farmers on proposals for food price controls.

"A consultation will launch shortly for further views."

News.title: Twenty-seven people rescued from rollercoaster
News.content:
Firefighters have rescued 27 people who were stuck on a rollercoaster for up to three hours.

Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service said it was called to the Wipeout ride at Pleasurewood Hills in Lowestoft at 13:36 BST.

An eyewitness described what appeared to be a power cut affecting multiple rides at the attraction, and video footage showed the moment the carriages came to a stop about 15m (49ft) in the air.

Pleasurewood Hills said it was "incredibly grateful for the way [the riders] handled" the situation and to their families for their "understanding and patience".

"We appreciate that being stuck on a ride is not something anyone expects when visiting us."

News.title: Grandfather dies months after confronting burglars
News.content:
An 85-year-old grandfather has died more than four months after confronting burglars who broke into his home.

Gordon Nicholass was the victim of a burglary at about 03:00 BST on 29 April at his home in the village of Helmshore, Lancashire.

Lancashire Police said he was assaulted and suffered injuries to his head and cuts to his face when he confronted the burglars. He was treated in hospital and sent home, but was later taken back to hospital and died on 12 August.

Post-mortem tests have been carried out, but further inquiries are being made to establish if the assault was a cause or contributory factor, police said. His family added: "Gordon was a wonderful husband, dad and granddad."

They added in a tribute: "He was a lifelong motorcycle enthusiast and well known for his engineering skills.

"He was always there to do anything for anyone - family, friends even strangers, you name it!"

They described him as "mister fix it" who was a "jack of all trades".

His family added: "We will all miss him dearly."

News.title: UK raises case of British activist detained by settlers in West Bank with Israel
News.content:
The UK Foreign Office says it has raised the detention of a British national in the occupied West Bank with Israeli authorities.

Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old student activist, was arrested in Umm Al-Kheir on Saturday after he was forcibly detained by Israeli settlers who had advanced on the Palestinian village.

There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

All settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts are also illegal under Israeli law, although they are often supported by state services and funding.

The confrontation on Saturday took place in a town near Hebron that has been recently surrounded by settlers.

According to other activists who witnessed what happened, Palestinian children were playing football when children from settler families started intervening. They then ran to a house and started to dismantle a fence.

Footage posted online by both settlers and activists and seen by the BBC appears to show Joughin standing by the fence and trying to protect it using his body as a child pushes against him.

Settlers removed Joughin forcefully and took the London-based student to an outpost.

Israeli police said a foreign national "who disrupted public order" was detained by security personnel of a settler community who suspected him of an indecent act against a minor and other offences.

In a statement on Sunday, police said the suspect was transferred to their custody for questioning before documents relating to the case were sent to the Population and Immigration Authority for review.

"This was carried out as part of ongoing cooperation and efforts to prevent provocative activity involving confrontations and disturbances," police said.

A lawyer for Joughin said: "We absolutely deny all the allegations."

Inbar Shaked Vardi told the BBC that the student was initially accused of assault.

But Shaked Vardi said police later added to the paperwork an allegation of an indecent act.

Joughin is being deported back to the UK on a flight scheduled for Monday afternoon, according to his lawyer.

"So far they have not decided officially on closing the case," Shaked Vardi said.

Joughin is the only one being investigated and as he is being deported, "it's safe to assume they won't continue to pursue charges against him", she said.

"Police use deportation in order to get what they want â which is to get activists outside of the West Bank while continuing to allow settlers to do what they do", she added.

Activists who were with Joughin at the time deny there was any inappropriate behaviour.

"In every single instance, it was the settler kids who approached Finn," fellow activist Matthew, who declined to give his surname, told the BBC.

Britain’s Harriet Dart battled through to round two at the US Open after coming from a set down to oust home hope Peyton Stearns.

The 30 year-old, who had to come from behind to beat compatriot Heather Watson in the final round of qualifying, won a gruelling tussle 3-6 6-3 6-2 in two hours and 24 minutes.

Dart needed treatment on a foot problem after winning the second set and squandered three match points in a nervy ending.

But she got over the line with a fourth, clenching her fists in delight when Stearns netted a forehand before celebrating with former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli, who is part of her coaching team.

Frenchwoman Bartoli won the SW19 title in 2013 and has been working with Dart on an ad-hoc basis since January.

“She does a lot of my training weeks as we live near each other,” said Dart,

“She’s done primarily the slams but on the grass she did three weeks, and before here in Florida. She has a busy schedule and so do I so we have to co-ordinate but I feel like I’m benefitting from all the work we do together.

“She a great coach and an even better person – she’s very funny – but I’m just trying to soak up as much as I can from such a champion.”

British number one Katie Boulter, who beat American wild card Carol Young Suh Lee on Sunday, found out her next opponent will be seventh seed Karolina Muchova after the Wimbledon runner-up thrashed Sinja Kraus 6-3 6-0.

In the men’s draw, Jacob Fearnley picked the worst possible moment to play probably the worst shot of his entire career.

The British number four, only in the first round proper as a lucky loser, was on match point and had the simplest of overhead put-aways to secure a five-set victory over Spain’s Martin Landaluce.

open image in gallery Jacob Fearnley is also through ( Getty )

But Fearnley must have taken his eye off the ball as he missed it completely, playing an air shot any club player would have been embarrassed by, before scrambling back to keep it in play.

Landaluce went on to win the point, and to rub salt in the wounds even the ball kid was smirking as Fearnley trudged back to the service line.

Having been leading 5-1 in the final set, shell shocked Fearnley was reeled back to 5-3, but he held his nerve to eventually serve out for a 4-6 6-2 4-6 7-5 6-3 victory, at four hours 10 minutes the longest match of his career.

The Federal Trade Commission and a coalition of 22 states are suing Amazon for “secretly and systematically” overcharging advertisers on its platform, ultimately bringing in more than $20 billion over seven years.

The complaint, filed in a Washington federal court Monday, accuses Amazon of manipulating the minimum price that advertisers had to pay to place ads on the e-commerce giant’s website.

Amazon allegedly did not properly disclose the pricing of the “sponsored” ad space, which users typically see at the top of a page when searching for products.

“Amazon has millions of advertising customers who were misled into paying significantly higher prices. These higher costs were largely passed on to American consumers,” FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson said in a press release.

Monday’s lawsuit is the third time the FTC has brought major legal action against Amazon.

open image in gallery The Federal Trade Commission is accusing Amazon of running deceptive practices when it comes to selling ‘sponsored’ ad space on the online retailer’s website ( Reuters )

Last year, the FTC sued Amazon for duping customers into enrolling in Prime and then making it difficult to cancel. In 2023, the FTC sued Amazon for operating a monopoly.

This time, the lawsuit focuses on Amazon’s auction prices for three different advertising spaces: Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display.

According to the lawsuit, Amazon allegedly told advertisers it ran a “second price” auction, in which potential advertisers could bid for ad space, and the winner would pay only “one cent” more than the next highest bidder.

The model attracts more bidders while allowing advertisers to pay less.

But in practice, Amazon allegedly replaced the price determined by the runner-up bidder with a higher price, known as a “soft reserve,” which prosecutors say was “designed to maximize Amazon’s profits and decrease the cost efficiency of its advertisers’ campaigns.”

open image in gallery Amazon accused the FTC of filing a ‘misguided’ lawsuit against it and said the complaint ‘fundamentally misunderstands how advertisers operate’ ( Reuters )

In a blog post Monday, Amazon disputed the FTC’s allegations, calling the lawsuit “misguided” and saying the agency “fundamentally misunderstands how advertisers operate.”

“The FTC wants the public to believe this case is about higher prices for consumers. It is not,” Amazon said in its statement.

“Advertisers adjust bids based on real-world performance, not descriptions of auction mechanics. Even accepting the FTC’s flawed premise that advertisers do not adjust bids, we estimate they saved over $8 billion from 2021 to 2025 as a result of Amazon prioritizing ad relevancy over selecting ads on bid price alone,” Amazon said.

Amazon has the third-largest digital advertising business, generating $19 billion in ad revenue in the second quarter of the year alone.

The company boasted that shoppers who clicked a “Sponsored” prompt convert sales 48 percent more often and spend 21 percent more on average than those who don’t, in its Q2 filing.

The FTC has cracked down on online advertising giants in more recent years. Last year, the FTC opened an investigation and filed a complaint against Google for its search advertising practices.

News.title: Teen girl who recorded livestream of San Diego mosque shooting charged with murder, DA says
News.content:

A 17-year-old girl who recorded a livestream of a shooting that killed three people at a San Diego mosque and disseminated the attackers’ hate-filled writings has been charged with murder by aiding and abetting, according to a North Carolina district attorney.

The girl, whose name was not immediately released, was arrested last week, Forsyth County District Attorney Jim O’Neill said at a news conference in Winston-Salem. A grand jury indicted her on three counts of murder and one count of conspiracy on Monday, just before she was due to begin the school year.

In North Carolina, aiding-and-abetting charges carry the same punishment as if the girl had committed the attack herself, according to O'Neill. She agreed before the attack that she would record the livestream, distribute it and release a document written by the shooters, according to an indictment seen by The Associated Press.

Candles with victim's names written on them outside the Islamic Center of San Diego, in the aftermath of a shooting ( AP Photo/Ty ONeil, File )

She carried out those tasks, and bought a patch featuring a white-supremacist symbol and sent it to one of the gunmen to wear during the shooting, the court papers allege.

“The individual here, locally, was the person who was recording the livestream," O'Neill said. “She disseminated that information and she published their manifesto.”

San Diego mosque shooting

Cain Clark, 17, and Caleb Vazquez, 18, both died after attacking the Islamic Center on May 18. They killed three people, Amin Abdullah, Mansour Kaziha and Nadir Awad, who lost their lives trying to deter the shooters.

Kaziha and Awad were trying to lure the two gunmen away from the mosque but were “unfortunately unable to flee,” San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl said at a press conference after the shooting. “Both suspects were able to successfully corner them and kill both of them.”

Abdullah, a father of eight who was working as a security guard, was able to keep the two teenage gunmen from entering the mosque, Wahl said.

“His actions, without a doubt, delayed, distracted and ultimately deterred these two individuals from gaining access to the greater areas of the mosque, where as many as 140 kids were within 15 feet of these suspects,” Wahl added.

The mosque’s director, Taha Hassane, echoed the police chief’s sentiment, saying, “If it was not for him ... The carnage would be much worse. He’s the one who stopped them, who slowed them down. ... He sacrificed his life.”

The attackers cited a range of far-right ideological inspirations in their rambling writings and included hateful rhetoric toward Jewish people, Muslims and Islam, the LGBTQ+ community, Black people, women, and the political left and right.

The shooters said they were trying to accelerate the collapse of society and Vazquez wrote of having “some mental health issues” and being rejected by women.

In a written statement, the Vazquez family said Caleb Vazquez was on the autism spectrum and had started to resent parts of his identity. They said they believed that, along with exposure to hateful rhetoric online, contributed to his radicalization.

News.content:

Government action against small boat Channel crossings is starting to "bear fruit," according to the Home Secretary, following a drop in summer arrivals to their lowest point since 2019.

Between June and August, 102 small vessels were detected making the journey across the English Channel. This marks the lowest summer total since 2019, when 57 boats were recorded.

Although calmer weather during the summer months typically leads to an increase in crossings, fewer vessels have attempted the trip this year. Recent reports suggest, however, that smuggling gangs are now packing larger numbers of migrants onto fewer, bigger craft.

Official figures show 2,313 individuals arrived during August, excluding unpublished numbers from Bank Holiday Monday. Over the three summer months, 7,371 people completed the crossing, representing the lowest overall summer total since 2020, when 3,307 arrived.

The Home Office highlighted the impact of the UK-France enforcement deal, which has led to increased French police activity across beaches in northern France ( PA )

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: "This Government is committed to restoring order at our border.

"This work is beginning to bear fruit, with June, July and August recording the lowest number of small boat crossings in seven years.

"But we know there is more to do.

"We will be relentless in targeting the criminal gangs behind these crossings, and we will continue to remove the incentives that draw people here on unsafe and illegal routes."

The Home Office highlighted the impact of the UK-France enforcement deal, which has led to increased French police activity across beaches in northern France.

Collaborative action has stopped more than 48,000 crossing attempts since the 2024 election, the department said, while the National Crime Agency and international partners have seized over 1,100 boats and engines to choke supply lines.

The Home Secretary aims to enforce stricter measures via the Immigration and Asylum Bill. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is due to meet French President Emmanuel Macron at Downing Street to discuss joint efforts to stop the crossings.

Franklin Ochoa says that since losing his eyesight 16 years ago, he has started to take on new adventures that he hadn’t thought of when he could see, and it’s all thanks to a bicycle club.

Every Sunday, a group known as the Ciegocleta meets in Ecuador’s capital city of Quito to ride tandem bikes that are steered by volunteers who can see, but pedaled by blind riders.

Ochoa, 44, is one of the group’s most active members and he’s taken his passion for riding well beyond the streets of Quito. Recently, he completed a 1,000 km (650 mile) tandem bike ride that spanned much of Ecuador.

“When I arrive on a bike in a new city I feel like shedding tears of happiness,” Ochoa said. “I love speed and I always tell my guide to let go of the brakes.”

Ciegocleta, whose name comes from the Spanish words for blind and bicycle, was founded 19 years ago by Miguel Ramos, a resident of Quito who built his own tandem bikes. He used them during the ciclopaseo, a weekly event in which the city bars cars from many avenues and turns them over to bike riders and joggers.

Ramos built the tandem bikes so he could ride the ciclopaseo with his children. But one day, one of Ramos’ children couldn’t go, so he decided to invite a blind neighbor to ride with him.

That became the first of many more outings, in which volunteers using tandem bikes, or even bikes with three or four seats, lead people who are visually impaired.

“This is true inclusion,” Ramos said. “We have blind people who are now enjoying cycling without any limits.”

Before heading out to the streets on Sundays on the bikes provided by Ciegocleta, blind people receive some security tips, while volunteers ride on the back of a bike with their eyes covered, to get a sense of what their visually impaired counterparts will experience.

The Ciegocleta group has 150 members, though only about 30 show up to ride on a given Sunday.

Ximena Lozano, a 54-year-old psychologist who was born without sight, says she has been part of the bicycle club for the past 14 years.

Lozano says that when she was younger she spent too much time at home reading, writing or surfing the web. The bicycle club gives her a reason to be outdoors, she said, and “experience freedom.”

According to Ecuador’s government, around 56,000 people in the country are visually impaired, and while blind people have been able to find work with increasing success, their inclusion in sports is still a work in progress.

José Paéz, one of the volunteers at Ciegocleta, said he joined the club after his father-in-law quickly lost his sight due to disease, and brought him to the free rides to help him overcome depression.

“At first it felt scary to lead a blind person on a bike,” Paéz said. “Keeping a (tandem) bike balanced and sustaining the rhythm is not as easy as when you use a regular bike.”

Franklin Ochoa says that his next challenge will be to undertake a ride from Ecuador to Mexico. Through the club he has found a partner willing to join him on the adventure, which can take several months.

News.title: Aston Villa vs Arsenal LIVE: Premier League champions hang on but Rice limps off in injury concern before Chelsea showdown
News.content:
Bukayo Saka’s second-half goal earned Premier League champions Arsenal a narrow victory at Aston Villa, who fell to a second consecutive defeat to start the season despite an improved performance from Unai Emery’s new-look side.

Saka converted Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross as the Gunners clicked into life in attack after the break, with substitute Eberechi Eze involved in the goal after Mikel Arteta brought off Christos Tzolis at half time.

The hosts could not break Arsenal’s defence down, as Ezri Konsa made his debut for the champions following his move from Villa earlier this month, but Villa’s performance was much improved from the disastrous 4-0 defeat at Brighton last week.

Declan Rice appeared to limp off late on in the only other note of concern for Arsenal, who host London rivals Chelsea next week in an early meeting of two sides on maximum points on the third weekend of the season.

Follow all the action from Aston Villa vs Arsenal with our live blog below:

News.title: Despite ugly ending to his Argentina career, Messi redefined beautiful game
News.content:
To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely-scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

That alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pele’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route. It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa’s John McGinn escapes without card despite kicking Arsenal star Riccardo Calafiori in face
Sports.content:
JOHN MCGINN escaped a caution during Aston Villa’s clash with Arsenal after kicking Riccardo Calafiori in the face.

Villa and the Gunners were playing at a new-look Villa Park on Monday when McGinn and Calafiori clashed in the first half.



The Scottish midfielder was in the Arsenal penalty box attempting to win the ball.

However, Italian Calafiori was on hand to defend the ball and clear it away.



The 24-year-old bravely moved his head down towards the ball as McGinn’s boot flew up in turn to try and win it back.

But rather than making clean contact with the ball, McGinn’s boot only caught Calafiori in the face.

Referee Jarred Gillett awarded a foul in Arsenal’s favour as Calafiori rolled around on the floor.

However, he did not reach into his pocket to book the 31-year-old, with both stars okay.

Fans on social media weren’t too happy with that decision one way or another.

One said: “Dangerous challenge by John McGinn from Aston Villa. Riccardo Calafiori on the receiving end of that.
