A second said: “Calafiori was furious lol McGinn nearly messed up the money maker.”

A third added: “Glad Calafiori ducked out of that McGinn high boot.”

Villa captain McGinn did later pick up a yellow after a crunching foul on Mikel Merino.

By then Arsenal had taken the lead after Bukayo Saka ghosted in behind Ian Maatsen to tap home a cross from Calafiori.

Sports.title: Man City approach Chelsea over British-record Enzo Fernandez transfer as they eye £200MILLION deadline day double deal
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY are gearing up for a £200million double deadline day swoop.

City are confident of beating Tottenham to the signing of £60m Everton star Iliman Ndiaye — after Liverpool rejected their £80m bid for Cody Gakpo offer.



And Etihad chiefs are finally engaged in club-to-club talks with Chelsea over midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

It is understood City and the Blues remain quite a distance apart on the valuation of the Argentina star.



Chelsea made Fernandez available for £120m, with a strict instalment schedule, until August 14.

And they will now hold out for a bigger fee — likely up to a British record £140m.



Negotiations are likely to go down to the wire, with the transfer window closing at 11pm on Tuesday.

Some sources believe it is possible no deal will be struck in time.

But the Blues have lined up Monaco’s Lamine Camara and Roma’s Manu Kone as potential replacements for Fernandez if talks progress quickly enough for them to sell and buy.

City moved swiftly to hijack Tottenham’s pursuit of Ndiaye after ending their interest in Gakpo.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Etihad bosses offered Liverpool a £75m fee up front, plus £5m in add-ons for the Holland international.

But when Anfield chiefs turned it down, City renewed their interest in Senegal international Ndiaye.

The news was a big blow to Spurs, who had been expecting the former Sheffield United player to arrive for a medical.

Tottenham had also been pursuing Gakpo to fill their left-wing slot and be the final jigsaw piece in a £400m summer spending spree.

Now they are looking at the cut-price option of signing Mykhailo Mudryk on loan from Chelsea.



Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi worked with Mudryk at Shakhtar Donetsk and expressed support for him during his ban for failing a drugs test.

After Tottenham and Chelsea met in a pre-season friendly in Sydney, De Zerbi described the Ukraine international as “my son”.

Sports.title: England Lionesses hero has face painted over as Aston Villa remove trace of Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez
Sports.content:
THERE’S no room for sentiment at Aston Villa as a mural depicting Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez has been hastily painted over.

The mural near The Holte End of Villa Park has now officially been removed.



The mural was originally painted onto a wall near the iconic stand in 2024, with Ollie Watkins, Emi Martinez and women’s player Rachel Daly.

Watkins has departed for Saudi Arabia and Martinez has moved on to Chelsea.



But Daly, 34, is still very much playing for Aston Villa’s women’s side.

It appears as though she is collateral damage as Watkins and Martinez had to go.

But who knows, maybe she’ll be painted on the next one?

Daly, MBE, has been with Villa since 2022 and has scored 63 times during her time in the Midlands.

She has a seriously decorated career that features representing Great Britain at the Olympics, collecting a runners-up medal for England at the 2023 Women’s World Cup and, of course, winning the 2022 Women’s Euros.

Watkins had also been a great servant to Aston Villa, scoring 108 goals in six seasons.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, given he turns 31 in December, Villa cashed in to the tune of £51 million.

Martinez had looked like he was going to depart Villa Park last summer, but no deal ended up materialising.

This time Chelsea stepped in and bagged the 2022 World Cup winner for a paltry £7.5 million.

Sports.title: Tottenham reject mystery transfer approach for Archie Gray with England kid, 20, keen to play in natural position
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM have turned down an approach for Archie Gray from a mystery club – insisting he is not for sale.

SunSport revealed at the weekend that Brentford are interested in the midfielder, 20, two years on from when Spurs hijacked their move to sign him from Leeds.



The Bees are not thought to be the identity of the club who made the approach, though.

Gray wants to play in his natural central midfield position but has been filling in at right-back so far this season.



Boss Roberto De Zerbi does not want to let the England Under-21 star leave, though.

Tottenham are set for an eventful end to a busy summer transfer window.



Spurs have made a loan enquiry for Mykhailo Mudryk.

De Zerbi’s men are trying to sign one more forward before Tuesday’s deadline and have missed out on Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City.

That has led to them asking Chelsea about Ukrainian Mudryk, who is free to play again after his drugs suspension.

The 25-year-old has a good relationship with De Zerbi, having worked under the Italian at Shakhtar Donetsk.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

De Zerbi has previously described ‘Misha’ Mudryk as “like a son” and “a top player”.

Chelsea beat Arsenal to the £88million signing of Mudryk from Shakhtar in 2023.

But between December 2024 and July this year, Mudryk was banned by the FA for violating anti-doping rules.

He was handed an initial four-year suspension but all charges were dropped and he was allowed to play again in all competitions.

Leeds have shown interest in borrowing him from Chelsea, where his minutes will be restricted under Xabi Alonso. Sunderland have been mooted as a possible option too.



But now Spurs have entered the fray as we head into the final day of the transfer window.

Spurs are in negotiations for Tosin Adarabioyo on loan from Chelsea too as a possible replacement for Kevin Danso, who wants to leave and is in talks to join Sunderland.

Sports.title: Referee blows for half-time early… before playing final 30 seconds of first half and immediately beginning second
Sports.content:
THERE were bizarre scenes in National League football on Monday when a referee blew the final whistle for a game early, and then played those remaining seconds AFTER the half-time break.

Maidenhead United were facing AFC Totton in the National League South on Bank Holiday Monday and played out a 1-1 draw in front of just over 1,000 fans at York Road Stadium.

However, fans in attendance were left scratching their heads at the start of the second half as the officials corrected a time-keeping error.



The two teams emerged following the half-time break, but after 30 seconds, changed ends.



This was because the referee had blown the whistle to end the first-half 30 seconds early.

The teams were then told they would re-enter the pitch, play the remaining 30 seconds of the first half and then swap sides to start the second.

A Maidenhead United statement communicated the situation to fans: “The first half was blown early…



“Once we re-enter the pitch we will play 30 seconds of the first half, resuming with a Maidenhead free-kick.

“We will then swap sides and start the second half…”

Maidenhead goalkeeper Jordi van Stappershoef got proceedings underway with a free-kick when the teams emerged to resume the first half.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The ref then blew his whistle to end the first half and start the second.



The Maidenhead Advertiser reported fans chanted: “You don’t know what you’re doing!”

One fan seeing the stunning events on social media said: “The most bizarre thing I’ve ever seen at a football match, what the actual f*** is the ref on.”

A second said: “Farcical.”

A third added: “Is this for real? Astonishing.”

Another said: “Things you love to see… oh, no, wait, that’s ‘things you should never ever have to see’.”



A fourth said: “Wow.”

Including the Totton draw, Maidenhead have drawn three of their opening five league games, while losing one and winning one.

Meanwhile, Totton have won two, drawn one and lost two.

Sports.title: ‘Genuinely ridiculous’ – Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, ‘moving like a young Neymar’ with outrageous turn and goal
Sports.content:
JJ GABRIEL scored a brilliant goal as he again impressed for Manchester United’s Under-21s.

The forward, 15, made his maiden first team outing in pre season and is playing SIX years above his age group in Premier League 2.



Gabriel was brilliant as he grabbed a goal and two assists against Ipswich Under-21s last week.

And he scored again in the Young Devils’ 4-1 triumph over Leicester earlier today.



The wonderkid performed an outrageous spin in the box before shimmying and firing a left-footed shot beyond the goalkeeper.

Gabriel’s effort put his side 4-1 up on 86 minutes, with Shea Lacey having scored twice and Amir Ibragimov netting the other.



His goal swiftly got plenty of attention among United fans on X.

One wrote: “He’s moving like a young Neymar wtf”.

And a second gushed: “He’s actually a superstar bloody hell”.

A third swooned: “Genuinely ridiculous how good this lad is”.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Another added: “This kid is a magician!”

Should Gabriel feature for the first team in the coming weeks, he will become United’s youngest ever player.

The record is currently held by the late David Gaskell, who was just 16 years and 19 days old when he kept a clean sheet in the 1956 Charity Shield.

First team boss Michael Carrick was in attendance at the Under-21s’ clash with Ipswich last week.

Carrick said of Gabriel: “I really enjoyed the game. You could see the quality.



“JJ is one of the boys. He’s obviously got a really big talent. He’s trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time.

“He’s physically adapting to each step that he makes, and we’re just continuing his development.”

Sports.title: Chelsea’s last ‘bomb squad’ member leaves Stamford Bridge after costing Blues £2.5million per game
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have at last waved goodbye to the last-standing member of their infamous ‘bomb squad’.

In the last window, Raheem Sterling, Axel Disasi and David Datro Fofana made up the last three players who were training entirely away from the first team, with Sterling then having his contract terminated.



Axel Disasi has moved to Crystal Palace on loan, after spending last season on loan at West Ham and now Chelsea have finally found a permanent suitor for Fofana.

He has completed a switch to Swiss Super League side Servette, who Chelsea fans formed a friendship with, funnily enough, after playing each other on their way to winning the Conference League.



The Blues released a statement which read: “David Fofana has completed a permanent transfer to Swiss Super League side Servette.

“The 23-year-old signed for the Blues from Molde in January 2023, scoring 17 goals and providing three assists during his time at Chelsea and on loan.



“We thank David for his efforts during his time at Chelsea and wish him well as he begins a new chapter in his career.”

Fofana scored 22 goals in 39 games for Molde to convince Chelsea to spend £10million on him back in 2022.

But the Blues won’t be making a profit on him like the Norwegians did. Molde got him on a free transfer from Abidjan City.

Fofana then had FIVE different loan spells during his time at Stamford Bridge as he struggled to convince the powers that be to give him a chance.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A meagre 16 goals in 130 outings over those loan spells did precious little for his stock and his days at Chelsea were long numbered.

Four of those goals did come for Burnley in the Premier League where he played 16 games.

Xabi Alonso continues to trim his squad as the transfer window approaches its climax, and Enzo Fernandez could be the next to leave.

The Argentine was left out of the club’s victory over Brighton and Manchester City are prioritising adding him to their squad.

City finally made contact with the Blue on Monday evening but will likely have to pay over £120m to get their man.

Sports.title: First look at new-look Villa Park with stadium capacity drastically reduced for 2026/27 season in £100m expansion
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA are set to play at a reduced-capacity Villa Park for the first time this evening.

Only around 37,000 fans will take to the stands for the clash with Arsenal – down from the previous 43,000 capacity.



That’s because Villa have made the decision to close their North Stand for the entire 2026-27 season as it undergoes dramatic renovations.

The project will see Villa Park’s capacity eventually rise to 50,000.



The £100million redevelopment will also see new glossy concourses added, as well as fresh changing rooms and first-team facilities for players.

Ahead of the Arsenal match, the North Stand structure looked very different to last season.

It had been completely stripped of its roof, as well as all of the seats in its bottom tier.

The stand is effectively now a building site and has been gated off from fans.



Some of the structure has been pretty much reduced to rubble as Villa continue their ongoing project.

Diggers and heavy machinery can be seen surrounding the North Stand.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Villa hope to have the project completed by the 2027-28 campaign.

And the historic ground will have been properly revamped by the time it hosts matches at Euro 2028.



Villa Park is scheduled to host three group stage matches during the tournament, in addition to a round of 16 clash.

A major change has also been made outside the Holte End.

The graphic featuring Emi Martinez, Ollie Watkins and Rachel Daly has been painted over.

This comes following the departures of Martinez and Watkins to Chelsea and Al-Hilal, respectively.

Sports.title: Arsenal launch last-minute £50m transfer push as Mikel Arteta races against deadline
Sports.content:
Arsenal launch last-minute £50m transfer push as Mikel Arteta races against deadline

Arsenal have Belgium winger Malick Fofana on their shortlist with the player having been offered to the Gunners by Lyon

View 2 Images Malick Fofana could join Arsenal before the transfer deadline (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are pushing for a late signing, with Lyon winger Malick Fofana on their shortlist. The 21-year-old was put forward to the club ahead of Tuesday's transfer deadline.

‌



The Gunners are intent on adding another attacker to provide cover for Christos Tzolis, aiming to avoid Eberechi Eze becoming the obvious fallback option should they miss out on Fofana. Arsenal have already finalised exits for Gabriel Martinelli - set to join Al Hilal in a deal worth around £60million, Gabriel Jesus, who will move to Barcelona for £8.6m plus £4.3m in add‑ons, and Fabio Vieira, who is heading to Hamburger SV in a £7.7m transfer.

‌



Leandro Trossard has also left the Emirates, leaving Mikel Arteta short of options on the left flank. Attempts to secure a deal for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez have so far been unsuccessful.

‌



What is happening to Villa Park? Aston Villa redevelopment work explained as Arsenal visit READ MORE :

A wide‑player addition such as Fofana would represent the fourth piece of business Andrea Berta is working to complete before Tuesday's 11pm deadline. Mirror Football understands Lyon are demanding a fee in the region of £50m with Arsenal still in talks with the 21‑year‑old's representatives.

However, should a deal fail to come to fruition before the transfer deadline, failing to land a left winger to support Tzolis and fill the void left by departing duo Martinelli and Jesus will undoubtedly be considered a significant shortcoming. Berta is already under the microscope for the club's inability, thus far, to pinpoint and secure a genuine upgrade in the wide-left position.

Bradley Barcola attracted admiration from Arsenal, but a price tag in excess of £120m was never going to be entertained. Jeremy Monga was another highly-regarded target whom they made approaches for, yet the club were unwilling to meet the asking price - something Manchester City had no hesitation in doing.

‌



Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has reaffirmed that Arsenal remain steadfast in their commitment to a self-sustaining model, while insisting this does not mean agreeing to sales that are not in the club's best interests.

View 2 Images Arsenal have so far been unable to agree a deal for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"That's what we are trying to get as a club but the balance has to be right," Arteta said. "There are areas that we have to improve to hit those numbers. And if it's not with sales, because maybe we don't want.

"We have to sell what we want to sell as well, not just to sell. And then when we want to sell as well, we have to be very careful because some of the assets, after maybe they grow and we still want them.

"So maybe we can grow in other areas across the club as well. And commercially, we've done incredible. The fan base that we have is incredible.

Article continues below

"Our mass revenue is incredible. And there are other ways to grow and that's the club's strategy. But we want to improve in all of them, obviously, because it's going to give us a bigger room to be stronger financially."

Sports.title: Richarlison launches incredible rant as Iliman Ndiaye twist threatens Everton return
Sports.content:
Richarlison launches incredible rant as Iliman Ndiaye twist threatens Everton return

Tottenham forward Richarlison had been heavily linked with a return to Everton but the Brazilian has made his frustrations known with a public statement

View 2 Images Richarlison has demanded he be treated with respect amid talk of his Tottenham exit

Richarlison has launched an incredible rant on social media with the Tottenham striker insisting no one will force a move upon him.

‌



The Brazilian has been in north London since 2022 when he was signed by Antonio Conte, but has been heavily linked with a move back to Everton as the Toffees and Tottenham had look to agree on a deal which would've seen Iliman Ndiaye head to the capital.

‌



Richarlison, since signing, has seen Dominic Solanke arrive at Tottenham and then this summer they've landed the likes of Omar Marmoush and Savio. That has raised question marks over his role under Roberto De Zerbi but the player himself has come out and demanded "they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs".

‌



Tottenham's move for Ndiaye has since been hijacked by Manchester City, who look to be closing in on the winger's signature, just as Richarlison made his frustration known.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He said on Instagram: "After everything I've gone through in recent years, I decided that NEVER AGAIN would they decide my future for me. I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation - none of that scares me. I've been through worse things... believe me!

‌



"I have always made it clear, at every opportunity, that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn't, I would never accept it... just as I didn't accept it when everything here was crumbling and they needed me. I stayed and gave my life. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't try to decide for me.

“If they reach an agreement Between Spurs and Everton I will return to my heart's club. My intention was indeed to return to the place where I was very happy. It's just that negotiations were going the way people wanted, and it won't be that way anymore. Despite this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs And I will be at the club's disposal."

View 2 Images Iliman Ndiaye is now poised to move to Man City (Image: (Michael Regan/Getty Images))

‌



City have reached an agreement in principle with Everton to land Ndiaye in a package worth £65million. The 26-year-old is expected to undergo a medical on Tuesday morning, reports the Athletic. Ndiaye declined multiple contract offers last season from Everton.

Since losing out, the north Londoners have made an enquiry over a potential loan move for Chelsea forward Mykhailo Mudryk - with Richarlison still receiving no clarity over his future.

The 29-year-old has scored 32 times in 134 games for Tottenham and led the line during their opening weekend loss at Tottenham. In their second outing of the season, a home loss to Newcastle, it was Marmoush who was their central point in attack.

Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes in talks over new Man Utd contract to make him club's best-paid star

Manchester United are set to make Bruno Fernandes their top earner when he signs his next deal as the Portugal star continues to prove his worth at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes' value is set to be rewarded with a huge pay bump

Manchester United are ready to make Bruno Fernandes their highest earner after the playmaker underlined his talismanic status with a hat-trick on Sunday.

‌



Fernandes, just days on from being named the PFA Player of the Year, scored three times in United's 5-2 rout of Ipswich at Old Trafford. The Portugal star was on hand to net their equaliser before the side ran riot in the second half.

‌



Fernandes signed new terms with United in 2022 and 2024, the expiry date of his contract was only extended by a year on each occasion, but his salary increased significantly. The Sun report that his next deal could see him earn around £350,000-a-week

‌



The ex-Sporting Lisbon man currently earns £300,000-a-week. Marcus Rashford is United’s highest earner on a weekly wage of £325,000, but he's spent the last 18 months away from Manchester before returning to the fold.

United have attempted to change their wage structure, adopting more of a measured approach, but those at the club accept that Fernandes is performing to an incredibly high level and is deserving of a major pay bump.

‌



As well as the PFA award, Fernandes also claimed the Football Writers’ Association Player of the Year gong midway through last season, where he broke the record for assists in a single Premier League campaign. He also won an unprecedented fifth Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year award in May.

Fernandes has scored 110 goals in 329 appearances for United since he signed from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola's first words after Liverpool transfer as shirt number revealed
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola's first words after Liverpool transfer as shirt number revealed

Liverpool have finally completed the blockbuster transfer of Bradley Barcola after prolonged negotiations with Paris Saint‑Germain

View Image Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's new signing

Bradley Barcola admitted he can't wait to get on the pitch for Liverpool after being unveiled as their latest signing following a £123million move from Paris Saint‑Germain. The Reds will pay an initial £106m, with a further £17m in potential add‑ons for the winger.

‌



The 23‑year‑old will wear the No.29 shirt at Anfield after becoming the club's second‑most expensive signing of all time - just ahead of Florian Wirtz (£116.5m) and behind only Alexander Isak, who joined from Newcastle for £125m last summer.

‌



"It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy," Barcola told Liverpool's club media. "It took a long time but I'm really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play.

‌



Liverpool transfer state of play as Cody Gakpo holds key ahead of chaotic end to window READ MORE :

"I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it's one of my biggest dreams in my life. It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that's why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.

Barcola was Liverpool's number one target this summer, but it took lengthy negotiations with the French champions to finally get a deal over the line. He completed his medical on Sunday, just a day after Andoni Iraola's side drew 2‑2 with Nottingham Forest at home.

Personal terms with the winger were agreed well in advance, but PSG stood firm on their valuation - which has seen Barcola become Liverpool's second‑most expensive signing of all time.

‌



He arrives on Merseyside as the club’s fourth addition of the summer, following Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo.

His arrival has cast fresh doubt over the future of Cody Gakpo, who could join Manchester City in an £85m deal.

However, any move for Gakpo will only materialise if Liverpool bring in another winger or two, with Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr viewed as potential replacements.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

In France, Barcola collected a string of major honours - back‑to‑back Champions League titles and three successive Ligue 1 crowns during a three‑year spell at Paris Saint‑Germain.

His breakthrough in professional football, however, came at Olympique Lyonnais, where he made his senior debut in November 2021.

Article continues below

He spent 16 years at Lyon after progressing through their academy and went on to make 47 first‑team appearances before joining PSG in 2023.

At Anfield, Barcola will be aiming to replicate that level of success and could make his debut away at Ipswich Town on Friday, September 4, at 8pm.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire Man Utd handball debate could lead to rule change after heated referee review
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire Man Utd handball debate could lead to rule change after heated referee review

Harry Maguire's handball in the build-up to Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich Town has sparked debate over the Premier League handball rule, with calls for an overhaul before next season

View 2 Images Harry Maguire played a big part in Manchester United's controversial second goal vs Ipswich Town. (Image: Zohaib Alam, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Premier League sides have been warned that there could be another change to the handball law next season following Harry Maguire's controversial goal for Manchester United vs Ipswich Town. United came out as 5-2 winners over the Tractor Boys, but the goal to give United the lead came with a fair amount of protest from the away side.

‌



With the score at 1-1, Maguire has a shot on goal in the 57th minute. It deflected off Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves and past goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen. But replays showed the ball hitting Maguire's hand before he took the shot.

‌



It led Ipswich players and fans to demand that the goal be ruled out. It was, however, allowed to stand after a VAR review, due to Maguire not directly being the goalscorer.

‌



The early signs showing new Premier League season will be very different to last year READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Had Maguire directly benefited from the handball and found the net himself, Ipswich would have been awarded a free-kick. As he was not, United were handed a second goal and seized the lead for the first time in the match.

However, former Premier League striker Jay Bothroyd now believes the rule will be amended and that such a goal would be ruled out under new regulations he claims will be introduced for next season.

‌



"They got the decision right because it's in the rule," Bothroyd told Sky Sports. "But the rule is rubbish. At the end of the day, it's a handball and a goal came because of it. That is unfair.

View 2 Images Harry Maguire takes a shot that leads to Manchester United's second goal vs Ipswich. (Image: Richard Sellers/Allstar, Getty Images)

"Maguire's handled the ball, it's not intentional as his hands are up there. But as soon as it falls to him and he has the shot and it goes in via a deflection, it should be brought back. Because that goal doesn't happen if it doesn't hit his hands. It's a poor rule because Man Utd have benefited from it the same way as if Maguire had scored.

‌



"The decision is 100% right. But the rule is wrong. It will 100% be changed by next season."

Meanwhile, former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher weighed in with his assessment, siding with referee Craig Pawson and VAR in their ruling that the goal should stand.

"It's definitely the right decision. it strikes his hand, but striking his hand isn't an offence in itself," Gallagher said. "It has to be deliberate or lead to a goal scored by himself.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"It strikes Maguire's hand, he shoots, it's going wide and hits Greaves, so it becomes an own goal. So through no fault of the referee or VAR, they have to give the goal. It's always been the rule. It was changed a few years ago. It's clearly an own goal and it's covered in law.

"It's accidental handball. It's unfortunate for Ipswich but it's ironic that we're debating the decision. The only thing to debate is whether you like the rule or not."

Sports.title: Gary Neville reveals dream end to Man Utd transfer window with two new arrivals
Sports.content:
Gary Neville reveals dream end to Man Utd transfer window with two new arrivals

Manchester United have until 11pm on Tuesday night to add more players to Michael Carrick's squad and Gary Neville is worried about their defence after the Ipswich win

View 2 Images Gary Neville has given his assessment on Manchester United's squad (Image: YouTube/Sky Sports)

Gary Neville has urged Manchester United to sign TWO defenders before the summer transfer window closes at 11pm on Tuesday.

‌



United have focused on their midfield this summer, signing Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba from Aston Villa, Chelsea and Brighton respectively for a combined £155million. Michael Carrick said he was "quite happy" with his squad following the 5-2 win over Ipswich on Sunday and hinted more deals might not follow.

‌



That is despite United so far failing to sign a left-back to provide competition for Luke Shaw. Having failed to land top target Lewis Hall from Newcastle and baulked at Barcelona's asking price for Alejandro Balde, United are facing the prospect of going without a new left-back this summer.

‌



While United's attack impressed at Old Trafford, with Bruno Fernandes scoring a hat-trick, their defence looked vulnerable and conceded two goals for the second consecutive week against a newly-promoted side. Shaw was beaten by Abdul Fatawu for Ipswich's opener before Lisandro Martinez was robbed for their late consolation.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Neville commentated on the game for Sky Sports, was concerned by what he saw and believes immediate action is necessary. "Manchester United's back four can be got at," he said on The Gary Neville podcast.

"We knew that because it's the same defenders as last season and the season before. They conceded 50 last season, so it's not going to change unless they play better - which let's hope they do - but also that the midfield two protects them more.

"That has to happen or else they'll concede a lot of goals. They've conceded four in two [Premier League games] already, they've conceded a lot of chances against Ipswich in the first half and this is not going to be a team that's going to be in the top half of the league, more than likely, so that would be the concern.

‌



View 2 Images Luke Shaw is in his 13th season at Manchester United and needs competition (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"It's not me shouting, 'buy a load of players, do this, spend your money' but what Manchester United have done is they've rebuilt their attack last season. They've rebuilt the midfield this season. It feels like they're going to wait to rebuild the defence for another 12 months.

"I don't know if there are one or two defenders available, but if there are, can you somehow try and advance that money into this window and then spend less next season? Because it would really make a massive difference if they could get a centre-back and a full-back in.

‌



"You saw at the end of the game [against Ipswich] when [Diogo] Dalot and Shaw go off, you've got [Leny] Yoro playing right-back, and you've got [Noussair] Mazraoui playing left-back. That's not ideal at all.

"One of them [Yoro] is makeshift full-back at best, there's no lack of willingness for him to play there, but he's not a full-back. Mazraoui can play left-back, but he's not the left-back that you want there."

Journalist: "I'm curious, with the week leading up to the Open, there are so many events and everything, it can be kind of physically draining. On top of being the top seed here and among the favourites, how do you balance the energy, especially with the energy that New York brings into your tennis? And then looking over the next two weeks, how do you kind of maintain a steady level with your energy?"

Sabalenka: "What is the question there?"

Journalist: "I'm curious, you had so much going on last week. Now it's just focus on tennis and there's a bit of pressure."

Sabalenka: "Why do you think the week before I wasn't focused on tennis?"

Journalist: "Oh I think you were. I just think you were busy with a lot of events."

Sabalenka: "It's like my hobby outside of tennis. The whole schedule we plan is all around tennis. So all of those events are not drawing me away in any way."

Sports.title: Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Sabalenka also wins
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open.

Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.

The severity of the injury, which did not require surgery, meant Alcaraz was a doubt for the US Open but he entered Flushing Meadows and showed with his 6-4 6-4 6-4 win over Safiullin that he cannot be dismissed to defend his title from last year.

"There were some doubts in the match, I'm not going to lie. Thinking about if I would last the match, best of five, playing four or five sets," said Alcaraz, who will play Portugal's Jaime Faria in the next round.

"I had a little bit of doubt, but I tried to forget everything and focus on the things I needed to improve. I thought about what would happen in the match and physically I felt really well."

Henman: Alcaraz got the game he wanted Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman



"If you’d have asked Alcaraz how he’d have liked this game to go, he would have signed up for a straight-sets victory, a few pressure moments, and just over two hours work.



"That is exactly what he got today. He and his team will be delighted with all aspects of this game."

Watched on by rapper Travis Scott, who helped design Alcaraz's brown outfit for the US Open, there was plenty of attention on the seven-time Grand Slam champion's serve and groundstroke speed, given he had not played competitive singles for over four months.

He needed to save two break points from Safiullin in his opening three service games before breaking himself in the eighth game which proved enough to claim the opening set.

Alcaraz was broken at the start of the second set but broke back immediately and upped his intensity to break in the eighth game again and go on to win the second set.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz reflected on his US Open round one win. against Roman Safiullin

After an early break in the third set, Alcaraz never came under threat on his serve and continued to move well while maintaining a high level on both wins to see off the tricky Russian.

One of the biggest threats in Alcaraz's half was Arthur Fils, after he won the Cincinnati Open title last week, but he was knocked out of the tournament by Stefanos Tsitsipas in a 4-6 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 6-4 defeat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How many previous US Open winners could you name in 20-seconds?

Sabalenka overcomes Osorio test

Like Alcaraz, Aryna Sabalenka started her US Open title with a straight-sets win as she beat Colombia's Camila Osorio 6-2 6-4.

Sabalenka is bidding to become the first player to win three consecutive US Open titles since Serena Williams in 2014 and was put under serious pressure by Osorio in the second set.

"Camila is a tough opponent but I was ready to do whatever it takes to get the win," she told Sky Sports Tennis.

"I really enjoyed the atmosphere and support. A fun and tough match but happy to get through in straight sets."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Aryna Sabalenka and Camila Osorio

Sabalenka's form has been questioned after losing in the last 16 in her last three tournaments - Wimbledon, the Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open.

It means she could lose her status as world No 1 for the first time since October 2024 with Elena Rybakina, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula all having the chance to knock Sabalenka off her perch.

But Sabalenka's best surface is the hard court, having won her four Grand Slam titles on hard, and her raw power will always make the Belarusian difficult to beat.

Elsewhere, Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova will be looking for another big run and she got off to a great start by beating Austria's Sinja Karus 6-3 6-0.

Sports.title: McIlroy: 'Grumpy' world No 2 needs 'new goal' after FedEx Cup claims
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy needs to assess how much he truly wants to be world No 1 again alongside balancing his home life, according to former golfer Rob Lee.

The Northern Irishman finished in a seven-way tie for fourth at the FedEx Cup over the weekend, finishing five shots off tournament winner Scottie Scheffler despite showing earlier signs of promise.

Now 37, six-time major winner McIlroy admitted his "fuse was shorter than it used to be" before the final round at the East Lake Golf Club.

Image: Rory McIlroy has admitted his patience with the demands of professional golf is thinning

He had arrived in Atlanta off the back of three weeks of competing in a row, something he admitted he would never exceed again despite still managing a fourth-place finish over the weekend.

"That just tells you how good he is," Lee told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast. "But I think Rory's body language this week wasn't great. He looked slightly… is grumpy the right word?

"But he's just slightly off that kind of affable, bouncy Rory that we normally see. So there's stuff going on with him… Rory's in this position. He's played golf for 20 years at the highest level. He's 37.

"He realises there are other things in life, but the last thing he wants to do is not be able to be peak Rory. So his conundrum is 'how much can I pare back my schedule, but still perform the way I know I can?' That's the place he's in now.

"37 is still golfing prime. It's going to come down, for him, to desire. How much does he still want it? And if he still wants it, I think he's going to have to play a bit more."

McIlroy took an extended break after The Open, spending more time with his family before returning for this three-week run of events.

Image: Scheffler clinched his second FedExCup title after he secured a three-shot victory at the Tour Championship

"I absolutely think he can win more majors," Lee continued. "But going along with that is you sacrifice your home life. You're not as home as much as you want to be… I actually think Rory is in mentally quite a good place at the moment, and he is focused on some family stuff at the moment."

Speaking before his final round, McIlroy admitted: "once you lose your enthusiasm to go to the course, it is time to take a break." That comment could suggest golf fans could be seeing less and less of the world No 2 as time goes on.

"I think that's plausible," Sean Zak agreed. "I think that the changes coming to the PGA Tour schedule could pull a little bit more out of him, could help him balance being a dual member a little bit better."

Zak went on to suggest McIlroy may need to set himself a goal of beating Scheffler to top spot to reignite his motivation.

"You know, of all the golfers at the top of the game, I think he better than most shows what things matter to him and shows the goals that he's set," he said.

"And I think ever since that Grand Slam-finishing Masters win, he has just struggled to really place "OK, what's the next goal?"

Image: Rory McIlroy won the Masters in 2025 and 2026

"When you look at 2025, when he won that Masters, the next goal was really, 'OK, let's win at Bethpage' - and then they did that.

"Then after that, it was 'gosh, OK, what is the next goal?' I think for him to live up to what we're asking him to do right now, what a lot of fans would like him to do, is his next goal needs to be taking Scottie off the top mark or matching Scottie in some way.

"I bet if Scottie won a major this year, Rory might feel a little bit more of the fire beneath him because you get to some point where they've all won a bunch.

"What is the tiebreaker? How many majors did you win? Rory still has a nice little lead on Scottie - but how long will that last? We think that he probably won't hold that lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sean Zak from golf.com asks what is Rory McIlroy's next goal after his grand slam Masters win?

"It's just funny because I think Rory McIlroy, let's say [at] 21 years old was like "I want to be number one in the world. I want to win every single tournament."

"Rory McIlroy, 37-year-old, he may have to do the same thing. It should be 'I want to be number one. I want the world to think I'm the best golfer because at my best, I certainly am.'"

McIlroy will next compete at the Irish Open, starting on September 10.

Sports.title: Man City agree £65m Ndiaye deal as Spurs turn attention to Mudryk
Sports.content:
Manchester City have agreed a £65m deal with Everton for winger Iliman Ndiaye as an alternative to Cody Gakpo.

With contact already established between City and Everton over Jack Grealish, discussions have moved swiftly.

City's deal is broken up into a £60m guaranteed payment plus £5m in bonuses.

Richarlison's reluctance to make a final decision on a move to Everton held up Spurs' advanced talks involving Ndiaye that had been ongoing since yesterday.

It means Tottenham are looking to alternative targets and have started talks with Chelsea about a loan for Mykhailo Mudryk.

Earlier on Monday, Liverpool rejected City's £80m bid for Cody Gakpo.

Sky Sports News understands Liverpool are concerned about their chances of bringing in a replacement for the Dutchman.

Manchester City want to sign a wide forward and a central midfielder before the window closes.

City also opened talks with Chelsea for Enzo Fernandez on Monday.

Manchester City allowed Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham earlier month, reducing Enzo Maresca's options on the wing.

City did not name a winger on their bench in Friday's win over Crystal Palace and started with Phil Foden - who Enzo Maresca admitted is not a winger - out wide at Selhurst Park.

Liverpool signed Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday while Victor Munoz arrived from Osasuna earlier this summer.

Spurs also targeted Gakpo in this window before signing Savio and Marmoush.

Sports.title: McInnes ban verdict over 'disgusting' comment revealed after Rangers appeal
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes' immediate touchline ban has been reduced following Rangers' appeal.

The 55-year-old was initially handed a four-match suspension by the Scottish FA, with three of those games to be served immediately.

While the overall ban remains in place, he will now only serve two of those with immediate effect, while the other two will only be triggered should he breach disciplinary rule 72 again before the end of this season.

As part of disciplinary rule 72 you can not: (i) criticise the decision(s) and/or performance(s) of any or all match official(s) in such a way as to indicate bias or incompetence on the part of such match official; or (ii) make remarks about such match official(s) which impinge on his character

It's after the former Hearts boss described the penalty awarded to Celtic against Motherwell's last May as "disgusting".

The first game McInnes will be in the stands for is Wednesday's trip to Falkirk, live on Sky Sports, followed by their game at Ibrox against Motherwell on Saturday.

It means McInnes will return to the touchline for their league match against St Mirren next Wednesday.

Following that is their Old Firm double-header as Celtic visit in the League Cup on September 13, before a trip to Celtic Park in the Premiership a week later - live on Sky Sports.

Rangers' fixtures Wednesday: Falkirk (A) - Scottish Premiership - live on Sky Sports

Saturday: Motherwell (H) - Scottish Premiership

Sept 9: St Mirren (H) - Scottish Premiership

Sept 13: Celtic (H) - League Cup

Sept 20: Celtic (A) - Scottish Premiership - live on Sky Sports

McInnes has endured a tough start to life as Rangers manager, with his side knocked out of Europe completely after Europa League and then Conference League defeats.

Domestically, Sunday's win at Aberdeen was his first in the Premiership, with the club five points behind Celtic after three games.

What was the ban for?

In May, then Hearts head coach McInnes saw his side beat Falkirk in their penultimate league match. Meanwhile, Celtic were being held at Motherwell, meaning Hearts were set to go three points clear at the top and had a better goal difference over Celtic. That meant Hearts would be crowned champions if they avoided a heavy defeat at Parkhead on the final day.

However, in added time, Celtic were awarded a late penalty at Fir Park following a VAR check for a handball by Motherwell's Sam Nicholson. That was converted to seal victory for Martin O'Neill's side, and leave the gap between the sides at just one point.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the interview from May, when then Hearts boss McInnes expressed his disappointment over the decision to award Celtic a penalty for handball against Motherwell

McInnes said the decision to issue the spot-kick was "disgusting". Celtic then went on to beat Hearts on the final day, denying them a first top-flight title in 66 years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The incident that angered McInnes as VAR awarded Celtic a penalty in the dying seconds of their game at Motherwell

Former Motherwell player Elliot Watt was handed a four-match ban by the SFA for describing that penalty award as the "worst VAR decision in history".

The Fir Park side were also fined £5,000 after their own social media post following that match.

Sports.title: Is now the right time for Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' US Open loss?
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic said he "despised" every moment of the five-set, near five-hour ordeal which ended his US Open hopes in the first round, so now the question is whether he calls time on his trophy-laden career.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion was knocked out in the first round of the US Open for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina.

Djokovic was 19-0 in the US Open first round and hadn't lost his opening match in any major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Djokovic was visibly upset during the final set in his US Open first round defeat to Mariano Navone

The 39-year-old also admitted the underlying health issue he first revealed two weeks ago was "serious", although he remains intent on getting the problem fixed.

Djokovic looked physically spent, was repeatedly sick and regularly doubled over in pain. He held back tears at one point but managed a gracious smile as he congratulated world No 49 Navone on the biggest win of his career.

He has previously revealed that he plans to retire at the LA Olympics in 2028, draped in the flag of Serbia for one last time.

Former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli said: "It was so sad to watch. To see him suffer that much was heart-breaking.

"The way he was physically suffering is worrying. His health should come first, so he needs to have proper medical checks to see what happens."

A tough watch

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Navone and Djokovic

Former British No 1 Tim Henman admitted defeat for Djokovic "was a tough watch" but does not think he should retire.

"Djokovic wasn't feeling well out on court. He gave it his absolute all to find a way through the match. When he was up two sets to one with a break in the fourth, you thought he could," said the former US Open semi-finalist.

"But he was vomiting on the court and didn't have the energy. Navone kept on fighting and, with youth on his side, he ran away with the fourth and fifth set."

On the idea of retirement, Henman said: "Absolutely not. It's his decision, it's his prerogative. He's No 5 in the world. If every person who was fifth best in the world at their occupation retired, there wouldn't be many people working. It's purely his decision. He should play for as long as he likes and I definitely don't think he should be stopping right now."

Asked whether an ailing Djokovic has what it takes physically anymore, Henman replied: "His mentality and will to win is still good enough [to win titles] but when you see the physical challenges of being 39 and what his body is going through and trying to find solutions - it's tough.

"When you hear him saying he 'despised being out there', that's awful.

"I'm sure he will go away and assess things because that's not the way we want to see Djokovic depart any tournament."

Sports.title: Aston Villa v Arsenal: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
now 16.54 EDT 90 min +6: Maatsen clatters Saka out on the right touchline in the you-shall-not-pass style. Into the book he goes. Villa frustrated, Arsenal doing a good job of running down the clock. Share

40s ago 16.53 EDT 90 min +5: McGinn clips Merino out on the right touchline. On a booking, the Villa captain wants to watch himself here. Nothing comes of the free kick. “Looks like the carefree, freewheeling Arsenal, released from the burden of not winning the title, has lasted one whole match,” observes the tinder-dry Matt Emerson, one eyebrow hoisted high. Share

2m ago 16.51 EDT 90 min +3: Buendia and Wan-Bissaka apply pressure down the right, but Guimaraes muscles them both out of the road, before ushering the ball out for a goal kick. Then he celebrates as though he’d just scored the clincher. Share

4m ago 16.50 EDT 90 min +2: It’s all Villa in terms of possession … but they can’t get anything going in the final third. Share

5m ago 16.49 EDT 90 min: There will be eight additional minutes! There’s been a lot of substitutions and some hot VAR action, to be fair. Share

6m ago 16.48 EDT 89 min: Suzuki races out of his goal to deal with a long ball down the middle. A powerful header clear. And this is as good a time as any for Ben Suenaga, of 50 min fame, to explain himself re Japanese superstars in the Premier League: “I know I bring shame by uttering the words but for once with Suzuki we can have a protagonist.” Share

7m ago 16.47 EDT 88 min: How’s this for a stat, flashed up by Sky Sports? Aston Villa have yet to have a shot on target this season! Coventry next on the list with four attempts, while Palace, Leeds and Forest have had five. Share

9m ago 16.45 EDT 86 min: Saka wins a corner down the right … then wastes it. McGinn tries to find Garnacho with a long pass … but overhits it. Raya claims, and waits an age with the ball at his feet before a Villa player closes him down. Abraham finally arrives, and as Raya picks up, both players have a short conversation. For a second, it threatens to escalate, but the two grown men eventually see sense. We play on. Share

11m ago 16.43 EDT 85 min: Zubimendi comes on for Rice, who isn’t moving freely. Share

12m ago 16.42 EDT 84 min: Maatsen scampers down the left and enters the box, going over as Rice and White sandwich him. He screams for a penalty, but there’s no way that’ll be given. And it isn’t. Share

12m ago 16.41 EDT 83 min: Arsenal are sitting back, holding their shape. Villa seeing the majority of the ball for the first time this evening. Share

14m ago 16.39 EDT 81 min: Now McGinn goes into the book for an agricultural lunge through the back of Merino. That wasn’t so great, and he’s lucky the referee has been, for the most part, in a laissez-faire mood tonight. Share

16m ago 16.38 EDT 80 min: Alysson is booked for a late clip on Gabriel. Share

16m ago 16.38 EDT 79 min: Mosquera is indeed unable to continue, so Konsa comes on for his Arsenal debut … and though there’s a few boos, the majority of home fans applaud their former player, who played such a big part in last season’s Europa League victory. That a lovely – and pretty cool – moment. Share Updated at 16.39 EDT

18m ago 16.36 EDT 78 min: … but first, a couple of Villa debutants, as Garnacho and Wan-Bissaka come on for Barkley and Cash. Share

19m ago 16.35 EDT 77 min: Mosquera goes down with what looks like cramp. Looks like a baptism of fire coming up for erstwhile Villa hero Konsa. Share

20m ago 16.34 EDT 75 min: Suzuki makes good by saving from Havertz, the Arsenal striker having been put clean through by Guimaraes. Havertz opened his body and looked for the bottom left, but the keeper won the duel with a fine parry. Share

21m ago 16.33 EDT 74 min: Havertz has a dig from the edge of the box. Suzuki spills the shot, which rebounds the best part of ten yards in front of him, but there’s nobody in 1979 yellow to take advantage, and he covers the ground to gather. Share

22m ago 16.31 EDT 73 min: Alysson immediately gets involved, tearing his way past Calafiori down the right. He’s unable to find anyone in the centre with his low cross. His aim not so true. Share

23m ago 16.30 EDT 72 min: … so Aston Villa respond by throwing on Abraham and Alysson, at the expense of Jackson and Hemmings. Share

24m ago 16.29 EDT 70 min: Arsenal send on Merino and Guimarães in place of Lewis-Skelly and Odegaard … Share

27m ago 16.27 EDT 68 min: Odegaard finds Havertz in space inside the box on the right. He’s tugged back by Kamara, but neither ref nor VAR shows any interest in giving a spot kick. Then Villa go up the other end, Maatsen nibbled at by White as he cuts into the box from the left, but ref and VAR collectively shrug again. Just about everyone in the crowd fuming, for one reason or another. Share

30m ago 16.24 EDT 66 min: Hemmings strides into a pocket of space down the middle of the park. He’s got Barkley to his right, but tries to release Jackson down the middle with a slide-rule pass. Rice is on point to intercept with a swagger. Share

31m ago 16.22 EDT 65 min: … and so having said that, Villa finally reach the Arsenal box, McGinn embarking on a baroque ramble down the inside-right channel. But he can’t get a shot away, and when he cuts back for Cash, Calafiori is on point to deal with the danger. Share

32m ago 16.22 EDT 63 min: … and as if to prove that point, Arsenal slip straight back into a state of calm authority. Villa are yet to respond. Share

34m ago 16.20 EDT 61 min: That goal had sort of been coming. On Sky, Gary Neville points out that Arsenal hadn’t really looked like scoring, but were in the ascendency and staying patient, and finally got their reward. Share

36m ago 16.18 EDT GOAL! Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal (Saka 59) That little chain of events had put Villa fans in a good humour. But they’re not so happy now. Gabriel finds Eze to the left of the box. Eze plays Calafiori in down the channel. Calafiori slides ahead of Lindelof to meet the pass and whip it low into the centre, and Saka, beating his old foe Maatsen, can’t miss from a couple of yards. View image in fullscreen Saka scores. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters Share Updated at 16.23 EDT

39m ago 16.15 EDT 57 min: Odegaard whips a cheeky free kick over the wall and inches wide of the right-hand post. Suzuki hadn’t been expecting it, and wouldn’t have got there. Goal kick. Share

39m ago 16.14 EDT VAR: No penalty for Arsenal 56 min: VAR gets involved. Maatsen did foul Saka, leaning into his back … but the foul occurred just outside the box, to the right of the D. It’ll be a free kick to Arsenal instead. Share

41m ago 16.13 EDT Penalty for Arsenal 54 min: Maatsen’s woes continue as Saka nips in ahead of him down the right, and he leans in from behind, bringing the winger down as he enters the box. After some thought, the referee points to the spot. View image in fullscreen Bukayo Saka is fouled by Ian Maatsen. Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at 16.19 EDT

42m ago 16.11 EDT 52 min: Thinking about that, Ben … Shinji Kagawa (Manchester United), Shinji Okazaki (Leicester City), Takumi Minamino and Wataru Endo (both Liverpool), Japanese Premier League title-winners all, may want a word. Share Updated at 16.15 EDT

44m ago 16.09 EDT 50 min: Rice curls a delicious cross in from the right, but Havertz can’t beat Lindelof in the air at the far stick. Suzuki claims. Speaking of whom … “Here is hoping Japan have our first Premier League superstar in Zion!” begins Ben Suenaga. “Quite a jump coming from Parma but he is looking right at home. No disrespect to Mitoma and Daizen.” Share

48m ago 16.06 EDT 48 min: Maatsen looks for Jackson this time, with a pass down the left touchline, but only manages to roll the ball out of play, nowhere near his team-mate. Not the best 60 seconds of his career. Share

49m ago 16.05 EDT 47 min: Barkley spots Maatsen in acres of space out on the left. He loops a pass down the flank. Maatsen enters the box and, with only Jackson in the middle, and not in that much space, opts for the spectacular, aiming for the top-left corner. He finds the top-left corner of the Holte End. Share

51m ago 16.03 EDT Aston Villa get the second half underway. Arsenal have hooked Tzolis, who was on a booking and involved in a running duel with Cash, and replaced him with Eze. Share

53m ago 16.01 EDT Half-time postbag II, because why not? “Football refereeing is so stuck in the subjective age and so little reference is made to the actual stated rulebook that there will no improvement in consistency or ‘fairness’. Listen to the TV refs in rugby and cricket and they quote the rulebook and say whether what has happened does or does not comply with the factual rule. VAR in football is just the pundit class pontificating about this or that with little or no reference to any particular rule. I don’t like VAR for what it does tot he flow of the game, but being applied this badly just rankles with my sense of decency” – Nic “Judging by his delivery to camera in the kit video, a career in the movies beckons for John McGinn after his playing days are over. He’s got the cheeky chappie Scot ex-footballer with a twinkle in his eye parts sewn up” – Simon McMahon Share

1h ago 15.50 EDT Half-time postbag. “I know the new stand will benefit Villa in the long term, but it feels like another thing counting against them at the moment: they could really use the extra support after the summer they’ve had. Always had a soft spot for Villa and hope they do well, but feel like this season could turn into a real struggle for them. Like a flirting with relegation-type struggle. Hope I’m wrong” – Joshua Keeling “Emery is a splendid coach and a Villa legend, but this enforced rebuild needs to work and it needs to work fast. Sports.title: Argentina’s Lionel Messi retires from international football: ‘This hurts me a lot’
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football seven weeks after Argentina were beaten by Spain in the World Cup final in the US. The 39-year-old captained Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022 and two Copa América titles after winning his first cap in 2005.

On Monday, Messi posted a picture on Instagram of notes that he wrote on 21 July, two days after the World Cup final, confirming he was ending his Argentina career and said the death of his father, Jorge, in early August made him feel “more convinced than before”. Messi was often visibly emotional during the tournament and revealed in the knockout stages that Jorge was undergoing medical treatment.

Messi’s statement, addressed to Argentina fans, read: “After the time that has passed since the final, thinking a lot, I want to let everyone know that I am retiring from the national team. It is a decision that hurts my soul but I know it is time. I can say for sure that I always gave everything, not only in the last few years when we won everything [but] before as well, and I always fought and gave everything for the shirt, to give you joy and make you proud of being Argentinian through football.

“There’s not long left and chapters are coming to an end – and this is one that hurts me a lot. I love, have loved and I will always love being part of the national team. I have emptied myself: now I have nothing more to give and, besides, there are great young players coming through who deserve to be [selected].”

Messi thanked his family for accompanying him on a “beautiful but difficult journey”. He previously announced his retirement from international football in 2016 after Argentina lost on penalties to Chile in the 2016 Copa América final – at the time his fourth defeat in a major final out of four. The then Barcelona forward was often criticised for not producing his club form at international level and comparisons were constantly made with the World Cup-winning Diego Maradona. However, Messi was persuaded to continue and finally lifted silverware with his country at the 2021 Copa América in Brazil.

“I take with me unforgettable memories and moments,” his statement said. After victory against Brazil at the Maracanã in the 2021 Copa América final, Messi was central to Argentina’s first World Cup triumph since 1986 and scored in every knockout round in Qatar, including twice in the final against France – two years after the death of Maradona.

Quick Guide How do I 

Argentina defended their Copa América title in 2024 amid speculation that Messi, by then playing for Inter Miami, would call it a day. He turned 39 during the World Cup this summer, briefly becoming the tournament’s all-time record scorer before being overtaken by Kylian Mbappé.

His statement finished by returning to address Argentina fans: “I go with the satisfaction and the pride of having, along with my teammates, giving you moments we dreamed about. I love you! I thank God for making me Argentinian.”

Messi retires as Argentina’s record appearance maker – he won the first of his 207 caps in a friendly against Hungary in August 2005 and was sent off almost immediately for catching Vilmos Vanczak with an elbow. He is also Argentina’s record scorer with 125 goals. Before playing for the senior team, he won the Under-20 World Cup and also won Olympic gold in 2008.

Since the end of his sixth World Cup, Messi has featured seven times for Inter Miami and scored four goals in the 7-1 rout of Montreal in Major League Soccer on Saturday. Messi signed a contract extension last year to 2028, when he will be 41.

Sports.title: Manchester City gazump Spurs over Iliman Ndiaye and eye Enzo Fernández deal
Sports.content:
Manchester City are poised to ­bolster their attack by buying Everton’s ­Iliman Ndiaye for up to £65m and have opened talks with Chelsea over a deal to sign Enzo Fernández.

City’s hijack of Tottenham’s deal for Ndiaye came after their attempts to sign Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo broke down. The Senegal international is poised to undergo a medical after a fee of £60m plus £5m in add-ons was agreed with Everton, who have little time to find a replacement for one of their most important players before the transfer window shuts on Tuesday night.

It had seemed that Ndiaye would move to Spurs after they agreed a deal in principle with Everton on Sunday. Richarlison was poised to move in the opposite direction but that transfer stalled on Monday.

Richarlison released an emotional statement on social media and said that he would not allow his future to be decided for him. The Brazilian is cold on a move to Everton and is expected to stay at Spurs.

City registered their interest in Ndiaye last week and moved in after Liverpool pulled out of an £85m deal for Gakpo. Spurs have moved on to other attacking targets and in a surprise development are poised to sign Mykhailo Mudryk on loan from Chelsea.

The Ukraine winger, who is free to play again after his doping ban was resolved this summer, played for Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk and favours a ­reunion with the ­Tottenham manager. Leeds and Brentford have also contacted ­Chelsea about Mudryk.

Chelsea are poised for a busy end to the window and have finally been contacted by City about Fernández. The Argentina midfielder wants to leave and has his heart set on a move to City. Fernández has a close relationship with City’s manager, Enzo Maresca, who left Chelsea earlier this year.

Chelsea set a price of £120m for Fernández this summer and may push for a higher fee with the deadline drawing close. Another consideration for the Stamford Bridge club as they face up to losing one of their biggest players is the need to improve their squad.

Chelsea have sounded out Roma’s Manu Koné and Monaco’s Lamine Camara as potential replacements for Fernández. are tracking Morgan Gibbs‑White but know Nottingham Forest are unlikely to sell at this stage.

The goalkeeper Robert Sánchez is poised to leave Chelsea as he nears a loan to Como. Sánchez lost the No 1 spot after Emiliano Martínez’s arrival.

Sports.title: Liverpool sign Barcola in £123m deal and expect Gakpo to stay after City offer £80m
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola is aiming to win the Premier League after completing his move to Liverpool from Paris Saint‑Germain for an initial £106m, which could rise to £123m. The France international has signed a five-year deal.

Andoni Iraola has prioritised signing wingers this summer after replacing Arne Slot. Barcola follows the arrival of Victor Muñoz as the former Bournemouth head coach aims to rebuild the front line.

“It took a long time but I’m really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play,” Barcola said. “I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it’s one of my biggest dreams in my life. It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that’s why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.”

Barcola, who will be 24 on Wednesday, was a long-term target for Liverpool, who have tracked his progress over a number of seasons. Completing the transfer has been delayed while PSG waited to make signings to compensate for the exit of the former Lyon player, who attracted interested from other clubs but was adamant that he was willing to join only Liverpool.

Quick Guide How do I 

“When I knew about Liverpool’s interest in me, I didn’t ask questions and I knew it was a very big club for me,” Barcola said.

The Frenchman will probably be Liverpool’s final incoming. The club are expecting Cody Gakpo to stay after rejecting an £80m offer from Manchester City for the Dutchman over the weekend. Liverpool would regard selling a first-team player at this stage as problematic because it would allow little time to source a replacement.

Harvey Elliott is expected to join Valencia on loan for the season. The midfielder returned this summer from a similar spell at Aston Villa, where he failed to make an impression and although he was part of the pre-season plans, has failed to make the squad for the opening two Premier League fixtures.

Liverpool have targeted younger players in this window, evidenced by the signings of Barcola, the 21‑year‑old Jérémy Jacquet and the 23‑year‑old Muñoz in the hope of building a squad for the long term.

Sports.title: Chelsea’s perfect yet unserious start to the Premier League season | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Two Premier League games played for Chelsea under Xabi Alonso: two wins and seven goals scored. It’s the sort of start that would delight many new managers – only two other clubs can boast about a six-point start this Premier League season (albeit with Arsenal to play later on Monday). Points gained in this odd transitional phase, when almost nobody seems quite ready, could prove extremely valuable come the end of the season. And yet, for all the attacking potency, there must also be concerns about Chelsea’s openness and the five goals conceded.

Context must also be considered, and it projects both ways. It’s early in the season. There has been, as ever, a lot of change at Chelsea. They will get better; they will achieve greater coherence. But equally there has to be a sense of realism about the nature of the teams they’ve played. Brighton may have thrashed a shambolic Aston Villa 4-0 last weekend, but they were missing seven frontline players at Stamford Bridge and still put three past Chelsea on Sunday. And while Fulham looked very lively as Chelsea won 3-2 on the opening weekend, they couldn’t muster a shot on target against Sunderland on Sunday.

How good are Brighton? Were Villa just terrible on that first weekend? Was it really just Granit Xhaka’s appeal for Sunderland to be themselves again that made a side that had lost at Ipswich capable of dominating Fulham through midfield? It’s very hard at this stage to trace any patterns, other than perhaps to say that Xhaka’s performance against Fulham showed why Chelsea wanted to sign him in the summer.

The systems are different, so the comparison perhaps isn’t entirely fair, but Xhaka, and his midfield partner Noah Sadiki, offered a level of control that Chelsea under Alonso have so far been entirely lacking – striking, given the degree of control Enzo Maresca insisted upon as manager last season. Both Chelsea games so far have felt almost like a pastiche of the modern Bundesliga: all high tempo and turnovers, chaotic and fun and slightly unserious.

This is not how it’s meant to be. Alonso’s Bayer Leverkusen side, in which Xhaka was partnered in central midfield by one of Robert Andrich, Aleix García, or Exequiel Palacios, won the Bundesliga in 2024 conceding only 24 goals in 34 league games. They averaged 59.5% possession, whereas Chelsea so far this season have had just 32%. Perhaps when Moisés Caicedo returns to fitness – he managed 14 minutes from the bench on Sunday before being forced off again – his energy and mobility will bring an immediate improvement, but the way both Fulham and Brighton have at times sliced through Chelsea suggests there are structural issues.

The usual criticism of the 3-4-2-1 formation used by Chelsea is that it is too blockish, that creativity comes almost entirely from the two inside-forwards, making the side playing it predictable if they dominate possession. Its usage, at least in the Premier League, tends to have been as a counterattacking system – this is how, for instance, Oliver Glasner deployed it at Crystal Palace over the last two seasons. Two holding players operating in front of a back three should provide the trapezoid shape that has become the default for sides hoping to guard against the counter. Yet with Roméo Lavia alongside either Reece James or Malo Gusto, that solidity has been lacking.

Why, then, is Alonso’s system suffering the opposite problem? The issue really stems from a positive: Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 is not the blockish formation often seen. Rather it is a basis from which multiple variations stem. It has a variety that helps overcome a potential over-reliance on the two inside-forwards. That’s how, for instance, center back Maxence Lacroix ended up bursting through to set up a goal against Fulham. Breaking the lines and varying the pattern is part of the pattern.

The defensive concerns predate Alonso. It’s been 18 games since Chelsea last kept a clean sheet, their longest run in the top flight since 1961. While the signing of Emí Martínez should give them a more assertive, less error-prone figure in goal than Robert Sánchez in goal, there will be issues, at least in the short term, in getting the balance right at full-back. Plus, defences are best when they are stable, when interactions become automatic; while Lacroix is the sort of central defender Chelsea have been short of and will almost certainly make them better in the long term, and while Josh Acheampong, who played well against Fulham and came off the bench against Brighton, looks a hugely promising presence (he started only eight league games last season); incorporating both of them while adapting to a new goalkeeper will take time. There is a cost to the constant churn at Chelsea.
