Arsenal, next Sunday, will provide a far stiffer test. Chelsea’s front three of João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer give them a puncher’s chance, but there is a chance Arsenal render them irrelevant by dominating the game through the midfield. They are two teams at very different stages of their development.

Sports.title: Fifa extends ban on man who secretly filmed female footballers in Austria
Sports.content:
Fifa has extended worldwide the ban on a former match official and SCR Altach employee found guilty of taking secret videos and photographs of members of the club’s women’s team.

In February, a regional court in Feldkirch, Austria, handed the man a seven-month suspended prison sentence, a €1,200 (£1,046) fine and ordered him to pay the victims €625 (£545) each in compensation after he was found guilty of filming and taking photographs of players, including minors, in the changing room, gym and showers of Altach’s women’s team between 2018 and 2025.

The sentence provoked outrage from former Altach players and more widely in Austria. After a request from the Austrian players’ union (VdF) and the global players’ union Fifpro, the Fifa disciplinary committee extended on 4 August the man’s ban from football-related activities to a global one.

Quick Guide How do I 

The man did not request a statement of the reasons for the decision within a prescribed timeframe, so the decision has become binding and final. Federations are able to ban individuals from football related activities only in their respective countries.

Christos Papadimitriou, the women’s football coordinator at the VdF, said: “Anyone who secretly films players in the locker room crosses a clear line. The fact that the ban now applies worldwide sends an important signal: those who seriously violate players’ rights cannot escape the consequences by moving abroad.”

The Czech players’ union, CAFH, has called for a lifetime ban from all football-related activities for Petr Vlachovsky, the former coach of FC Slovacko, who was convicted of similar offences in addition to being in possession of child sexual abuse material. Vlachovsky was convicted in May 2025 and handed a suspended one-year prison sentence and five-year domestic coaching ban.

In March Fifpro said: “Because the Czech criminal process and the Czech FA’s administrative proceedings are separate and can run in parallel, the union is challenging the FA to implement a lifetime football ban for Vlachovsky and all sexual offenders. Fifpro is exploring possible legal avenues on behalf of players to achieve a global ban.”

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 10: London City Lionesses
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 4th (NB: this is not necessarily Suzanne Wrack’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th

Prospects

Trying to figure out what London City will look like this season, or where they will finish, is nigh on impossible. Eight players have come in as the owner, Michele Kang, bids to continue her drive towards the top of the Women’s Super League and there are some superstars in that group, among them the two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas.

The WSL debutants finished a respectable sixth last season, but were 22 points adrift of the top three. Evidence suggests Kang will be ruthless if the team do not meet her expectations – despite a strong start to the 2025-26 campaign, Jocelyn Prêcheur was sacked as manager shortly before Christmas and replaced by Eder Maestre.

Wholesale changes to teams hoping to break into the top three have proved costly in the past. The hope will be that the level of the players coming in will help London City develop into a side capable of securing Champions League football and challenging for the league. What is clear is that Kang’s spending and ambition is playing a big role in bringing some of the biggest players in the world to the WSL. Mapi León said of her: “Everything counts when you make this kind of a decision, and of course, she was an important part because seeing another woman doing so much to help women’s sports and women’s football grow, I think it’s impossible not to value that. I think it’s something very powerful.”

Off-field picture

London City’s accounts for 2024-25 showed an operating loss of £10.6m and the effect of their big spending before their first season in the WSL, and even bigger spending this summer, will show in future filings. The 2024-25 loss was more than 10 times their £902,000 revenue in that period. Critically, there is a need to grow the fanbase and, with no men’s club supporter pool to draw from, London City will have to be inventive.

The manager

Maestre was appointed in January having previously managed UD Tenerife in Liga F, guiding them to sixth. Maestre’s contract runs until 2028, but he cannot rest on that given Kang’s high expectations. The 42-year-old has shifted the way London City play and a host of new signings could prove fruitful in his system.

Star signing

Mary Earps, León and Kadidiatou Diani have arrived from Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and Lyonnes respectively, but it is the recruitment of Putellas that has rocked the WSL. The 32-year-old spent 14 years at Barcelona, helping them to the top of the women’s game, in the process becoming a talismanic figure. Putellas is far from past her prime and had the pick of clubs worldwide when deciding to leave Spain. Her recruitment was a statement of intent from Kang.

View image in fullscreen The 32-year-old Alexia Putellas has plenty to offer London City Lionesses. Photograph: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

Stat attack

London City made more Opta-defined defensive errors that led to goals and conceded more penalties than any other team in the WSL last season. Elene Lete saved one penalty and the players in front of the 24-year-old goalkeeper need to make her life easier.

Set for a breakthrough

Superstars have come through the door this summer, meaning Nicole Anyomi is one that has slipped under the radar and could go on to make a big impression. Anyomi is a little bit of an unknown to UK audiences having played all her club football in Germany. The forward scored 60 goals in 130 games for Frankfurt in five years. She also has four goals in 34 games for Germany.

What they say

“I’m going to bring to the project whatever the project needs from me, so I’m 100% committed. I’m hungry to win, to be better day after day, to fight with my teammates for the victory” – Putellas

Where are they playing their home games?

Hayes Lane in Bromley is far from an ideal ground for such an ambitious club given the 5,150 capacity. The medium- to long-term goal is to upsize, but space for a ground in and around London is limited. Before any move, however, London City need to increase their fanbase.

Sports.title: Fiorentina’s Serie A renaissance feels a way off after chastening centenary | Nicky Bandini
Sports.content:
Fiorentina’s 100th birthday party had been going for four days, starting with a fan procession through the historic centre of Florence on Wednesday night and extending to their home game against Frosinone on Saturday afternoon. The club was founded on 29 August 1926, but a decades-old discrepancy in the reporting of that date has led supporters to celebrate traditionally on the 26th.

This time they started a few hours earlier, gathering in their thousands beneath the marble façade of the Basilica of Santa Maria Novella on the evening of 25 August and building to a firework show beside the river Arno at midnight. The club’s president, Giuseppe Commisso, stopped by to give a speech. At least one former player, Borja Valero, was among the crowd.

In the days that followed, historic monuments across the city were lit up in purple to match Fiorentina’s home strip. They have worn that colour since 1929, having played their first three years in shirts half red and half white. A limited-edition replica of those original tops, priced at €180, sold out in less than two hours.

Fiorentina’s players would wear them against Frosinone. Before kick-off, the club hosted some of their greatest former players and coaches for a lunch at their headquarters in Viola Park. The likes of Gabriel Batistuta, Rui Costa, Adrien Mutu and Cesare Prandelli gathered to eat and then head to the stadium, where they were greeted with a party atmosphere.

Not every preparation had gone to plan. Fiorentina had intended for renovations to their Stadio Artemio Franchi to be completed in time for this occasion, but delays meant the Curva Fiesole – the stand traditionally occupied by ultras – remains closed. Still, those same groups arranged a striking choreography at the opposite end instead, recreating the original club badge against a sea of purple flags.

Spirits were high. Despite an opening 4-0 drubbing by Roma, Fiorentina’s supporters had reasons to believe their team was on a good track. They had spent more than €120m on refreshing their squad with exciting young talent, including the Ivory Coast midfielder Christ Inao Oulaï and highly-rated teenage defender Víctor Valdepeñas from Real Madrid Castilla, as well as Arthur Atta and Mateo Pellegrino, coming off breakout seasons with Udinese and Parma.

View image in fullscreen Choreography by Fiorentina fans before kick-off. Photograph: Andrea Martini/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

And that’s not to mention the players they landed on loan. Real Madrid paid €45m to sign the Argentinian winger Franco Mastantuono from River Plate last August and now the 19-year-old would be lining up in Fiorentina’s attack. Radu Dragusin and Álex Jiménez brought Premier League experience from Tottenham and Bournemouth.

The new manager, Fabio Grosso, would need time to blend this group together. But a home game against newly-promoted Frosinone seemed a perfect opportunity for new faces to establish themselves while marking the club’s centenary in style.

It did not work out that way.

Fiorentina started well enough. After a clumsy first few minutes they began to dictate, Mastantuono on the right taking turns with Albert Gudmundsson on the left at getting behind the defence. Jiménez supported ably with overlapping runs from full-back. It felt like a matter of time before they scored.

But a warning arrived in the 25th minute, when Frosinone launched a counter from a Fiorentina free-kick. They reached the penalty area with a numbers advantage, three on two, but Seydou Fini dallied and got dispossessed as he checked back.

Frosinone’s centre-forward, Antonio Raimondo, roared in frustration. A minute later, he opened the scoring. This time Giorgi Kvernadze drove to the goal-line down the left, barely keeping the ball in, before cutting it back for Raimondo to force home at the near post.

Fiorentina responded well. Atta forced a save from Lorenzo Palmisani, before Mastantuono and Valdepeñas smacked shots against the left post. There were moments of quality. Mastantuono did outrageously well to salvage a ball played behind him, controlling with one heel, then knocking the ball across his defender with the second. The stadium appealed for a penalty as he went to ground under contact from Gabriele Bracaglia, but Mastantuono bounced back to his feet and nutmegged another opponent as he shot against the far upright.

Narrow margins. Instead of pulling level, Fiorentina fell further behind in the 38th minute when Bracaglia headed home from a corner. Now the wind truly came out of their sails. Despite a series of substitutions, Grosso’s team offered no hint of a comeback. Raimondo made it 3-0 to Frosinone in the 68th minute with a glorious chest-down and outside-of-the-boot finish.

View image in fullscreen Mateo Pellegrino holds the ball after a Frosinone goal. Photograph: Claudio Giovannini/EPA

An astonishing scoreline. Frosinone only narrowly avoided relegation to Italy’s third tier in 2025, when they were set to contest a play-out with Salernitana before a points deduction for Brescia bumped them up the Serie B standings. La Gazzetta dello Sport predicted them to struggle again last season, but their manager, Massimiliano Alvini used the pink paper as motivation, showing it off to players at the start of what became an unexpected run to promotion.

There is much more to say about Frosinone, and Alvini, whose only previous experience in Serie A was a winless 18-game stretch with Cremonese four years ago. An unassuming character, who even now maintains an active LinkedIn page but who has earned his place after finding continuous work as a manager – albeit mostly in the lower divisions – for a quarter of a century.

It is hard to move past Fiorentina as the story, however, on the weekend that they marked their centenary by making their worst-ever start to a Serie A season. They have lost their first two games now by a combined seven goals. It is the first time they have begun a top-flight campaign being shut out in back-to-back defeats.

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Milan 2-0 Venezia, Sassuolo 2-1 Torino, Monza 2-3 Udinese, Fiorentina 0-3 Frosinone, Juventus 2-0 Parma, Napoli 1-2 Como, Lazio 1-0 Genoa, Cagliari 0-1 Inter Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Perhaps this will all prove an aberration. We are still a way off yet from the horrors of last season, when Fiorentina took six points from their opening 15 matches, winning none. But this was certainly not the night Giuseppe Commisso wanted. His father, Rocco, had sought to transform Fiorentina after taking the club over in 2019, investing heavily to create what has been billed as Italy’s biggest sports centre at Viola Park, with upgraded training facilities for Fiorentina’s men’s and women’s teams, as well as their academy.

Since Rocco passed away in January, Giuseppe has spoken of wanting to carry forward his father’s legacy. “Our family’s total financial commitment to Fiorentina is €1.1bn,” he said on Saturday. “This summer Fiorentina made the largest single transfer window investment in new players in the history of the club.”

View image in fullscreen The post-game show inside the Stadio Artemio Franchi. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

He was speaking from the pitch, part of a post-game show to mark the centenary. An event that could not escape the shadow of the 90 minutes that preceded it. Many fans did stay to applaud Batistuta, Rui Costa and other club legends who came out for reintroductions and reminiscences. But the current team were drowned in whistles.

“Today, on Fiorentina’s 100th anniversary, I am not declaring that we have arrived, I am declaring that we have begun again,” said Commisso, swapping between English and Italian. “From this fresh start, Fiorentina’s Renaissance will commence.”

All words that fans love to hear. And all a little harder to buy into, in the aftermath of yet another chastening setback.

Sports.title: Arsenal urged to complete late deal for Vinicius Jr alternative who rejected Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Lyon forward Malick Fofana has been offered to Arsenal, talkSPORT understands.

The Belgium international previously rejected a move to Hull City earlier in the summer.



3 Arsenal have been offered the chance to sign Lyon forward Fofana Credit: Getty

Roma and RB Leipzig have also been credited with interest in Fofana.

However, he could now complete a late switch to the Premier League champions.

The Gunners have until the window closes at 11pm on Tuesday to conclude their transfer business.

Having missed out on the signing of Vinicius Jr, adding another wide attacker remains under consideration.



Fofana's Lyon future is up in the air after the Ligue 1 side missed out on a place in the league phase of the Champions League.

They were beaten by Turkish giants Fenerbahce last week, causing them to drop into the Europa League.



The 21-year-old's current Lyon deal expires at the end of next season.

Since joining the club from Gent in 2024, he has scored 19 goals and added eight assists in 84 appearances across all competitions.



talkSPORT verdict

European football journalist Andy Brassell has tipped Fofana to be a success if he were to move to the Emirates Stadium.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT.com, he explained: "Straight off, ever since Lyon have been eliminated from the Champions League play-offs, they've had a lot of players on the block.

3 Vinicius Jr signed a new six-year deal with Real Madrid to end any hope of Arsenal landing him Credit: AFP

"They are not just willing to sell, they need to sell, and they need to make around €50million, before the window shuts.



"The quickest way of doing that, because they have at least one more definitely out already, is Malick Fofana.

"Obviously, he's been linked with a lot of different teams so far. Hull City made an approach and rejected that pretty much out of hand, slightly more politely perhaps.

"Linked to Roma for a number of weeks, seems like Leipzig might be in and there's even been talk in France that he's been offered to Arsenal.

"Now, even though he's not Vinicius Jr, clearly, I think him being offered to Arsenal is really interesting because he is a player exactly in the spot where they want a player.



"His ceiling is very, very high. He missed most of last season because of a really bad ankle injury that he received in the game against Strasbourg.

3 Fofana has been tipped to make an 'interesting' move to Arsenal before the window closes Credit: Getty

"He still had some pain when he came back, so it took a while for him to get that sorted out and since he has got that sorted out, he's been really good in the early part of this season for Lyon when he has played.

"I think he can add more goals to his game as well. He's got speed and he's really good at bringing the ball up the pitch quickly.



"I think he was clocked the season before the one he was injured in as the fastest player in Ligue 1. So, I think that's an interesting one for sure."

Arsenal have already spent over £200million on four new signings following their Premier League triumph last term.

Mikel Arteta's side ended their 22-year wait for a 14th league title victory.

They have since added Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Christos Tzolis to their ranks.



Meanwhile, Pieor Hincapie's loan from Bayer Leverkusen has been made permanent for £45million.

Several exits could still be finalised before the window closes, though, with deals involving Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus in the works.

Sports.title: Tottenham move for Iliman Ndiaye hijacked by Man City despite deal being agreed
Sports.content:
Tottenham move for Iliman Ndiaye hijacked by Man City despite deal being agreed

Manchester City have completed the signing of Iliman Ndiaye after Tottenham agreed a deal to sign him, talkSPORT understands.

Enzo Maresca's side have secured the services of the Everton forward in a £60million deal, with £5m in add-ons.



4 Ndiaye insisted on going to City once they revived their interest in him Credit: Getty

This is despite Spurs agreeing a £60m move with the Toffees, however, the player pushed for a switch to City.

Spurs' move being hijacked also appears to end any hope of striker Richarlison going back to Merseyside.

City pivoted towards Ndiaye having lost out on the signing of Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo.



City initially usurped Spurs in the race for Gakpo and were confident they would sign the Dutchman.

But talkSPORT understands Liverpool will only sanction a sale of Gakpo if they can sign another winger before Tuesday's deadline despite securing the services of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.



Tottenham instigated a deal for Ndiaye, who famously knocked them out of the FA Cup in 2023 with Championship side Sheffield United.

The Senegalese star spent two years with Everton and etched his name in the history books by scoring the final two goals at Goodison Park in 2025.



The 26-year-old appeared in both the Toffees' games this season and got an assist against Crystal Palace in their 2-0 win in their first fixture.

Across all campaigns he managed a total of 20 goal contributions and Tottenham are now set to land him as they seek to improve their forward line.

He also managed one goal and two assists at the 2026 World Cup with his nation.

4 City are set for a very busy end to the transfer window Credit: Getty



talkSPORT understands Ndiaye has turned down multiple contract offers from Everton over the past 12 months.

Richarlison looked set to go the other way, in a separate transfer and return to the club he left for £60million in 2022.

However, in a statement released on Monday, the player appeared to hit out at the club for the way they acted during the negotiations.

The Brazilian hit 53 goals in 152 appearances for The Toffees, becoming a fan favourite, before securing a move to the capital.



There, though, he spent much of his first campaign limited behind Harry Kane and beset by fitness issues.

This would be a common theme in north London, despite hitting 32 goals in all competitions while moving between centre-forward and left wing.

4 Spurs are back in the Premier League relegation zone after two games of the 2026/27 season Credit: Getty

Tottenham moved quickly in the summer transfer window after narrowly avoiding relegation.



They brought in Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100million, Mateus Fernandes from West Ham for £85m, and Jan Paul van Hecke for £52m.

This was swiftly followed by the free transfer signings of Andrew Robertson, Marcos Senesi, and Martin Dubravka.

After a long saga, Savio and Omar Marmoush then arrived from Man City last week with the former joining for £85m and the latter on loan with an obligation to buy for £60m.

4 Kevin Danso is also keen to depart the club Credit: Getty



However, they have lost their first two games of the season in a disappointing start to their new era.

A 4-0 loss to Brentford was followed by a 2-0 defeat to Newcastle.

An number of stars were left out, including Kevin Danso, Pape Matar Sarr, and Richarlison.

And De Zerbi addressed this after the Newcastle game.

"Richarlison, he's said too many times he wants to leave," the Spurs head coach said.

"Danso came to me two days ago, and he said he wants to leave.

"The other player, Sarr, is the same but he's suffered a small injury. But, he's almost ready to train."



He added: "I love these players, and they are great guys," the Italian explained. "I have very good relationships.

"But, if they want to leave, they have to bring the economic solution to the club and they can go, and we'll find other players."

Sports.title: Tottenham to win race against four Premier League clubs over Mykhailo Mudryk loan in biggest shock of transfer window
Sports.content:
Tottenham to win race against four Premier League clubs over Mykhailo Mudryk loan in biggest shock of transfer window

Tottenham have agreed a deal with Chelsea over the loan signing of Mykhailo Mudryk, talkSPORT understands.

Spurs are trying to strengthen the wide attacking areas and have seen a few deals fall through, sparking a late shock move for Ukrainian winger Mudryk.



6 Mudryk is free to play football once again after his doping ban was lifted Credit: Getty

The 25-year-old is back from his doping ban after all charges were dropped against him earlier this summer.

However, he is yet to play a single minute of first-team football for the Blues since returning.

Xabi Alonso hasn't involved him in the Premier League or Carabao Cup so far, and Spurs are looking to reunite him with Roberto De Zerbi.



The duo worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk with Spurs also agreeing a deal with Chelsea to sign Tosin Adarabioyo on a permanent basis.

Mudryk has been the subject of interest from Sunderland, Leeds United and Coventry City.



Scrambling

It has been a dramatic 24 hours in the transfer market for Tottenham.

Spurs agreed a deal with Everton to sign Iliman Ndiaye with Richarlison heading back to the Toffees in a separate deal.

But in a shock twist, Manchester City came back in for Ndiaye to wrap up a move due to Liverpool calling off a deal for Cody Gakpo to go to Manchester City.



Spurs had been keen on the Dutchman too but he favoured a move to the Etihad Stadium in the event of him leaving Liverpool.

However, the Reds haven't been able to find a replacement, with moves for Yankuba Minteh and Ismaila Sarr stalling.

6 Tosin is set to leave Chelsea after two years at the club Credit: Getty

6 Ndiaye had looked to be heading to Tottenham, but Man City are back in Credit: Getty



And this means City turned attentions to Ndiaye and are understood to have completed the signing of him.

Enzo Maresca has been interested in the Senegalese international for some time, but they cooled their interest to focus on Gakpo.

But with Gakpo off the table, City went back in for Ndiaye with Jack Grealish potentially going the other way.

talkSPORT understands that Grealish would prefer a move to Everton over any other club this summer as well.



6 Richarlison has also thrown some chaos in the air with his update on his future

Further complicating Spurs' deal for Ndiaye to join Spurs is Richarlison.

What has Richarlison done?

The Brazilian international was set to return to Everton, but in a bombshell series of Instagram stories, he has appeared to suggest that he is staying put.

This comes despite him asking Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi to leave.

But he hit out at Spurs and suggested that he was being forced to leave not on his own terms despite wanting to return the Toffees.



The stories were in Portuguese, but they have been translated as follows.

"After everything I've been through in recent years, I decided that they would never again decide my future for me," he wrote.

"I've been through a lot of bad things these days and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people.

"Pressure, threats, retaliations, none of this scares me. I've been through worse things… believe me!



"I have always made it clear, at every opportunity, that an exit of mine to another place would also have to be good for the club.

"If it wasn't, I would never accept… as I didn't accept when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.

"I stayed and gave my life. So, I hope you treat my situation with the same respect that I always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't want to decide for me.

"If they enter into an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I go back to my favourite team.



"My intention was to return to the place where I was very happy. But the negotiations were the way people wanted and it won't be like this anymore.

"Despite this riot, I have a contract with Spurs and I will be at the club's disposal."

6 Richarlison is going nowhere, or so it seems Credit: Getty

Sports.title: Richarlison could stay at Tottenham in shock U-turn as he furiously hits out in cryptic statement
Sports.content:
Richarlison could stay at Tottenham in shock U-turn as he furiously hits out in cryptic statement

Richarlison has suggested he will not be re-joining Everton from Tottenham Hotspur.

The striker had appeared set for a return to the Toffees ahead of the Premier League transfer deadline.



3 Richarlison has announced he will not be leaving Spurs to re-join Everton Credit: Getty

Clubs have until 11pm on Tuesday to conclude their summer business.

A deal between Everton and Spurs for Richarlison had been agreed alongside a separate transfer involving Iliman Ndiaye.

It came after Roberto De Zerbi had revealed the forward had asked to leave the club.

Whilst Manchester City could still move for Ndiaye, Richarlison suggested he won't be on the move.



Richarlison statement

In a message posted on his Instagram story, the player appeared to hit out at Spurs for the way they've acted during the negotiations.

His message suggests that while he was open to going back to Merseyside, Richarlison now may want to honour his Spurs contract, which expires next summer.



He wrote: "After everything I've been through in recent years, I decided that they would never again decide my future for me.

"I've been through a lot of bad things these days and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people.



"Pressure, threats, retaliations, none of this scares me. I've been through worse things… believe me!

"I have always made it clear, at every opportunity, that an exit of mine to another place would also have to be good for the club.

3 Richarlison released a furious statement on social media to confirm his future Credit: Getty

"If it wasn't, I would never accept… as I didn't accept when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.



"I stayed and gave my life. So, I hope you treat my situation with the same respect that I always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't want to decide for me.

"If they enter into an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I go back to my favourite team.

"My intention was to return to the place where I was very happy. But the negotiations were the way people wanted and it won't be like this anymore.

"Despite this riot, I have a contract with Spurs and I will be at the club's disposal."



Richarlison previously spent four years at Everton after signing from Watford in 2018.

3 The Toffees had agreed a deal with Spurs to bring Richarlison back to the club Credit: Getty

During that time, he scored 53 goals in 152 appearances across all competitions.

Having moved to Spurs in 2022, the Brazil international was part of the side which won the Europa League last year.



The triumph ended the club's 17-year trophy drought with victory in the final over Manchester United.

The 29-year-old was not included in the matchday squad for Saturday's defeat to Newcastle United.

He started in a defeat against Brentford the previous week.

Sports.title: EFL forced to reschedule three matches as they launch scathing attack on UEFA over fixture chaos
Sports.content:
EFL forced to reschedule three matches as they launch scathing attack on UEFA over fixture chaos

The EFL has been forced into a fixture shake-up following confirmation of Liverpool's Champions League schedule.

A total of three matches have been moved in order to accommodate the Reds' European commitments.



3 The EFL have been forced to move two Carabao Cup ties due to UEFA's scheduling Credit: Getty

It follows the draw for the third round of this season's Carabao Cup.

Everton had been due to host Wolves on Wednesday, September 9.

However, UEFA have scheduled Liverpool's league phase opener against Atletico Madrid at Anfield for the same night.

Rules currently prevent both Merseyside clubs from playing at home on the same night.

As a result, the Toffees will now meet Wolves on Wednesday, September 16.



Meanwhile, Liverpool's own third round tie, a home clash with Tottenham Hotspur will be played the day before at 8pm.

A third fixture has also been moved in order to accommodate the Carabao Cup matches.



Wolves had previously been set to host Portsmouth in the Championship at Molineux on September 9.

The fixture was pushed back to September 16 after their trip to Everton was given a date.



That Championship match will now be played at 7:45pm on Tuesday, October 20.

3 Wolves' Carabao Cup tie away to Everton has been rescheduled to September 16 Credit: Getty

EFL statement

In a statement confirming the news, the EFL said: "The EFL has been left with no option than to rearrange a number of its fixtures following the announcement of fixture details for the league phase of the UEFA Champions League.

"On 28 August, we confirmed that the Carabao Cup Round Three tie between Everton and Wolves had been scheduled for Wednesday 9 September.



"This was confirmed with local stakeholders as per usual practice ahead of announcement.

"On Saturday, UEFA announced that it had scheduled Liverpool v Atletico Madrid for the same date, despite it being clear that Everton and Liverpool cannot play home fixtures on the same evening.

"The EFL met with UEFA officials on Monday morning to explore available options, however in those discussions it was made clear that they were unwilling to consider rescheduling the Liverpool v Atletico Madrid fixture, and avoiding the consequences for other fixtures as a result."

The EFL added: "Over recent seasons the League has made a number of changes to accommodate the expansion of UEFA club competitions – a decision which was made without adequate consultation with domestic leagues.



3 Liverpool's home match against Atletico Madrid has caused the EFL a fixture headache Credit: getty

"These changes have included splitting Carabao Cup Round Three ties across two weeks, and implementing draw conditions for Round Three which prevent scheduling conflicts for clubs playing in the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League.

"This makes UEFA’s unwillingness to cooperate all the more frustrating, not least for the supporters of the five clubs that will now be inconvenienced as a result."

A separate statement from Portsmouth explained: "The knock-on effect of this is that disappointingly, our visit to Molineux has been postponed for a second time and will now take place on Tuesday, October 20 (7.45pm kick-off).



"Due to the extremely late notice of these changes, Wolves are unable to host the game on the original date of September 9.

"Portsmouth Football Club are extremely frustrated that our fans, many of whom will have twice made arrangements for this game, are adversely affected."

Pompey had only announced the previous date change for their trip to Wolves on Friday.

Sports.title: Cody Gakpo transfer decision made as Man City submit £80m bid to Liverpool
Sports.content:
Liverpool have rejected an £80million bid for Cody Gakpo from Manchester City, talkSPORT understands.

The forward is now set to remain at Anfield beyond Tuesday's 11pm transfer deadline.



3 Liverpool have rejected an £80million bid for Gakpo from City Credit: Getty

It is the Reds' intention to keep hold of Gakpo, with an exit never guaranteed to be sanctioned despite the player being open to a move.

A deadline day departure is unlikely due to the lack of time left for Liverpool to sign a replacement.

Their need to bring in a successor is seen as a key stumbling block as opposed to the financials of a potential deal.



As for City, they intend to complete the signing of Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

A move for Iliman Ndiaye could also be pursued despite a deal being agreed between Tottenham Hotspur and Everton for the playmaker.



Gakpo's Liverpool future

Gakpo started, and got an assist, in Liverpool's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

However, with Bradley Barcola coming into the club there has been speculation over his future.



Tottenham have been the club showing the most interest in Gakpo this summer.

But now City have ramped up their pursuit of the Dutch international in recent days.

Despite formal talks with Liverpool over a deal, though, their offer has been knocked back.

3 Iraola could have a busy last few days of the window Credit: Getty



talkSPORT verdict

Speaking on Saturday, talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs said: “Manchester City in the last few days have gone really big on Cody Gakpo. It's taken the player a little bit by surprise because for much of the summer, it was Tottenham and Cody Gakpo. He’d spoken to Roberto De Zerbi.

“But our information is that Cody Gakpo favours Manchester City.

“As a consequence, this is expected to develop. I actually think that Tottenham now realise they can't do that deal. Do they turn to Iliman Ndiaye as a result?

“Bradley Barcola comes in, as we exclusively revealed this morning, for £106million with £17million in add-ons.

“It may come down to the player realising even if they don't add now another attacker, Victor Munoz has come in and Rio Ngumoha needs a pathway.



"Gakpo maybe in previous seasons could have looked out wide, looked in the centre. But now up front, it's Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitike. Behind them, it's Florian Wirtz.

3 Gakpo is a Premier League winner with Liverpool Credit: AFP

“So I think he seems to believe that even if it's not now, it might be the beginning of the end.

“This was kind of what Luis Diaz thought when Liverpool wanted to keep the player, but eventually they sold him to Bayern Munich.



“Cody Gakpo has got a big decision to make. From Liverpool's perspective, if they were to sell, they know they're bringing in more money.

“It might mean that they can overpay for an Ismaïla Sarr or a Yankuba Minteh. Then two attackers will come in as well.”

The 27-year-old signed for Liverpool from PSV in 2023 for around £44m.

He signed a new long-term contract with the club last summer.

Gakpo also has 51 goals in 182 games in all competitions for the club.



More Liverpool signings?

Asked by talkSPORT's Sam Matterface after his side's 2-2 home draw with Nottingham Forest whether he'd be happy with his squad should the Barcola deal go through, Iraola said: "I think now we need to be patient. We don't know what's going to happen.

"There are still some days [left] in the market and obviously there are going to be movements. We will need to analyse when this happens.

"I'm looking forward to being in the second half of September and knowing what we have, and then making definitive plans with this.

"But the competition works like this – the rules are the same for everyone.



"It's uncomfortable in terms of uncertainty until the market closes, but now it's just a matter of a couple of days, so we will wait."

Sports.title: When is transfer deadline day? Premier League summer window info amid £2billion spending spree
Sports.content:
Deadline day for the 2026 summer transfer window is nearly here, with big-money business being completed left, right and centre.

Top-flight clubs have already spent well over £2billion this summer, with still plenty of time to splash more cash.



2 Bradley Barcola's switch to join Liverpool has been the biggest transfer of the summer Credit: Getty

There have been multiple record-breaking £100million-plus transfers made in the Premier League despite it being a World Cup summer.

Elliot Anderson has joined Manchester City, Sandro Tonali has signed for Tottenham and Morgan Rogers is now a Chelsea player.

But the biggest deal is Bradley Barcola's potential £123million switch to Liverpool from Paris Saint-Germain.



However, time will feel like it's quickly running out for all clubs to get their deals done as the deadline gets closer...

When does the transfer window shut?

The transfer deadline in England is set for Tuesday, September 1.

For the last two windows, the closing time was set for 7pm, but the time will now return to its original later deadline.



It means the summer window closes at 11pm on September 1.

Clubs can submit deal sheets before the deadline to give themselves a two-hour grace period to complete transfers.

This deadline is in place for the Premier League and EFL.

In the WSL, the window closes at 11pm on Thursday, September 3.

And that's the same day as the Scottish Premiership, but in Scotland, the deadline is going to be set for 5pm rather than 11pm.



2 England star Anderson has joined Man City for a record-breaking fee Credit: Getty

When is the deadline across Europe?

For LaLiga clubs, their summer window shuts at a similar time to in England, with the deadline set for September 1 at 10:59pm.

In Italy and Serie A, clubs have until 8pm on the same day.

As for the Bundesliga, their deadline is Monday, August 31 at 7pm.

When does the winter transfer window open?

Once the summer deadline shuts, clubs will not be able to do any more business until the winter window opens.

In England, transfers will be possible again from January 1, 2027.

The window will run for a month, closing again on February 1 at 11pm.

Meanwhile, in the WSL, the winter window will open on January 4 and close exactly a month later on February 4.



And in Scotland, their window will open on January 5, closing at 5pm on February 4.

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott gets career lifeline from European club once managed by his namesake
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott gets career lifeline from European club once managed by his namesake

Harvey Elliott is set to complete a loan move to Valencia this season, talkSPOT understands.

Valencia are understood to have reached a verbal agreement with Liverpool to allow Elliott to join the LaLiga club on a temporary switch.

3 Elliott was part of the Aston Villa squad that won the Europa League, but due to a clause in his contract, he barely played Credit: Getty

Elliott is set to undergo his Valencia medical with the Spanish club set to cover the majority of his salary.

Three other clubs are tried to sign Elliott before the end of the transfer window.

The former England Under-21 international isn't part of Andoni Iraola's plans, having been left out of the squad for Liverpool's opening two Premier League games this season.

Harvey Elliott transfer to Valencia

Elliott become just the second English player to represent the LaLiga side - although they were once managed by former Tottenham player Jimmy Elliott in the 1920s.

However, the only other English player to actually play a competitive game for the club is Max Aarons.

The ex-England U21 full-back joined Valencia on loan from Bournemouth in January 2025.

It wasn't the most successful loan spell, given he made just five appearances, but Elliott could follow in his footsteps.

Last year, Elliott joined Aston Villa on loan near the end of the transfer window.

The deal was a loan with an obligation to buy for £35million.

This would have been triggered if Elliott had appeared a certain number of times.

3 Elliott was heavily involved in pre-season, but he has played no part in the competitive matches for Liverpool this season Credit: Getty

However, Unai Emery revealed very early on that Elliott wouldn't be playing that much because of the clause.

Villa decided they didn't want to sign Elliott at all, so he spent the majority of last year on the bench.

Across all competitions, he played just ten games for Villa.

3 Elliott is looking to revive his career, and he is still very young Credit: Getty

Iraola not convinced

When asked about why Elliott played no part against Newcastle, Liverpool head coach Iraola had a pretty brutal response.

In his post-match interview, he said: “Harvey is trying and improving every week, but I still prefer other options, about the balance on the bench.

“That’s why James McConnell was in the squad, but it’s now another new week and new chances for everyone. They have to keep that mentality!”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi retires from Argentina duty: 39-year-old bows out after defeat in World Cup final by Spain - just a few weeks after his father passed away
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football following Argentina's defeat in the World Cup final to Spain last month.

The 39-year-old revealed on Monday afternoon that he made the decision to retire two days after the 1-0 defeat in the final on July 19, citing it was 'the right time'.

Messi then added in a note at the bottom of a statement that the death of his father Jorge at the start of the month made him 'even more convinced than before' about his decision.

His statement on Instagram read: 'After all this time that has passed since the final, and after much thought, I want to announce to everyone that I am retiring from the National Team…

'It was a decision that hurt, and still hurts, to my core, but I understand that it's the right time. I swear that I always gave my all, not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that too. I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football.'

Messi made his debut for Argentina in 2005 as an 18-year-old, going on to earn over 200 caps for his country, and captained the nation to their third World Cup triumph in 2022.

Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from Argentina duty after 21 years in the team

Messi played 207 times for Argentina and guided them to a World Cup triumph in 2022

Messi stated that the recent passing of his father Jorge made him 'more convinced' to retire

The attacker netted 125 goals in the famous blue and white, eight of which came during the World Cup in the US, Mexico and Canada, while he also won two Copa America titles.

But after 21 years of playing international football, Messi stated 'I have nothing more to give' and that he believes there are plenty of 'great young players' ready in line to replace him.

He continued: 'Thank you for all the love and support over these 20 years. I'm going to miss hearing you all from the inside so much. Now I'm going to be just one of you, cheering and supporting you from the sidelines (in good times and bad, even more so).

'Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this beautiful but difficult journey. Thank you to each and every one of the coaches, teammates, and managers I had the privilege of working with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments.

'I leave with the peace and pride of having given you, along with my teammates, dreamlike moments. It was incredible to have experienced it with you all. I love you!

'Thank you, God, for making me Argentinian. Go Argentina!'

The footballing world has paid tribute to Messi, whom many consider the greatest footballer of his generation – if not every – with many of the Argentina squad writing messages of thanks on social media.

Argentina's Rodrigo De Paul, considered one of Messi's closest team-mates, wrote a heartfelt message for the legendary attacker on his Instagram story.

It read: 'Your unconditional love for our country, your internal battles to never give up, your strength to always endure injustice, your leadership and human qualities with every player who entered the training grounds to make them feel welcome, the thoughtful gestures towards every member of our national team staff...

'Simply thank you, the greatest of all time, thank you for making us so incredibly happy, you can't imagine how many smiles you brought to our faces. You are eternal.'

Angel Di Maria, Cristian Romero and many others also relayed their love for their captain on social media.

Another team-mate of Messi's, Leandro Paredes, who is currently serving a ten-match ban from international football for his antics following the World Cup final, dubbed the former Barcelona star 'the greatest of all' in his tribute.

Messi started his career on the international stage in 2005 when he was just 18 years old

Messi also guided Argentina to two Copa America triumphs during his time as captain

'Thank you for absolutely everything,' he wrote. 'You are and always will be the greatest of all. We love you, captain.'

Messi has previously hinted that he was considering retirement from football following the devastating death of his father, Jorge, who was an integral figure in the career of his legendary son.

Jorge passed away on August 7 following a battle with illness that overshadowed the Argentina captain's mesmerising World Cup campaign in the United States.

Lionel, who broke down in tears following Argentina's group-stage win over Algeria while Jorge's health was deteriorating, shared a heartbreaking letter to his father on Instagram at the time – in which he cast doubt on his playing future.

'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. It hasn't sunk in yet, or rather, I don't want to accept it. It's very difficult for me to imagine never seeing you again, never talking to you again. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much to enjoy together,' he wrote.

'I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on. I only played football and now I have serious doubts that I'll continue doing that for much longer. You were by my side from the beginning, it was so close to the end. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together?'

Messi revealed that his father was the driving force behind his decision to play at this summer's World Cup, but he will not attempt to play at a record seventh in four years at the age of 43.

The death of Messi's father saw an outpouring of emotional tributes from the football world, including from Messi's first team Newell's Old Boys, Barcelona and his great rival Cristiano Ronaldo.

Ronaldo, whose own father, Jose Dinis Aveiro, passed away in 2005, passed on 'much strength' to Messi in these 'tough times'.

Messi steps away from international football as one of the most successful ever to play the sport. In his two decades playing for Argentina, he won five titles with the national team, including the magical World Cup triumph in Qatar.

Messi netted 125 goals for his country while he also notched up 60 assists in blue and white

The Argentinian also suffered World Cup heartbreak back in 2014 after a final loss to Germany

MESSI'S STATEMENT IN FULL

'After all this time that has passed since the final, and after much thought, I want to announce to everyone that I am retiring from the National Team… 'It was a decision that hurt, and still hurts, to my core, but I understand that it's the right time. I swear that I always gave my all, not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that too. I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football. 'There's not much time left, and chapters are closing, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, loved, and will always love being on the National Team. I've given everything I have; I have nothing more to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up behind me who deserve to be there. 'Thank you for all the love and support over these 20 years. I'm going to miss hearing you all from the inside so much. Now I'm going to be just one of you, cheering and supporting you from the sidelines (in good times and bad, even more so). 'Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this beautiful but difficult journey. Thank you to each and every one of the coaches, teammates, and managers I had the privilege of working with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments. 'I leave with the peace and pride of having given you, along with my teammates, dreamlike moments. It was incredible to have experienced it with you all. I love you! 'Thank you, God, for making me Argentinian. 'Go Argentina! '*I wrote these words on July 21st, two days after the final. Today, after what happened to my dad, I'm even more convinced than before.'

The forward netted seven of his 21 goals in the tournament en route to Argentina lifting the trophy, including a brace against France in the final at the Lusail Stadium.

The defeat to Spain this summer was Messi's second World Cup final heartbreak, after the loss to Germany in 2014.

It is believed that Messi will continue to play at club level for Inter Miami in the MLS, with his contract set to expire in 2028.

The forward once again showed that he is still a class apart despite everything he has gone through this past month, netting four goals in Miami's 7-1 thumping of CF Montreal in the league.

Messi's historic career at club level dates back to 2000, when he moved to Spain to join Barcelona's famed La Masia academy from his childhood club, Newell's Old Boys, in Argentina.

He became one of the greatest to play the sport in an incredible 21 years in Barcelona, before stunning the world with a move to Paris Saint-Germain – orchestrated by Jorge – in 2021.

He moved to Inter Miami in 2023, where it seems he will stay for a further two years as he enters his 40s.
