Sports.title: What Sydney Swans stripper believes caused her 'medical episode' that saw hotel party spill into chaos - and how an AFL star came to her aid as the 'Pullman Five' panicked
Sports.content:
More details are emerging about the wild stripper party that ended with five Sydney Swans players being stood down and barred from the Brownlow - including fresh claims regarding the 'medical episode' allegedly suffered by one of the dancers.

A source with knowledge of the events alleges another Swans player, not believed to be one of the so-called 'Pullman Five', came to the woman's aid after she fled into the hotel hallway in the early hours of August 17, a detail not previously reported.

The Daily Mail revealed last week how the night after Sydney's win over Essendon at the MCG descended into chaos when a small group of players hired female entertainers from the 'Party Girls Melbourne' agency to celebrate.

As dawn broke, teammates, coaches and club officials began gathering in the Pullman East Melbourne foyer in official club attire ahead of the team's flight home. Families, couples and business travellers were also checking out of the hotel.

Upstairs, however, the situation on the eighth floor was beginning to unravel.

Unbeknownst to club officials, one of the three women paid to perform private lap dances for the players had become unwell and was suffering from what she believes was carbon dioxide poisoning.

It has been confirmed that Swansmen Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Riley Bice were at the party. They were stood down and banned from the Brownlow Medal

The so-called 'Pullman Five' allegedly panicked as one of the exotic dancers, who believed that she was suffering from carbon dioxide poisoning due to the stuffy hotel room, dashed into the hallway topless. (Isaac Heeney is pictured with his fiancée Steffie Waters)

The Daily Mail previously revealed how the night after Sydney's win over Essendon at the MCG descended into chaos when a small group of players hired female entertainers to attend the Pullman East Melbourne hotel (pictured)

In the hours beforehand, the women had been negotiating fees for dances and bottom slaps with a group they believed were tradesmen after allegedly being told the men were 'carpenters'.

Eventually, the trio would make their way downstairs, where the sea of red jackets and AFL logos would confirm their clients weren't chippies but well-paid footballers.

This discovery, coupled with the dancer's medical episode, sparked tensions in the lobby as the women made a beeline for coach Dean Cox to complain.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon were subsequently stood down for the remainder of the AFL season.

The Mail can now reveal details of how the women came to arrive at the hotel in the middle of the night, after one of the five men made a booking with the agency.

Remarkably, we have been told that one of the three women wasn't actually a stripper by trade, and was simply on a night out with her friend, who received the job offer.

'The job was listed in a WhatsApp group chat [of adult entertainers] and requested two girls at the hotel,' a source with knowledge of the matter told the Mail.

'One of the dancers accepted it and told the agent that she would take her mate [who wasn't a stripper] along because she wanted to get into the industry anyway.

'She felt sick during the party and she actually thinks it was carbon dioxide poisoning because there were so many people crammed into one room and there wasn't enough fresh air,' claimed the insider. (Pictured: A generic photo of a hotel room at the Pullman East Melbourne)

According to the insider, an argument broke out after the men asked the dancer to step back inside and put some clothes on. She was later found by another player sitting by the lifts in the hallway. (Pictured: A generic photo of a corridor at the Pullman East Melbourne hotel)

The Mail has been told that one of the three women wasn't actually a stripper, and was simply on a night out with her friend, who received the job offer via the Party Girls Melbourne agency. (Pictured: the Party Girls website which uses stock imagery, not photos of the actual strippers)

'The agent disagreed and said she had already booked the second girl, who was one of her regulars, but she ended up just bringing her mate anyway.'

This meant that three women eventually arrived at the hotel rather than the two requested by the agency.

As the Mail previously reported, the night's entertainment started pleasantly enough.

'Everyone was just chatting to start with and they [the women] asked what they did for work because there were so many of them staying at the same hotel and nine of them crammed into one room [at one stage].'

The other four men mentioned by the source have yet to be identified, but there is no suggestion of any wrongdoing by them.

Indeed, a club spokesman confirmed last week: 'The Sydney Swans can confirm that all investigations carried out by the club have consistently indicated that the only representatives of the club in the room central to the police investigation were the five players who have been stood down.'

The source went on to claim: 'They [the players] said they were carpenters and working in the area.'

Because of their trade, 'the girls agreed to charge $200 per girl for a lap dance [performance] across all the guys,' they added.

'The girls performed to one song each and moved between the guys.'

It was shortly after the performers had finished their lap dance routine moving between the men that one of the women began feeling unwell. (Stock image posed by model)

'All five players were high profile and some were in relationships,' said the source. 'They really didn't want to be seen drinking in hotel rooms with strippers during footy season because they had a lot to lose.' (Pictured: Isaac Heeney with his fiancée Steffie Waters)

The source said this kind of performance would usually cost between $250 and $300, on top of the agency's standard booking fee.

'But because it was late and they didn't think [the men] earned much, they did them a deal and they just wanted to get the job done and leave,' the insider added.

The men paid on the spot and some physical contact was allowed while the dance was taking place, the source claimed.

According to the source, some of the men were 'wasted', swaying and unsteady on their feet, as the girls shimmied through their routines.

At one stage, a woman said that if the players wanted to touch the dancers, they would have to pay more.

'One guy agreed to pay an extra $50 to slap her a**e three times,' said the source.

It was shortly after the performers had finished their lap dance routine moving between the men that one of the women began feeling unwell.

While the father of the woman in question has previously indicated she suffered from an asthma attack, the Mail's source now claims something else entirely.

'She felt sick during the party and she actually thinks it was carbon dioxide poisoning because there were so many people crammed into one room and there wasn't enough fresh air,' claimed the insider.

While it is theoretically possible to suffer ill effects from elevated carbon dioxide levels in a crowded, poorly ventilated room, serious cases are considered rare and are more commonly associated with confined spaces where fresh air is limited.

Regardless of what caused her distress, the situation escalated when the woman rushed to the door, flung it open and leaned topless into the corridor in search of fresh air. The mood inside the room changed instantly, claimed the source.

'All five players were high profile and some were in relationships,' they said.

'They really didn't want to be seen drinking in hotel rooms with strippers during footy season because they had a lot to lose.'

According to the insider, an argument broke out after the men asked the dancer to step back inside and put some clothes on. She then wrapped herself in a hotel dressing gown and left the room, but ended up sitting on the floor by the lifts.

It was at this point that another Swans player, who the source indicated may not have been one of the five players named in connection with the hotel incident, was walking down the hallway and saw the woman in distress.

'He found her and asked if she was OK,' said the source.

This viral WhatsApp message purports to show the fraught scene in the Pullman East hotel foyer on the morning of Monday, August 17

The women confronted one of the club bosses in the lobby. Previous reports indicate that the representative they spoke to was coach Dean Cox, who is not accused of any wrongdoing

'He was pretty shocked when she told him she had been booked by some guys at a party, and he helped her up and walked her back to the room where the others were.'

The three women then made their way downstairs, where the situation began to attract even more attention.

In the lobby, the woman suffering the suspected medical episode said that she felt dizzy and couldn't breathe. She tried using an asthma pump, although it is not known if it was hers or one supplied by another person.

Her presence soon became noticeable as she waved her arms around and walked in and out of the hotel in search of fresh air, the source alleged.

Meanwhile, her friend went back upstairs to collect their belongings left behind at the party.

As more Swans players and staff began gathering in the lobby, the woman's friend returned from the eighth floor and it was only then that she realised why the 'Pullman Five' had been so desperate to keep the situation private: they were AFL players.

It was at this point that the women confronted one of the club bosses. Previous reports indicate that the representative they spoke to was coach Cox, who is not accused of any wrongdoing.

In a remarkable turn of events, a woman at the hotel who was unaware of the drama unfolding around her allegedly approached star player Heeney, whose hood was pulled up, and politely asked him to pose for a photo with her child.

Heeney obliged, claimed the source, but asked her not to use the camera flash.

Unbeknownst to the mother, the photo also captured one of the women in the background during the heated exchange with a club official.

As the bizarre scene continued to unravel, more guests began to take notice of what was going on. At least one person present in the lobby took a photo, which was later widely circulated on WhatsApp.

'I'm at the Pullman in Melbourne and three girls [are] getting kicked out... And one of them said to the guy, "We have everything recorded,"' read the viral message.

Heeney's fiancée Steffie Waters was seen looking stressed while speaking on the phone in Noosa on August 21. She was later pictured in happier spirits during a trip to the beach

The women made calls to their agent as well as police and, according to the source, were eventually asked to leave the hotel.

The dramatic scenes at the hotel were followed by serious allegations the next day.

Two women made police complaints alleging sexual assault. Later in the week, the third woman also made a police report with similar claims.

The Daily Mail does not suggest any of the named Swans players are under police investigation or involved in any wrongdoing alleged by the women.

No charges have been laid.

The Mail also understands that all three women, who have separately engaged civil lawyers, were told by police they were not allowed to have any contact with one another while investigations were ongoing.

When contacted for comment on Monday, Victoria Police said there was no update.

Sports.title: Richarlison insists he won't allow 'other people' to decide his future as he posts angry statement on social media amid Everton and Tottenham transfer saga
Sports.content:
Richarlison insists he won't allow 'other people' to decide his future as he posts angry statement on social media amid Everton and Tottenham transfer saga

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tottenham striker Richarlison has cast doubt on a potential move to Everton after posting a cryptic message on social media insisting he will not let anyone else decide his future.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi told the media after Saturday's defeat to Newcastle that Richarlison, 29, had told him that he wanted to leave the club.

Daily Mail Sport then reported on Sunday that Everton had accepted a £60m offer from Tottenham for Iliman Ndiaye, with Richarlison set to go the other way for a fee of £35m plus add-ons.

This certainly seemed to be the solution Richarlison favoured, with the Brazilian referring to it on Instagram as the 'club of my heart', while Everton have now agreed a £65m deal with Man City for Ndiaye.

With just over 24 hours to go until the transfer deadline, Richarlison's post, written in Portuguese, said: 'After everything I've been through in the last few years, I've decided that no one will ever again decide my future for me.

I've been through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation - none of that scares me. I've been through worse... believe me!

Richarlison has cast doubt on a return to Everton, posting: 'After everything I've been through in the last few years, I've decided that no one will ever again decide my future for me'

RIcharlison had earlier posted this picture on Instagram which read: 'I am the villain of many poorly told stories'

'I have always made it clear, on every occasion, that any move to another club would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn't, I would never accept it... just as I didn't accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me. I stayed and gave my all.

'So I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't try to decide for me.

'If they reach an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I will return to my club of heart. My intention was indeed to return to the place where I was very happy.

'Only that the negotiations were the way people wanted and it will not be that way anymore. Despite this turmoil I have a contract with Spurs and I will be at the club's disposal.'

On Saturday, De Zerbi revealed that Richarlison was one of a trio of players who had communicated that they wanted to leave the club.

De Zerbi, who left Richarlison out of his matchday squad for the 2-0 defeat to Newcastle, said: 'Richarlison, he said too many times that he wanted to leave. Danso came to me two days ago and said he wanted to leave. Sarr the same.

'I love these players and these are great guys. I have very good relationships. But if they want to leave they have to bring the economic solution to the club and they can go, and we’ll find other players.'

On Sunday Richarlison then went on to share a photograph of a wall with red and black text on it reading, in translation: 'I am the villain of many poorly told stories.'

Richarlison has scored 32 goals in 134 matches for Tottenham since signing from Everton in a £60m deal in 2022.

The Brazilian previously scored 53 goals in 152 games for the Toffees.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson enters Old Trafford with his lower left leg in a protective boot - as legendary ex-Manchester United manager arrives for their Premier League clash against Ipswich Town
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson is at Old Trafford to give his support to his beloved Manchester United, but is doing so injured.

The iconic former Red Devils boss arrived at the Theatre of Dreams with his lower left leg in a protective boot on Sunday ahead of their first home Premier League match of the season against Ipswich Town.

Ferguson, 84, was assisted out of the car as he also walked with a stick to aid his balance.

As Ferguson got out of the car a loud cheer greeted him from United supporters.

The Scot won a stunning 38 trophies during his 26 years at the helm - including 13 Premier League titles and two Champions Leagues.

Sir Alex Ferguson was seen arriving at Old Trafford with his lower left leg in a protective boot

Ferguson was pictured watching Manchester United playing against Ipswich

He and the majority inside Old Trafford were hoping Michael Carrick's side could give them something to smile about after losing their Premier League opener at new boys Hull City on August 22.

And they duly did with a thumping 5-2 victory over Ipswich, although they were made to sweat initially.

Ipswich took the lead through a Leif Davis goal on 29 minutes. However, Bruno Fernandes equalised just before half-time and the Red Devils were reinvigorated after the break.

A Jacob Greaves own goal gave the hosts the lead on 56 minutes before Fernandes made it 3-1 five minutes later from the penalty spot after Matheus Cunha was fouled.

Fernandes then completed his hat-trick on 68 minutes before he set up Bryan Mbeumo to score with eight minutes remaining.

United pushed for a sixth goal but it was Ipswich who got a stoppage-time consolation when Lisandro Martinez was punished for an error as Chuba Akpom scored.

Sports.title: Man United's left-back dilemma: Why they wanted to wait a year before revamping defence, the three targets on radar in last-minute push to challenge Luke Shaw and the steep asking price that's put Lewis Hall out of reach... for now
Sports.content:
Carlos Baleba was paraded on the pitch before kick-off on Sunday and Old Trafford got its first glimpse of Manchester United’s other two big summer signings, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, in action against Ipswich.

Aside from bringing in new back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow as a free agent, midfield has been the priority project for United in this transfer window, a year after they reloaded the attack with Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha. More than £360million spent on improving two areas of the team.

The plan, it’s understood, was to leave the defence until next summer when Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez will be out of contract. Decisions will have to be made about those players – United have the option to keep Maguire and Martinez for an additional 12 months – and some of the club’s other defenders.

However, after the 5-2 win over Ipswich was dominated by Bruno Fernandes’ hat-trick, Marcus Rashford’s Old Trafford return and Kobbie Mainoo sparkling in the new midfield order, there was no ignoring the nagging concern that United cannot afford to wait so long to strengthen at the back – and, above all, at left back.

Shaw has experienced his fair share of ups and downs over a 12-year career at Old Trafford that makes him United’s longest-serving player by some distance. Still only 31, he exceeded all expectations last season by starting every Premier League game for United.

But after a summer in which he was left out of England’s World Cup squad, Shaw has had a bumpy start to the new campaign. On Sunday, he was left trailing in Abdul Fatawu’s wake as the Ipswich winger set up the opening goal for Leif Davis.

Luke Shaw was left trailing in Abdul Fatawu’s wake as the Ipswich winger set up the opening goal for Leif Davis on Sunday

Manchester United's initial plan was to revamp their defence next summer, when Harry Maguire (centre) and Lisandro Martinez (right) will be out of contract

After losing their first game of the season at Hull, United were able to recover against another of the newly promoted teams and win handsomely on this occasion, but the question mark over Shaw lingered. Afterwards, he admitted it wasn't good enough and said he is expecting some new signings before the window closes.

‘I’m disappointed in myself,’ Shaw admitted. ‘With my experience, I must be doing much better for the first goal – that’s not me. We showed the right mentality. It’s never nice to lose the first game when everyone is so optimistic, but we’ve got a lot of experience to block out the noise.

‘The objective has to be to win the Premier League, and last week’s result doesn’t mean we can’t do that. I’m sure there will be a couple additions to the squad which are needed to make us stronger.’

Will United use deadline day to sign a new left back? The word from inside Old Trafford is that the club are open to doing so if the right opportunity comes along, but there is no guarantee it will happen. Of course, director of football Jason Wilcox and the recruitment team led by Christopher Vivell have been aware of the issue all summer, even more so after the rarely used Tyrell Malacia left as a free agent.

It’s why United have maintained an interest in Lewis Hall throughout, while reluctantly accepting that it would be a difficult deal to execute in this window when so much of the budget has been committed to the midfield rebuild. Newcastle are determined to keep hold of Hall after selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, and it would take a bid of more than £75million to make them even consider letting the 21-year-old leave Tyneside.

Unless United can come up with that kind of money before the window closes at 11pm on Tuesday, the club will have to postpone any bid for Hall – as they did with Baleba, signing the 22-year-old Cameroon international for £70million a year after being put off by Brighton’s demand for £100million-plus.

But then what? It would seem reckless to head into the rest of a busy season that sees Michael Carrick’s team back in Champions League action without bringing in competition – or at least cover – for Shaw. Even if he regains his form and stays fit, it’s asking too much of him to start every game again – especially as United will have to play significantly more matches this season than the 40 (also known as the bare minimum) of last season.

United are believed to have assessed other options besides Hall, including Brighton’s Ferdi Kadioglu, Ian Maatsen of Aston Villa and Racing Santander’s Jorge Salinas.

United are in for Newcastle's Lewis Hall, but it would take a bid of more than £75million to make them even consider letting the 21-year-old leave Tyneside

Brighton full back Ferdi Kadioglu (centre) is also on United's list if they cannot convince Newcastle to sell Hall

Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas is another player United have assessed

Perhaps their best bet as the clock continues to tick down is a loan deal. United have looked at Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, but their options are limited at this stage of the window. So too, however, are the alternatives if no deal can be done. Right backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui are both capable of switching to the left, where Mazraoui plays for Morocco.

Patrick Dorgu was signed as a left wing-back but has performed better in a more advanced position. Academy graduate Harry Amass was Shaw’s understudy in pre-season and could continue in that role if United decide to keep him amid interest from Burnley. Martinez has also played there and Baleba, a left-footed defensive midfielder, has even been mentioned as a makeshift left back.

But if United have genuine title aspirations, as Shaw says, it seems like an unnecessary gamble not to sign another specialist defender in his position.

The bulk of United’s defensive overhaul will have to wait until next summer, even though conceding two set-piece goals in the opening-day defeat at Hull was alarming, and Martinez was punished for his sloppiness when Ipswich scored their second goal on Sunday. On the evidence of that game, attack may be United’s best form of defence this season.

The only other potential business at Old Trafford on deadline day would be a replacement for Joshua Zirkzee if the Dutch forward returns to Italy. Otherwise, all eyes will be on left back and whether United stick or twist.

Sports.title: What Tottenham are set to miss out on as the outrageously gifted Iliman Ndiaye opts for Man City - and why Everton star would have fixed Roberto De Zerbi's revamped front line
Sports.content:
What Tottenham are set to miss out on as the outrageously gifted Iliman Ndiaye opts for Man City - and why Everton star would have fixed Roberto De Zerbi's revamped front line

Unlock more from Matt Barlow inside the Spurs camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

After accepting defeat in pursuit of Cody Gakpo and picking up the bill from Tottenham’s transfer strategy summit over Italian food, Roberto De Zerbi emerged with Iliman Ndiaye in his sights.

De Zerbi insisted that ‘for once’ he was not the impatient one pushing hard and demanding more signings to ‘complete’ the team before the looming deadline.

Instead, he explained, the Spurs owners and chief executive Vinai Venkatesham were keen to press on and do more business and sporting director Johan Lange was armed with ‘ideas to make solutions’.

Somewhere amid this summit over spaghetti, Everton’s Ndiaye crystallised as an achievable target. And his future promises to be one of the big stories on deadline day with Manchester City now set to sign him after Liverpool had second thoughts about selling Gakpo.

At 26, Ndiaye is in his peak years. He has proven himself in the Premier League and though a Senegal international born in France, might qualify for registration as one of the eight homegrown senior players in a 25-man squad.

Ndiaye is outrageously gifted. No questions linger about his natural talent or technique on the ball, and he dribbles with a rhythm he attributes to childhood coaching drills designed by his father and performed to music.

Iliman Ndiaye is outrageously gifted. No questions linger about his natural talent or technique on the ball, and he dribbles with a rhythm he attributes to childhood coaching drills

Tottenham were closing in on a deal for the Everton winger but Manchester City are now set to sign him after he opted to chose the Etihad Stadium over north London

'His shoulders rock, almost as if he’s dancing,' said Jack Lester, then head of player development at Sheffield United and now on the coaching staff at Brentford. 'He goes past defenders, puts them down with his upper-body movements. He does things you can’t coach.'

There are few doubts either about his attitude or courage or work ethic. 'He’s a lovely lad, always smiling,' said Lester. 'Very popular. Fearless, a tough kid. Strong on the ball and not nice to play against.'

Questions remaining tend to revolve around his ability to exert his talent and influence games and maintain the tactical discipline required to succeed among the best teams in the Premier League. Ndiaye has worked hard to improve on this part of his game since breaking into Sheffield United’s team when still very raw and relatively uncoached at the age of 21.

The two years at Everton have shaped him into a Premier League footballer and a move to Spurs would have challengened him to develop further, to withstand greater competition for places, restore the club to past glories, cope with the pressure and scrutiny of a big-money move and establish himself as an elite player.

De Zerbi often claims a special connection with creative players, whether wide attackers or No 10s, because these were the positions he played. But he also knows those players must contribute goals and assists. Hard work alone will not cut it.

When he signed Savio from Manchester City, the Spurs boss told him to up his goal ratio and target 10-12 per season, which he said was the mark of the world’s best wingers.

Ndiaye has broken into double figures in a top-flight campaign only once, his first season at Everton when he scored 11 in 37 in all competitions, nine of them in the Premier League. Last season, there were only six in all. One season at Marseille produced four goals in 46, after which he was sold to Everton for £17million when De Zerbi arrived at the Stade Velodrome in 2024.

Spurs would have seen him primarily as a left-sided attacker and in their starting line-up - something he will not get guaranteed at City due to the likes of Jeremy Doku.

Ndiaye is versatile enough to play either side or as a No 10 but Spurs would have needed him on the left, where Son Heung-min has proved a tough act to follow and Mathys Tel still flatters to deceive. Savio can play either side but is most comfortable on the right, as are Mohammed Kudus and Dejan Kulusevski. Wilson Odobert, who likes to play on the left, and Xavi Simons, who has been most effective for Spurs as a No10, are recovering from serious knee injuries and not expected to be available until next year.

While now unlikely, a deal for Ndiaye would have offered De Zerbi a fresh new frontline with him and Savio either side of Omar Marmoush, none of whom were at the club when the season started with a dismal 3-0 defeat at Brentford.

One season at Marseille produced four goals in 46, after which Ndiaye was sold to Everton for £17million when De Zerbi arrived at the Stade Velodrome in 2024

Omar Marmoush got the nod at centre forward ahead of Dominic Solanke against Newcastle on Saturday, but flexibility will matter as Spurs trial-and-error their way to the best formula

New £85m signing Savio is comfortable on either flank but would prefer to play on the right - as would Mohammed Kudus and Dejan Kulusevski

Although Marmoush got the nod at centre forward ahead of Dominic Solanke against Newcastle on Saturday, flexibility will matter as Spurs trial-and-error their way to the best formula. All coaches value those who can operate in more than one position. Since taking control in April, De Zerbi has been committed to a 4-2-3-1 shape.

Ndiaye, Kudus and James Maddison might expect to challenge to start at No 10 but so far this season Spurs have reinforced midfield with Conor Gallagher or Mateus Fernandes in that role. Until they are stronger at the back and settled into a rhythm, it would be a surprise to see De Zerbi trade this ball-winning power for greater creativity.

For one thing, the play-making No 10 has become increasingly rare in the Premier League. More often they have come to be valued more for changing a game from the bench or starting when the opposition can be relied upon to sit deep and surrender possession.

See Eberechi Eze’s limited opportunities at Arsenal or Florian Wirtz’s struggles at Liverpool. See Rayan Cherki fight for a starting place at Manchester City. Those who regularly include a playmaker might do it as part of a front three not a front four. See Cole Palmer at Chelsea. Bruno Fernandes has been Manchester United’s best player for years but the best place to play him in their changing systems has often been a contentious issue.

Spurs will face a similar puzzle when Maddison, Kudus and Kulusevski are ready to start, but De Zerbi won’t care about that. He will just long for a day when he has all the options at his disposal and can find the best combinations.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
