World.title: Martelovo Jezero: Meet The Strange Cave Deep Below a Town in Istria
World.content:
August the 31st, 2026 – Martelovo jezero lies inside a strange cave deep below a town in Istria. It is the name of an even stranger lake that lies inside it. Very strict rules apply if you want to pay it a visit…

Croatia’s main “event” is certainly the coast, but there are plenty of incredible lakes to enjoy up and down the country. From the world-famous Plitvice Lakes to the “colourful” ones near Imotski, they all share one thing regardless of their shapes, sizes and depths: supernatural beauty. Putni kofer writes that some of them hide from our view, forcing us to make a little effort and look deeper into the secrets of the earth. One such lake is found in the very heart of Istria and its administrative centre, the town of Pazin. Martelovo jezero, or Martel’s lake, is a real gem of the darkness.

pazin’s most striking feature

Martelovo jezero is located deep within the Pazin Cave. As one of Pazin’s most distinctive features, the cave dominates the town: Pazin’s buildings cluster above this abyss, which has been protected since 1964. The protected area covers the canyon and sinkhole of the little river Pazinčica, about 500 metres long and around 100 metres deep, as well as the 300-metre-long speleological object known as the Pazin Cave, in which this largest Istrian sinking river disappears. It is precisely this cave that is home to Martel’s Lake.

the cave is named after a frenchman

But let’s start from the beginning, from the very entrance to the cave. It is called Dante’s Vestibule and is a huge, rock-vaulted fissure more than 20 metres high and 30 to 50 metres wide. The fissure continues into the darkness in a south-westerly direction, first narrowing to a width of only 10 metres and then widening again. At a distance of 100 metres from the entrance begins an expansion that essentially grows into an 80-metre-long and about 20-metre-wide terminal hall. In it lies the siphon lake named Martel’s Lake. The lake is widest at the very end of the hall, where water swirling can sometimes be observed. On average it is 10 metres deep. The lake owes its name to the French speleologist Édouard-Alfred Martel, who at the end of the 19th century began exploring the Pazin Cave in cooperation with Wilhelm Putick, a forestry expert from Ljubljana. The two of them also made the first detailed plan of the cave, and it was Martel who recorded the greatest flood that has so far occurred in the cave: in 1896 the water in the cave rose to 30 metres below the walls of the Castle that stands above it. Major floods were also recorded in 1964 and 1993.

adventure deep below the surface…

Martelovo jezero itself is located in the “terminal” hall of the Pazin Cave, but it is not the only lake the cave hides. It is connected by a siphon to another lake. That second, smaller lake is called Mitar’s Lake and was discovered in 1975, when Pazin speleologist divers dove into the terminal siphon and discovered a 70-metre-long continuation of the sinkhole. The diver responsible for that discovery was Mitar Marinović, and the smaller lake bears his name. Although Martelovo jezero is at first glance hidden from view, it is still possible to enjoy the sight of it as part of a guided speleo-adventure lasting two and a half hours, with equipment provided. As part of it, visitors also get a small zipline with which they cross over to the gravel bank of the underground lake.

a descent into the bowels of the earth…

“Physically, what awaits you is a somewhat more demanding walk that is accessible to all healthy people. It is not accessible to children without parental supervision or to people with physical motor impairments. It is necessary to bring sturdy sports footwear and a change of clothes; light long sleeves are recommended because of the cooler interior (around 15°C). The minimum age for children is 8 years,” state the pages of the Tourist Board of Central Istria.

If you aren’t up for this adventurous option, the Pazin Cave can also be enjoyed in other ways. For example, on the large zipline above the canyon itself, at a height of about 100 metres. There is also the possibility of walking along an educational trail or simply enjoying the view of the Pazin Cave from the Vršić Bridge or from below the terrace of the Hotel Lovac. These two locations are considered the best viewpoints overlooking the Pazin Cave.

diving is exceptionally dangerous…

But let us return briefly, at the end, to an activity in the Pazin Cave that will truly remain beyond the reach of ordinary mortals, and that is diving, which is left to experts. And even for them it is demanding and dangerous.

“Diving in the Pazin Cave is one of the more demanding cave dives because of the poor visibility (only 0.5–1 metre), which makes orientation and exploration of new space difficult. In addition, large quantities of branches and tree trunks are packed into the lake in front of the siphon, and in the siphon itself they are jammed between the rocks. This has caused cave divers to get tangled in the branches as well as the safety line being pulled under tree trunks, which made the return from the siphon difficult in already poor visibility. On top of that, the rocks in the siphon are very smooth and compact, which prevented cave divers from attaching the safety line,” states, for example, a document on the subject of the Pazin Cave.

World.title: Serbian Influencer Detained in Split Over Chetnik Tattoos Faces Deportation
World.content:
August the 31st, 2026 – A Serbian so-called influencer has been arrested and detained in Split for publicly displaying his Chetnik tattoos and now faces deportation and a 5-year ban from entering Croatia.

Split police arrested a 31-year-old Serbian citizen who publicly displayed tattoos of Chetnik leaders Draža Mihailović and Momčilo Đujić, as well as a Chetnik emblem, on Žnjan and then posted the photo on Instagram. Index reports that the court ordered him held for 15 days, and after the misdemeanour proceedings are completed he will be expelled from Croatia and banned from entering the country for five years. According to earlier media reports, this is Serbian influencer Marko Stojković, who has around 90,000 followers on Instagram. Nacional reported that Stojković had been photographed in a hospitality establishment on Split’s Žnjan, where a large tattoo of Draža Mihailović was clearly visible.

multiple people reported the man

Police revealed that the incident occurred on Thursday around 18:15 on the outdoor terrace of a hospitality establishment on Šetalište Ivana Pavla II. They say the 31-year-old publicly displayed on visible parts of his body a tattoo of Draža Mihailović, a tattoo of Momčilo Đujić, and an emblem featuring a double-headed spread eagle, a skull and crossed swords. Next to the symbol were Cyrillic inscriptions reading “with faith in God” and “freedom or death”. Police note that such insignia was used by Chetnik forces. About ten minutes later the man posted the photograph taken at that location on his public Instagram profile. “The post caused unrest and outrage among the public in Croatia,” police stated, adding that they subsequently received multiple reports from distressed members of the public.

the police discovered him in a car in split

Police launched a criminal investigation and yesterday established his identity and location. Around 14:00 they found and arrested him in a vehicle in the Split area. The criminal investigation, police say, established a well-founded suspicion that by publicly displaying the tattoos he disturbed public order and peace and that, “with the aim of causing fear and creating a hostile and humiliating environment,” he violated dignity and caused public disturbance. Police are also charging him with a misdemeanour under the Law on Combating Discrimination. He was brought before the competent court today, and police requested a 30-day prison sentence and a fine of 2,000 euros. The court has so far ordered him held in custody for 15 days, while the verdict will be delivered later.

he will face a 5-year ban from croatia

Police announced that after the misdemeanour proceedings are completed he will be issued an expulsion order from Croatia and a five-year ban on entering the country. Measures were also taken against a 56-year-old Serbian citizen who was in his company. His stay in Croatia was cancelled under the Law on Foreigners. Police state that by participating in the activities he promoted behaviour which he “knew or must have known” was contrary to Croatian regulations and public order.

who were the people his tattoos are depicting?

Draža Mihailović was the organiser and commander of the Chetnik movement during the Second World War. The Croatian Encyclopaedia states that from the autumn of 1941 he openly collaborated with the Germans and their allies, and that his forces committed numerous crimes and carried out ethnic cleansing of the non-Serb population in the territories of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. After the war he was convicted as a war criminal, sentenced to death and executed by firing squad in 1946.

Momčilo Đujić was a Chetnik vojvoda from the Knin area and commander of Chetnik formations in Dalmatia. The Croatian Biographical Lexicon states that he collaborated with the Italian occupation authorities and, after Italy’s capitulation, with German forces. Units under his command committed numerous crimes against the Croatian population, as well as against Serbs who did not accept Chetnik ideology.

this isn’t the first such incident…

A similar case occurred back in 2004. Croatia at that time banned the entry of Serbian basketball player Milan Gurović, who had a tattoo of Draža Mihailović on his upper arm and did not intend to cover it during a Partizan vs Cibona match in Zagreb. The Ministry of the Interior explained at the time that publicly displaying such insignia expresses or incites hatred or violence on racial, national or religious grounds.

World.title: One of Largest Railway Accidents in Europe Happened in Zagreb 50 Years Ago Today
World.content:
August the 30th, 2026 – One of the largest railway accidents in all of Europe occurred in Zagreb 50 years ago today. It tragically ended the lives of 167 passengers.

Turning the clock back 50 years, to this day in 1974, one of the largest railway accidents in Europe occurred in Zagreb. As Index recalls, a train arriving at the station overturned, tragically killing 167 passengers. All nine passenger carriages overturned, and the cause of the accident was the train entering the station too quickly; it then derailed on a curve and overturned. The train, travelling from Athens to Dortmund, was called the Direct Orient. That August it was mainly carrying guest workers returning from their annual holiday to Germany.

167 people died from smoke inhalation or catastrophic injuries

HRT/Screenshot

One of them left his compartment just before the Zagreb station to light a cigarette with a colleague. Then the carriage suddenly began to sway, only to overturn a few seconds later. The carriage continued sliding across the ground, and soon screams could be heard from the compartments. When the carriage finally stopped, the trapped passengers began to suffocate from the smoke. The compartment doors could not be opened, so they smashed the windows to save themselves. Around forty passengers could not be identified because of their severe injuries and were buried together at Mirogoj cemetery. The rescue operation involved the police as well as the army, which quickly appeared at the scene of the accident.

exhausted workers were blamed for the tragedy

HRT/Screenshot

The accident was caused by the driver and his assistant. On the way from Vinkovci to Zagreb they stopped only in Slavonski Brod, so the journey did not involve many duties. Fatigue then overcame them and both fell asleep. They woke up only when they had already arrived in Zagreb, and by then they could no longer slow the train, which was racing at a little over 100 km/h, although trains normally slow to 50 km/h before the station. Later investigations revealed that the train could have derailed on the curve between Ludina and Novoselec, but they had been lucky then.

It was also established that the driver and his assistant had been working continuously for 45 hours at that moment. After this accident, working-time legislation was regulated, stipulating that such work could not be performed for more than 6 hours without a break. The driver was sentenced to 15 years in prison, and his assistant to eight. The Direct Orient tragedy remains the largest railway accident on the territory of the former Yugoslavia, and today it is still among the five largest in Europe.

World.title: Dubrovnik Airport No Longer Requires Liquid and Electronics Removal
World.content:
August the 30th, 2026 – Dubrovnik Airport no longer requires liquid and electronic removal from hand luggage, making the security process much more smooth.

Dubrovnik Airport has begun introducing a new generation of technology for the security screening of passengers and hand luggage. These are devices that enable a three-dimensional display of luggage contents and a simpler, faster passage through the security screening process. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that the southernmost Croatian airport is currently the only one in the country using this advanced technology. The new security screening equipment includes six devices for screening hand luggage and six scanners for passenger security screening.

3d imaging

The first device is already in operation, and the remaining five will be installed by the beginning of December. Once all devices are installed, the entire passenger and hand luggage security screening system at Ruđer Bošković Airport will be equipped with the new generation of technical equipment. “By introducing this technology, we want to further improve and raise the level of aviation security protection and elevate the level of service and the overall passenger experience. The new devices enable higher-quality luggage screening, and for passengers they bring a simpler procedure because they will no longer need to remove liquids and electronic devices from their hand luggage. Together with the passenger security scanners, the entire process will be faster, more efficient and with less physical contact,” explained Viktor Šober, Director of Dubrovnik Airport.

faster security processing

This brand new equipment enables more effective detection of prohibited and dangerous items, while bringing passengers a faster passage through screening. The new C3 EDS CB technology brings concrete changes for passengers. With these scanners, it is no longer necessary to remove liquids, nor laptops, tablets, mobile phones and other larger electronic devices from hand luggage. Unlike conventional X-ray machines, C3 EDS CB devices create a three-dimensional image of the luggage contents and enable a more detailed inspection and more effective recognition of prohibited and dangerous items. This simultaneously speeds up passage through control and reduces passenger delays.

Part of the modernisation also includes new scanners for passenger security screening. During screening, the passenger stands in the device for a few seconds, and the system automatically alerts security staff if it detects an area that requires additional checking. The operator sees a generic outline of a human silhouette with any marked areas that need further inspection. The new equipment enables more effective detection of prohibited and dangerous items, while bringing passengers a faster passage through the security screening process, less waiting and less need to remove items from hand luggage. With this modernisation, Ruđer Bošković Airport is raising security screening standards and introducing technology used in the most modern European and world airports.

dubrovnik airport’s passenger numbers are very healthy

Back in June, Dubrovnik Airport ranked second in traffic among Croatian airports, behind Split, with 462 thousand passengers, which is also an increase of 3.3 percent on a monthly basis, while a slightly higher growth of 4.6 percent was recorded in the first half of the year, with 1.2 million passengers. In July, it served just over 558.5 thousand passengers, almost 18 thousand more than in the same month of 2025. The airport recently completed its Master Plan for the period from 2025 to 2045, which sets the framework for the next two decades of infrastructure development and capacity growth.

In general, they are satisfied with the tourist season thus far down in Dubrovnik. This year’s three-millionth overnight stay in the Dubrovnik area was recorded on 22 August, one day earlier than in 2025, reported the Tourist Board of the City of Dubrovnik. “This confirms stable tourism results and the continuous recognition of Dubrovnik on the international tourism market,” they stated from the Dubrovnik Tourist Board. According to data from the eVisitor system, more than 25 thousand guests are currently visiting Dubrovnik. From the 1st of January to the 22nd of August, a total of 931,660 tourists stayed in Dubrovnik, who achieved 3,000,099 overnight stays.

World.title: Speleologists Explore Biokovo Cave, Discover Evidence of Forgotten Craft
World.content:
August the 30th, 2026 – Speleologists have explored a deep Biokovo cave that has never been archived and discovered evidence of an almost entirely forgotten craft.

Croatia’s many rugged and imposing mountains hide many secrets of which we’re often not even aware while we admire them from afar or climb them. Putni kofer writes that a very large part of those secrets is hidden underground. On the Dalmatian giant Biokovo, high above Makarska, over 400 caves and pits have been explored. They continue to be explored, so members of the Speleological Section of HPD Biokovo recently descended into a pit near the mountain hut below Sveti Jure, which they themselves described as one from their series “it’s not in the archives.”

vertical walls in a 25-metre-deep pit

As Rikardo Škorlić from the speleological society revealed, the cave in question is called Kašogijeva jama, which was first explored back in 1987. “The pit is 25 metres deep and is located 120 metres east of the mountain hut,” he explained. Not unlike other Dalmatian caves, it is a typical karst pit, with almost vertical walls and narrow passages into which only a little daylight penetrates.

evidence of ice harvesting was discovered

What the speleologists found inside this Biokovo cave surprised them, as the pit hid many traces of an old craft that was important for decades on Biokovo. It seems that it was an ice house.

“This pit, quite like many other pits on Biokovo, was still full of ice about 30 years ago and once served the local population as a source of water in the dry summer months for watering livestock, and with the advent of tourism the ice was used for storing food and cooling drinks in Makarska. Today, due to climate change, there’s no more ice left, but traces of ice harvesting remain in the pit, including the remains of beams that the ice harvesters used to descend into the pit and extract the ice,” Rikardo Škorlić revealed.

harvesting ice on biokovo was a dangerous task

The ice houses on Biokovo are natural underground pits in which, due to the specific climate and cold air, eternal snow and ice are retained. In the past, local people called ice harvesters or cutters entered the dangerous pits. They broke off pieces of ice weighing up to 30 kilograms and then transported them on donkeys down to the foot of the mountain for cooling food and drinks in the Makarska area.

Fishermen, butchers and wealthier residents all came and bought it, and for many families, the sale of ice represented an important, for some even the main source of income. Before the appearance of electric refrigerators, what is everyday life for us today was a commodity that literally had to be extracted from the belly of the mountain. These old ice houses are also the subject of the international scientific project called IceLink, within which research of the Dusa and Crna ledenica pits in the area of Nature Park Biokovo was carried out this year.

World.title: Here’s What You’ll Soon be Able to Build in Croatia Without a Permit
World.content:
August the 30th, 2026 – You will soon be able to build certain types of buildings in Croatia without the need for a permit as the rules change.

The new Rulebook (Pravilnik) on buildings and works for which a building permit is not required is in public consultation until the 3rd of September. Poslovni reports that the new rules set out to define what can be constructed in Croatia and where, what the procedure is, and what documentation is needed for each type of work.

“When it comes to a canopy of up to 20 square metres that is constructed directly next to a main building or on the building plot of a main building, then a building permit isn’t required. However, if you’re building some kind of auxiliary building that serves the main purpose and is up to 50 square metres, you need the main design, a notification of the start of works, and an occupancy permit,” explained Dunja Magaš, State Secretary in the Ministry of Physical Planning, Construction and State Assets, for HRT.

what’s changing?

The biggest change concerns mobile homes or, as they’re now being referred to, single-storey modular-prefabricated or movable houses. These may be placed without the need for a building permit and without a main design within a campsite. They do however need to be in accordance with the conditions from the location permit on the basis of which the campsite obtained its occupancy permit and then its operating licence.

“A location permit for tourism buildings is required primarily for campsites, and within that for modular prefabricated houses of up to 40 square metres and a height of up to three and a half metres. The second subcategory is buildings for Robinson-style tourism, buildings of up to 20 square metres made of natural lightweight materials. These are the two types of buildings for which a location permit is required, but not a building permit,” Magaš explained.

Another exception is solar power plants with a capacity of up to 10 megawatts, for which a location permit and a main design are required. It’s also important to emphasise that mobile homes must not be built or placed in any other context. “The spatial plan must define what can be built outside the building area on agricultural land. Those mobile homes can only go into campsites that are planned by the spatial plan,” Magaš concluded.

World.title: Janika Lõiv 17th as gears fail at mountain bike worlds
World.content:
Reigning Estonian women's mountain biking champion Janika Lõiv finished 17th at the Mountain Bike World Championships in Val di Sole, Italy in particularly gruelling style.

Lõiv finished 5:44 behind the winner in the elite women's Olympic cross‑country race, Switzerland's Sina Frei, who won the gold in 1:27:50.

Lõiv said she had a strong start and felt good in the early laps. "The start went very well and I came out of the starting lap just 20 seconds behind the leader. During the first laps I tried to hold back a little because it was hot and I knew it would be a long race," she said.

However, her race took a technical turn for the worse on the third lap. "During the third lap I felt that the gears were sluggish — sometimes shifting, sometimes not. Until they stopped shifting altogether," explained the rider, who represented Estonia at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

This meant having to continue up slopes stuck in too high of a gear.

"Having to ride those 15‑20 percent climbs in one gear was a nightmare. Tears came to my eyes as I pushed myself up the hill through the pain."

Lõiv said while she managed to reset her gear system at a technical point, the damage was done. "Several riders passed me at once and my morale fell. I realised my legs were tired from that one crazy lap. From then on I rode at my own pace. My legs were cramping and I couldn't focus or think positive thoughts. I just wanted the finish to come quicker."

Of other Estonians competing, Mairit Kaarjärv finished 51st and Maribel Rannala 53rd in the women's under‑23 race, and Matthias Mõttus finished 58th in the men's equivalent.

World.title: Starting school in Estonia: Top tips for supporting your first grader
World.content:
For thousands of kids in Estonia, starting first grade on September 1 also means starting school. One psychologist offers tips to help families navigate this new chapter.

Children in Estonia generally start school at around seven years old, but Viktoriia Tkachuk, a psychologist at the Tartu Rajaleidja Center, explained in a video guide for "Let's Learn Together" that school readiness involves more than just a child knowing their letters and numbers.

Other factors include a child's emotional, social, cognitive, language and physical development, including their ability to focus, follow instructions, communicate and handle everyday tasks independently.

What matters most, Tkachuk said, is a child's overall, well-rounded development. A child who is curious, active, interested in learning, able to community and responsive to rules and requests is generally ready to start school.

"Other skills will develop along the way," she added.

Tkachuk said children should gradually learn to manage everyday tasks themselves, as independence can build confidence and reduce anxiety. Parents can help by involving kids in simple routines such as getting their school things ready in the morning.

The psychologist also advised encouraging a genuine interest in learning rather than drilling children on skills they'll need in school, including writing letters and numbers.

"The most important thing is to spark the child's interest," she said, warning that forced practice can ultimately backfire, leaving them tired and frustrated.

First graders starting school in Tallinn. September 1, 2022. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Starting school in a new language

Children starting school in a different language than those spoken at home face an entire extra layer of challenges, which Tkachuk said can leave even capable children feeling anxious, helpless or simply like an outsider.

Practicing communication skills at home can help, however, including learning basic Estonian phrases and roleplaying teacher-and-student situations in Estonian. Families can also make their own "My First 50 Estonian Words" dictionaries, and even watching cartoons and listening to music in Estonian can help.

At the same time, parents should also continue speaking their home language. Tkachuk said parents often worry this could cause their child to mix up languages or struggle to learn another one, but a strong first language can actually help children learn a second one.

"Your native language isn't an obstacle; it's a support," she emphasized.

As new first graders adjust to attending school, parents can help by talking about school positively, maintaining a predictable daily routine and making time each night to discuss how the day went.

A family in Tallinn on September 1. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"Children are very sensitive to their parents' emotions, and when parents are calm and confident, kids feel that support," Tkachuk said, suggesting encouraging messages like "Your teacher will help you if you have trouble understanding something."

A lot to handle

If a child says they don't want to go to school, she recommends responding with curiosity rather than jumping straight to arguing. Kids starting school have to navigate new relationships, social skills and a much bigger workload, all while adults can sometimes forget just how young they still really are.

Above all, the psychologist stressed, parents should avoid comparing them with others, as all children are different.

"Talk with your kid about their day," she said. "Ask what surprised them today, and who they played with at recess. Hold space for all their emotions."

If something has put your child off of school, ask what happened or what exactly they don't like.

"Let them be sad, angry or tired, and support them without criticism," Tkachuk said, stressing the importance of maintaining home as a safe environment for your child to be themselves. "Remind them that mistakes are normal and that we're all learning."

When it comes to homework, parents should support their child without taking over. They can explain instructions and check work together, but should let their child solve problems themselves, and praise effort rather than just results.

Families on the first day of school in Estonia. Source: Anna Aurelia Minev/ERR

"Kids can quickly lose motivation when they feel there's no point in trying because their parent can just do it better anyway," Tkachuk explained.

A child refusing to do their homework should also be taken as a sign — and an opportunity to talk to them.

"Tell them, 'I can see this is hard for you,'" she suggested. "'Let's figure out together what to do. Do as much as you can; it doesn't have to be perfect.'"

Helping kids make friends

Social skills develop through practice, Tkachuk said, and simply playing with other children provides valuable opportunities to learn how to communicate, resolve conflicts and cooperate.

"It can also help to talk through social situations together," she said. "If your child has a conflict with someone, talk about what happened without judging. Ask what they think about why the other kid acted the way they did, or how things could have gone differently."

Families should also talk to their kids about how various classmates may speak different languages at home and may need extra time to feel comfortable.

"They may avoid talking to other children even if they really want to because they are afraid of making linguistic mistakes," the psychologist explained.

Student on their first day of school in Estonia. Source: Anna Aurelia Minev/ERR

"But sometimes," she added, "just one friend is all it takes for a child who speaks a different language to feel more comfortable in a new environment."

Ask for help too

While adjusting to starting school can take several months, if your child continues to struggle, Tkachuk said it's worth seeking extra help.

"You can reach out to a psychologist, as well as contact a Rajaleidja center for educational advice and support," she said, adding that families can also talk to their child's teachers or school specialists.

"School is a big step toward independence, but the journey should be shared by the child, their parents and their teachers," Tkachuk said. "You are not alone in this process."

"Let's Learn Together" is a new online resource offering families practical guidance on navigating education in Estonia, from how the kindergarten and school system works to information on what additional help and resources are available.

Available in English, Estonian, Russian and Ukrainian, the site features articles, personal stories, podcasts and videos in which parents, young people and experts share their experiences with adapting to multilingual and multicultural life and education in Estonia.

All "Let's Learn Together" video guides include subtitle options on YouTube.

World.title: Association: While mistrust of AI still high, 3 out of 4 firms still use it
World.content:
The the Estonian Marketing Association (Eesti turundajate liit) noted cost savings is not always the main driver, but whatever the reasoning, AI should remain a tool and not an end in itself.

Supermarket Maxima runs around 300 campaigns a year which make use of AI. Its sales and marketing manager Jaanika Terasmaa said the technology allows ad agencies to bring hot ideas to meetings. "The agency comes to every meeting with a live idea, because it has been able to make quick clips of what a new advertising campaign could look like," Terasmaa told "Aktuaalne kaamera".

In any case, if agencies have been using AI, this has not been detrimental to campaigns, she went on.

"Unfortunately, or fortunately, an advertising agency is made up of people, so we don't recognize that from the price list, but we have been seeing better and more interesting quality in the content," Terasmaa added.

AI-created Ad on a billboard. Source: ERR

Kent Raju, creative director at Kala Ruudus, an advertising agency, said AI should remain a tool, not a final product. "We don't start by writing a command, but rather come up with an idea which is right for the brand," he said.

He criticised the use of AI for more simple tasks, such as restaurant menus, and which can be quite obvious. "I feel bad looking at the waste of artificial intelligence – material where restaurant menu pictures are taken with AI – for what purpose? You can take a real picture of real food, but it came with AI and it seems like the wrong choice."

Musician Mikk Saar said AI has created ads for events he has been a part of which have had defects, such as distorted faces or incorrect text, and he now wants to be consulted before ads get run. "A party won't be canceled, but if the poster is made with AI and everything is distorted, I won't be sharing it on social media – which means the organizer loses out. It doesn't match my brand image."

In any case, old‑fashioned advertising seems to be making a comeback. "It's become very popular to put out an ad and show that you actually made it," said Anniken Haldna, CEO of the marketing Association. This fact can get as many views as the ad itself, she added

The growing use of AI in advertising has also raised concerns about authenticity and trust. Studies cited by the association suggest that consumers are nowadays generally sceptical of AI‑generated ads, while experts warn that overuse could lead to a greater spread misinformation, as well as damaging companies' credibility. Creative professionals say the human perspective remains essential, with AI best employed as an aid rather than a replacement for human creativity.

World.title: School year opens with hundreds of students still waiting for placement
World.content:
As of Monday, 575 young people who finished basic school this spring still do not have a new school place registered in the Estonian Education Information System. The lists continue to change constantly, as some students decline the places offered to them, after which those places are offered to the next candidates.

The situation is especially tense in the capital. "There really aren't many free places in Tallinn," said Krista Keedus, head of education management at the Tallinn Education Department. "Estonian‑language high schools have completed their admissions and all places are filled," she added.

Tallinn's municipal high schools currently do not have the capacity to add more places, due to both space limitations and a shortage of teachers, Keedus said.

"There is no immediate plan to create additional places," she noted, pointing to the need to wait for the final data on needs and available places on 10 September.

The filling of school places is also strongly affected by the influx of residents from neighboring municipalities, as nearly 27 percent of students admitted to Tallinn's 10th grades for the new school year are not residents of the capital.

Tallinn's municipal high schools currently do not have the capacity to add more places. Source: Anna Aurelia Minev/ERR

Although high school places in Tallinn are full, there are still available study places at Tallinn Applied College and the technology college Tehno Tallinn. Keedus encouraged students without a place to consider vocational education: "Our vocational education is not only vocational training — it is also vocational secondary education." "They could at least try continuing their studies there first, and if it truly doesn't suit them, then look again for a gymnasium place," she said.

Places in preparatory studies — intended for students with weaker final results — were also filled already in the summer. Discussions are currently underway with the Ministry of Education about creating additional places based on need.

The final deadline for local governments to offer solutions to students in need is 1 November, but officials are already trying to contact young people now to understand why they have ended up without a school place.

"It is of course sad if young people haven't managed to secure a school place by 1 September and cannot start their school year," Keedus said. "But that doesn't mean starting later — a few days or even weeks — would be impossible. Their learning opportunities are certainly not locked," she added.

Keedus also pointed out that in previous years, the number of young people who ended their education after basic school was similar or slightly smaller, although monitoring was incomplete before the study obligation was introduced.

"The ministry has monitored each year how many young people do not reach the next level of education, and that number has usually been around 400–500," Keedus said.

"Previously, this was not a legal problem. It was, however, a problem for the young people and for Estonia as a whole, because those who continue their education have better chances of coping in life — which is why the study obligation was established. Until now, this issue wasn't directly on the table, because young people had the freedom to go to work, for example, and therefore we did not conduct this kind of ongoing monitoring at the start of the school year," Keedus explained.

World.title: 'Even If...' campaign assures sexual assault survivors help is available
World.content:
A new Estonian campaign is reminding survivors of sexual violence that they can seek free, 24/7 help even if they lack the words or don't remember everything.

The Social Insurance Board's (SKA) "Even If..." campaign highlights the free, round-the-clock assistance and care available at dedicated sexual violence crisis centers (SAKs) across Estonia.

It addresses three common reasons survivors may hesitate to seek help: "Even if no one saw," "Even if you don't remember everything," and "Even if you can't find the right words."

"After experiencing sexual violence, your memories may be patchy, and you may feel confused, angry, ashamed or guilty," said Kai Part, a gynecologist at the Tartu University Hospital (TÜK) center. "These are normal trauma responses to an abnormal event."

No police report or referral needed

Estonia's sexual violence crisis support centers are free and open 24/7 to anyone who has experienced sexual violence or suspects they may have, regardless of age or gender.

The sooner someone seeks help, the better, but it's still worth coming to a crisis center even after changing clothes, showering or waiting some time before deciding to seek help.

No referral or police report is required, and minors can also seek help independently.

Sexual violence crisis centers offer medical examinations, evidence collection, pregnancy prevention, STI testing and treatment, HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and counseling.

The centers will also help people access further psychological and other help, and provide support if a victim chooses to contact the police.

"People can decide for themselves what help they want to receive," Part said. "That can also be the beginning of healing — when they can once again decide what happens to them."

Patient at a psychiatrist appointment. Photo is illustrative. Source: Sigmund/Unsplash

Five centers across the country

Annika Silde, head of violence victims services at SKA, emphasized that anyone can become a victim of sexual violence, regardless of age, gender or background.

"You don't have to prove what happened or explain why you reacted a particular way in order to seek help at a SAK," she said. "The responsibility always lies with the perpetrator."

Sexual violence crisis centers operate at five hospitals across Estonia: West Tallinn Central Hospital (LTK), Tartu University Hospital (TÜK), Pärnu Hospital, Ida-Viru Central Hospital (IVKH) in Kohtla-Järve and Kuressaare Hospital in Saaremaa.

In 2025, 268 people sought help at the centers, including 106 minors. Women accounted for 95 percent of those seeking help.

SKA's "Even If..." campaign runs in public and online through September 13.

More help available

If you have experienced, are experiencing or think you may be experiencing domestic abuse, domestic violence or sexual violence, or are otherwise in crisis, help is available.

In case of emergency, call 112. Estonia's five sexual violence crisis centers (SAKs) are open 24/7 in Tallinn, Tartu, Pärnu, Kohtla-Järve and Kuressaare. On-call psychiatric care can also be reached by phone 24/7 in Tallinn at +372 617 2650, in Tartu at +372 731 8764 and in Pärnu at +372 447 3281. The Eluliin emotional support hotline is open daily from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. in Estonian (+372 655 8088) and in Russian (+372 655 5688). Another emotional support hotline is available every day from 10 a.m. to midnight in Estonian, Russian and English at 116 123. The Ohvriabi victim support hotline is available 24/7 in Estonian, Russian and English at 116 006. The child helpline is also open 24/7 in Estonian, Russian and English at 116 111.

World.title: Pioneering Estonian curling duo Kaldvee and Lill split after 11 years
World.content:
The duo, who won silver at the 2024 World Championships and were named Estonian Team of the Year the same year, made history as the first Estonians to compete in mixed doubles curling at the Olympics, which they did in February this year at the at the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics.

"We played together for 11 years — it's a very long and successful collaboration. We are both very proud of what we achieved," Lill told ERR. "The decision didn't come easily. We met several times and discussed what to do, as we always do after an Olympic cycle. This time we decided to go our separate ways, but we are both staying in curling."

Lill outlined just how extraordinary their sporting journey had been, starting from training in a Soviet-era munitions plant. "What we did is quite impossible — you come from an old Soviet rocket factory and make it to the Olympics," he said with emotion. "Against all the odds, we made it happen. I'm deeply proud of that."

Asked if he had any regrets, Lill said: "Every athlete feels they could have done better. We are ambitious people and always aimed high. We gave our maximum and achieved great results."

Lill will continue in the mixed doubles, partnering with Karoliine Kaare, his life partner. Kaldvee is to captain an all-new new Estonian women's team. "There were options — not too many, we are in Estonia after all," Lill joked. "With Karoliine, we decided it was worth trying. You never know how a new team will work, so we'll give our best and see what happens."

Kaldvee is at the helm of a young and talented women's team with Czech coach Jakub Bareš already on board. Lill was buoyant about the team's prospects. "Marie is Estonia's most experienced curler," he said. "She has captained the national team before. She will lead a young and talented team, preparing for the European Championships and the B‑division World Championships."

Lill and Karoliine Kaare. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

"If I ever leave curling, I want the sport to be in a better place than when I started. It would be sad if we just walked away and didn't pass on what we've learned," he reflected.

The Lill-Kaare new sporting pairing's immediate goal is to qualify for the World Championships in January. "First we need to qualify from Estonia," Lill said. "November will see who gets to represent Estonia."

In an Instagram post, the duo wrote: "One chapter ends but the journey continues! From an old Soviet missile factory to the Olympics. Against all the odds, we made Estonian curling history."

Kaldvee and Lill placed 10th at the 2026 Winter Olympics.

World.title: Population of major forest pest drops for second straight year
World.content:
Three to four years ago, the population of spruce bark beetles in Estonian forests was still increasing, but in recent years it has been trending downward.

The spruce bark beetle is a small insect, growing only 4–5 millimeters long. During mass reproduction, however, they are capable of killing large spruce trees and entire spruce stands.

Cooler and wetter summer weather has helped reduce their numbers, and the number of the beetle's natural enemies has also grown.

The spruce bark beetle is monitored across Estonia by the Environmental Agency in cooperation with the State Forest Management Center (RMK). In some counties in South Estonia, the Estonian University of Life Sciences also operates its own monitoring stations. Both the university's data and nationwide monitoring results show that the beetle's population has been declining over the past two years.

The beetle's population was very high in 2022 based on RMK and agency monitoring data, said Merit Ehrpais, senior specialist at the Environmental Agency.

A patch of forest with bark beetle damage in Ida-Viru County. Source: Dmitri Fedotkin/ERR

In 2023, the population remained high, but a downward trend began to appear in some counties. In 2024, the decline became clearer, and the 2025 results were even lower than those of 2024.

Kristjan Ait, junior researcher in forest management and forest ecology at the Estonian University of Life Sciences, added that based on this year's available data, the catch numbers are relatively modest. One direct factor influencing beetle numbers is Estonia's summer weather.

"Last summer was generally cool and rainy, which kept the population lower. This year's spring was also extremely unfavorable for the beetles: their flight began quite late, in early May," he said. Typically, the beetles begin flying in mid‑April. This year's spring dragged on, remaining cool and rainy, which further affected beetle numbers.

Ehrpais confirmed that results from pheromone traps show a clear link between weather and beetle activity. During cooler, wetter, and windier weeks, beetle spread is lower, while warmer periods bring higher numbers again.

In addition, the number of the beetle's natural enemies — such as bark beetle flies, ant beetles, and birds — has increased over the years. Their numbers have reached a level where they can now limit the beetle population more effectively.

Meelis Matkamäe Autor/allikas: Erlend Štaub

Meelis Matkamäe, chairman of the Estonian Private Forest Union and CEO of Rakvere Forest Cooperative, has also noticed that there have been fewer beetle outbreaks in the past two years.

"The last two years have been quite good, especially in managed stands. The spruce bark beetle mostly infests weakened trees, and in a properly managed forest it is generally difficult for the beetle to establish a colony. But in unmanaged stands — for example those with storm damage or weakened trees — it can operate more freely, and conditions for reproduction are much better," Matkamäe said.

Ait added that managed forests offer better opportunities to limit beetle numbers, and mixed stands also provide poorer breeding conditions for them.

What will happen to the beetle population in the future is impossible to predict. "Right now the situation is fairly normal, but nature is constantly changing. What will happen in a couple of years, we don't know. Many influencing factors are things you can't directly see. For example, how root rot develops and affects spruce health, or whether new drought periods or storm damage occur — any of these could turn this calm period upside down," Ait said.

World.title: Photos: Kaido Ole's exhibition "Krt" opens at Temnikova & Kasela gallery
World.content:
On 28 August, Kaido Ole's new solo exhibition "Krt" opened at the Temnikova & Kasela gallery in Tallinn.

Ole's new exhibition focuses on the artist's recent paintings, where a recurring motif of burning becomes a tool for giving shape to something difficult to define — an all‑encompassing "bad."

Ole describes the exhibition as an attempt to "move the bad out of oneself and into the pictures." "Through art, the bad can find a place, and the world can at least momentarily return to balance," the artist explained.

"Krt" is Kaido Ole's third exhibition this year. At the beginning of the year, he opened the show "Müüa maja Raplas" in Rapla, and in February he presented examples from his art collection at Vaal Gallery.

The exhibition "Krt" will remain open at Temnikova & Kasela gallery until 10 October.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate increases against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced an increase on Monday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,541.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,540 Iraqi dinars on Sunday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,545 Iraqi dinars and 1,535 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate increased, fluctuating between 1,541.5 and 1,541 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraqi judiciary sentences kidnapper of US journalist to 15 years in prison
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Central Criminal Court sentenced Amir Rahim Jabar Lazim, a member of the Iran-backed group Kataeb Hezbollah, to 15 years in prison under the country’s anti-terrorism law for kidnapping US journalist Shelly Kittleson on March 31.

Kittleson was kidnapped during the daytime on Saadoun Street in central Baghdad. Armed gunmen pushed her into a silver vehicle, while another getaway car crashed during the escape. Iraqi security forces intercepted the crashed car and arrested Lazim.

The US journalist was kept hostage for more than a week when Kataeb Hezbollah freed her in early April ahead of a US-Iran ceasefire.

Kittleson, who has extensively covered the Middle East for publications like the BBC and Politico, expressed her gratitude to the Iraqi justice system on X and affirmed her right to seek compensation.

This decision marks a rare court step against a major, Tehran-aligned armed group in Iraq.

The verdict comes at a critical time for Iraq’s new government, led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, which is under intense pressure from Washington to disarm pro-Iran militias and place all weapons under strict state control.

The effort to disarm Kataeb Hezbollah has pushed Iraq into a severe security and political crisis, as the group has rejected the government’s disarmament mandates and vowed to expand its military arsenal.

World.title: Iraq discusses oil and gas development with BP, ConocoPhillips
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair and representatives from British Petroleum (BP) and Texas-based ConocoPhillips discussed on Monday the development of Iraq’s oil and gas industry.

The meeting held in Baghdad included BP’s Iraq director Zaid al-Yasiri, Nader Zaki, Ariel Flores, and ConocoPhillips representative William Arnold, as well as senior Iraqi officials in the oil sector.

The discussions addressed strategic advancements to maximize the utilization of Iraq’s hydrocarbon resources, optimize field development, and upgrade extraction technologies, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The Iraqi Oil Ministry activated in early August its Kirkuk oilfield contract with BP, a project aiming to elevate crude oil production from its current capacity of 320,000 barrels per day to a peak target of 420,000 barrels per day.

The deal expands crude extraction while capturing associated gas to eliminate gas flaring and provide fuel for power plants.

The activation of the Kirkuk project represents a major step in Iraq’s broader energy strategy to achieve natural gas self-sufficiency and reduce reliance on imported fuel.

ConocoPhillips has agreed to purchase a 42 percent share in BP’s Kirkuk project, boosting its position in Iraq by redeveloping four key oil resources in the northern Iraqi province.

ConocoPhillips Chairman Ryan Lance said that the investment aligns with the company’s conservative approach by offering access to a big, high-quality, and long-life resource base while needing very little expenditure.

The agreement represents another initiative by Iraq to attract foreign investments and boost production from its aging oil assets, as well as to strengthen partnerships with prominent global energy companies.

World.title: India to receive first Iraqi oil shipment in five months
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – India is preparing to receive its first shipment of Iraqi oil in five months, a development reflecting the return of Iraq’s crude oil flows to one of Asia’s largest oil markets, despite ongoing shipping challenges across the Strait of Hormuz.

India’s Bharat Petroleum expects to receive the shipment within the next few days. The tanker carrying Iraqi oil has already passed through the Strait of Hormuz and arrived in Fujairah, UAE, for a ship-to-ship transfer, according to Reuters.

Bharat Petroleum’s Chief Financial Officer, Vetsa Ramakrishna Gupta, said that the company secured a vessel to load the Iraqi shipment and transport it to Fujairah. There, the oil will be transferred from ship to ship before reaching the company’s refineries.

These arrangements reflect the efforts of Asian refiners to find flexible logistical solutions for securing crude oil at a time when transportation cost, insurance, and tanker availability have become crucial factors in determining the viability of purchasing shipments from the Gulf region.

The Indian company typically requires around two million barrels of Iraqi oil per month, making a consistent supply from Baghdad crucial to meeting its refinery’s crude oil needs.

Bharat Petroleum has not disclosed the name of the vessel used to transport the shipment but stated that the ship’s owner agreed to load the crude and proceed to Fujairah for a ship-to-ship transfer.

Iraq is one of the countries most affected by disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, given that a significant portion of its oil exports depend on ports located on the Arabian Gulf.

World.title: Iraq exports 21 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s fuel oil exports through Syria have seen a significant increase since the outbreak of the US-Israeli war against Iran on February 28.

Iraqi oil flows via neighboring Syria are part of alternative routes for the country’s oil shipments to global markets following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Total Iraqi fuel oil exports transported via Syria reached 21.4 million barrels between March and the end of August 2026.

This step is part of Baghdad’s continuous efforts to establish alternate export channels amid shipping disruptions via the Strait of Hormuz, the country’s primary maritime trade artery, which led to unprecedented challenges to the oil industry.

Iraqi fuel oil began flowing overland through Syrian territory after the Iraqi state-owned oil marketing company (SOMO) reached deals to transport approximately 650,000 tons per month (approximately 4.7 million barrels) to be stored at the Baniyas port before being shipped to global markets.

Iraqi fuel oil shipments via Syria increased rapidly between March and the end of August 2026.

Iraq’s fuel oil exports through Syria were 254,000 barrels in March, 686,000 barrels in April, 3.86 million barrels in May, five million barrels in June, 5.65 million barrels in July, and 5.91 million barrels in August.

World.title: Integrity Commission halts 550-dunam land auction in Anbar, saving 19B dinars
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Federal Commission of Integrity announced on Monday, August 31, 2026, that it has successfully halted the fraudulent sale and auction procedures of a prime 550-dunam state-owned real estate parcel in Anbar Governorate, preventing the squandering of over 19.25 billion IQD (approximately $14.7 million) in public funds.

According to an official statement received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the operation was executed by a field investigation unit from the Commission’s Anbar Investigation Office as part of its ongoing oversight of state-owned properties nationwide.

Field investigators conducted comprehensive on-site audits and cross-referenced documentation across the State Real Estate Department in Anbar, the Urban Planning Directorate, and the City Organization Division at the Ramadi Municipality Directorate:

Location & Unauthorized Sale: The 550-dunam plot is situated within the master plan designated for the future urban expansion of Ramadi. It had been auctioned and sold to an individual buyer without obtaining statutory municipal approvals from the Ramadi Municipality Directorate.

Severe Undervaluation: The official appraisal committee at the Anbar State Real Estate Department had valued the property at just 25.09 million IQD per dunam, resulting in a total sale price of 13.75 billion IQD.

Market Discrepancy: The Commission’s field investigators analyzed land coordinates and comparable market pricing, referencing the General Commission for Taxes’ benchmark guidelines. They determined that the actual market value stands at 60 million IQD per dunam, bringing the true aggregate value to 33.00 billion IQD.

Total Prevented Loss: The fraudulent undervaluation represented a direct financial deficit of 19,250,000,000 IQD against the state treasury.

World.title: Iran president meets PM Modi, seeks help to end war
World.content:
In a meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek, PM Modi called for freedom of navigation and commerce while stressing that civilians and civilian infrastructure, including commercial shipping, and seafarers, must not be harmed under any circumstances.

World.title: HC reinstates bank official sacked without inquiry over hashtag campaign
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Jammu &

high court has set aside the dismissal of a J&K Bank executive sacked without an inquiry into an alleged #TortureKashmir hashtag campaign on social media, ruling that a financial institutionâs managing director âcannot be trusted with the drastic power to dismiss an employee without investigationâ.

âThe President and governor are high constitutional functionaries and, therefore, they can dispense with the services of an employee without holding an inquiry in appropriate cases. But the same level of trust cannot be reposed in an officer of the level of managing director and CEO of a bank,â the single-judge bench of Justice Sanjay Dhar said in its verdict last Saturday.

The petitioner, Saadut Hussain Pampori, joined J&K Bank as a computer engineer in June 1995 and rose to deputy general manager by 2022, serving as an officer on special duty to the chief minister from 2016 to 2018 under the BJP-PDP govt led by Mehbooba Mufti.

The bankâs then MD suspended him on April 15, 2024, pending investigation into misconduct before ordering his dismissal on July 15 that year under Clause 12.29 of the officersâ service manual.

The dismissal followed a report by DGP (CID) based on âcredible sources, as also from discreet enquiriesâ. The report accused Pampori of spreading misinformation about alleged state-backed atrocities on Kashmiris.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The court held that information gathered from sources or through discreet enquiries by DGP does not qualify as an âinvestigationâ under Clause 12.29, since the process involves no collection of evidence or recording of witness statements.





Justice Dhar drew a line between Clause 12.29 and Article 311(2)(c), under which govt may terminate an employee without the normal procedure if satisfied that retention is prejudicial to state security.

J&K administration has dismissed nearly 100 govt employees under that provision.

Clause 12.29, the court said, lays down specific preconditions, including an investigation by a state, Union territory or central agency, before an employee can be sacked.

Quashing the order against Pampori as ânot sustainable in lawâ, the court restored him to the post he held before his dismissal, albeit allowing the bank to proceed against him afresh.

World.title: It's time to move from endless war to end of war: PM to Putin
World.content:
With no end in sight to the Russia-Ukraine war, PM

renewed his message of peace to Russian President

on Monday, saying on this occasion that it was time to move from an endless war to the end of war for the sake of humanity.

Modi delivered the message in his opening remarks before a bilateral meet with Putin on the margins of the SCO heads of state summit in Bishkek in which the two focused on expanding cooperation in energy, defence, innovation, space, fertilisers and people-to-people linkages. The 'endless war to end of war' message is the latest in a series of televised statements made by Modi before Putin for the return of peace, beginning with his assertion in 2022- frequently cited by the Western world, one which even made it to the Bali Declaration - that this wasn't the era of war.

That message too was delivered on the margins of an SCO summit in Samarkand. He followed it up with a message to Putin in Moscow in 2024 - in the midst of outrage in the West over his Russia visit - that no solution can be found on the battlefield.

India's balancing act on the war saw Modi travelling to Ukraine a few months after his visit to Russia in 2024.

Modi told Putin in Bishkek that India supports all efforts for peace and will continue to do so in future.





âEvery day spent on the war pushes humanity back. And every step taken towards peace fills humanity with new hope and enthusiasm. We will have to move from an endless war to an end of war, which is very important for humanityâs well-being,â said the PM.

âThat all issues are resolved peacefully as soon as possible is the call of humanity. This is the message of India. This is the message of the land of Gandhi and the land of Buddha â the path to peace,â said Modi, adding that he was looking forward to welcoming Putin for the Brics summit.

According to foreign secretary Vikram Misri, PM Modi conveyed to Putin Indiaâs readiness to do whatever is feasible and necessary to move the conflict towards an end because âit is exacting a very heavy toll on the global community at largeâ.

âHad extensive discussions with President Putin. Discussed the full range of the India-Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. It is gladdening to see significant progress across various sectors in recent years,â Modi said on X.

In his own televised statement, Putin acknowledged Modiâs personal attention to the development of bilateral ties. Putin said Russia was preparing âseriouslyâ for the Brics summit in India.

Putin also said Russia was preparing âseriouslyâ for the Brics summit in India and highlighted that over the past 10 years, the number of Indian students in Russia has risen to 40,000.

World.title: 51 Indian nationals killed in Russian Army, 139 discharged; MEA says talks on with Moscow

NEW DELHI: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said on Monday that 139 of the 227 Indian nationals recruited into the Russian armed forces had been discharged, while 51 had died. India continues to have talks with Moscow to secure the release and repatriation of those still serving.Misri gave the figures while responding to a question on Indians serving in the Russian army during a Ministry of External Affairs briefing on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Kyrgyzstan.He said the issue of Indian nationals being recruited into the Russian armed forces had been raised with Russia âat various levels on various occasionsâ.âAt last count, we had information about 227 Indian nationals who had been recruited into the Russian army,â Misri said. âOut of that, we have information that 139 of our nationals have been discharged from the army. And unfortunately, of course, we have information also about 51 people who have perished so far.âMisri said India remained engaged with Moscow to secure the early discharge and return of those whose cases were still pending.âThis is an issue that we are in constant discussions with the Russian side,â he said.He added that the Indian Embassy in Moscow was regularly monitoring the situation and working with Russian authorities to facilitate the release and repatriation of the remaining Indian nationals.âOur embassy in Moscow is monitoring this situation regularly with regard to the release and repatriation of these Indian citizens,â Misri said, adding that India was seeking to ensure that those still serving were discharged at the earliest and returned to their families.MEA's remarks come as PM Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation meeting in Bishkek.During the meeting, Modi stressed the need for the world to move from an era of âendless warsâ towards the âend of warâ, while the two leaders discussed bilateral cooperation and global developments.Misri also said India and Russia were looking to expand bilateral trade. He said an Indian Exporters Forum would be organised alongside the next annual summit in Russia to encourage Indian businesses to diversify and increase exports to the Russian market.

World.title: IMD predicts ‘below normal’ Sept rainfall, Aug was the warmest Aug in India since 1901
World.content:
India is bracing for below-average rainfall this September, signaling an early end to the monsoon season with overall inadequate precipitation.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Monthly rainfall over the country as a whole is most likely to be âbelow normalâ in Sept, the last month of the monsoon season, said IMD on Monday â an indication that the four-month rainy season is likely to end with overall deficient cumulative (June-Sept) rainfall as predicted earlier with high probability due to the impact of El Nino.The Met department said August, which reported a deficit of more than 16 percent in monthly rainfall in the country despite good rains in certain parts, was the warmest August in India since 1901, recording a mean temperature of 28.01 degrees Celsius.Region-wise, August in south Peninsular India was the second-warmest August since 1901, whereas it was the third warmest for east and northeast India, and fifth warmest for northwest India in the past 126 years.So far, the country as a whole reported a deficit of 14 percent in cumulative (June 1-Aug 31) rainfall, despite ânormalâ rainfall in July. In June, the deficit was as high as 35 percent. Out of a total of 741 districts assessed for monsoon rainfall distribution, 312 districts (42 percent) received âbelow normalâ rainfall and 38 districts (5 percent) reported large deficient rainfall till Aug 31.A forecast of âbelow normalâ rainfall in Sept may lead to a deficit in overall kharif crop acreage.Though sowing of most of the seasonal crops is almost complete with a decline in acreage by nearly 2 percent compared to the corresponding period last year, low rainfall in Sept means an increase in the input cost due to farmersâ spending on irrigation of standing crops.âSpatially, many parts of the country are likely to receive below-normal rainfall, but some areas of northwest, northeast, east, east-central and south-east Peninsular India are likely to receive ânormal to above-normalâ rainfall,â said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.He said currently âstrong El NiÃ±o conditionsâ are prevailing over the equatorial Pacific Ocean, with sea surface temperature (SST) remaining above normal across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. âThese conditions are expected to strengthen further in the coming months,â said Mohapatra, hinting at its negative impact on Sept rainfall.El NiÃ±o, characterised by the warming of ocean surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is invariably associated with a weak monsoon and a harsh summer in India.At present, neutral Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) conditions prevail over the Indian Ocean and the forecasts from the Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecast System (MMCFS) indicate that neutral IOD conditions are likely to persist through Sept. It means the monsoon may not benefit from this climatic phenomenon as only positive IOD helps increase rainfall activities.IMD noted that the extreme weather events (lightning, thunderstorm and heavy rains) took 113 human lives in Aug. Mohapatra, however, said this figure can be cross-checked with the data compiled by the states.

World.title: ‘Where are the jobs?’ Congress challenges PM Modi after 7.8% Q1 GDP growth data
World.content:
File photo: Congress leaders Jairam Ramesh and Pawan Khera during a press conference

Jairam Ramesh flags investment, consumer confidence concerns

Congress asks: Where are the jobs?

PM Modi calls Q1 growth a âherculean featâ

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Congress on Monday hit out at the government over India's 7.8 per cent GDP growth in the April-June quarter, saying the figure was "not an economic spring" and presented a "Greatly Distorted Picture" of the state of the economy.The opposition party questioned why the country's economic growth was not translating into jobs and prosperity, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the first-quarter performance as an "exemplary" and "herculean feat".Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the quarterly GDP numbers did not reflect what he described as depressed private investment sentiment, both domestic and foreign."The quarterly GDP numbers, such as they are reported, present a GDP - Greatly Distorted Picture - of the economy. They do not convey the decidedly depressed private investment sentiment in the economy - both domestic and foreign," Ramesh said in a post on X.He also claimed that consumer confidence was sluggish, household savings rates had fallen and debt had reached record highs."Consumer confidence is very sluggish, hitting its lowest point since COVID and on a relentless downward trajectory since November 2025. Prices of household essentials are galloping.Educated unemployment is at alarming levels. The unabated trade deficit with China is wreaking havoc," Ramesh said.He further claimed that the concentration of key sectors among a few large conglomerates was having "deleterious effects", adding that the wealth of India's five richest families had grown by 400 per cent while the real wages of salaried workers had fallen.Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said one quarter of 7.8 per cent growth did not amount to an "economic spring"."One quarter of 7.8 per cent growth is not an economic spring. If India has truly 'bloomed', why do rampant unemployment, leaked exam papers, and a crumbling education system define the ground reality?" he said."Why is the republic's prosperity not translating into the prosperity of its public?" Khera asked.Taking aim at the prime minister's remarks, he said GDP measures national output rather than jobs, wages or opportunities."Modi can manage his headlines. For India's youth, the question remains the same as ever: Where are the jobs?" Khera said.The Congress's criticism came after government data released on Monday showed that India's economy grew by a faster-than-expected 7.8 per cent in the April-June quarter.The growth figure exceeded the Reserve Bank of India's forecast of 7 per cent for the quarter and kept India as the world's fastest-growing major economy.Responding to the data, PM Modi took a dig at those questioning the state of the Indian economy, saying "doomsayers were doomed and India bloomed yet again".The prime minister said India's GDP growth during the first quarter of FY 2026-27 was a "herculean feat"."The collective strength of our people ensured India delivered such growth despite oil price shocks and supply chain issues in the midst of global uncertainties," PM Modi said in a post on X.The Q1 growth compares with a 6.9 per cent expansion in the year-ago quarter.The RBI has projected India's economy to grow by 6.7 per cent in the full 2026-27 fiscal year.
