World.title: This Filipino couple has one of the biggest private collections of Yayoi Kusama’s art
World.content:
(1st UPDATE) Lito and Kim Camacho have over 100 works of the late Japanese avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama in various mediums

MANILA, Philippines – Filipino couple Jose Isidro “Lito” Camacho and Maria Clara “Kim” Acuña Camacho are among the world’s ardent collectors of the late Japanese avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama (who died on August 14), with dozens of pieces in their home in an exclusive village in Makati City.

Lito, a banker, served as energy and also finance secretary during the early years of the Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo administration or from 2001 to 2003. When Newsbreak magazine interviewed his wife Kim in 2002, she was then the country manager and representative for Sotheby’s, one of the world’s biggest auction houses for art and real estate. At the time, they were not yet collectors of Kusama’s works.

The Camachos now have such a wide collection that they’ve been invited to display some of Kusama’s works in special exhibits abroad. For instance, they loaned nine of their pieces for the Yayoi Kusama exhibition held at the National Gallery Victoria (NGV) in Melbourne, Australia, more than a year ago. The exhibit, which displayed nearly 200 of Kusama’s artworks, ran from December 15, 2024 to April 21, 2025, and was attended by over half a million visitors.

Among the pieces displayed from the Camacho collection were Kusama’s Sex Obsession painting and her Statue of Venus Obliterated by Infinity Nets sculpture. Sex Obsession can be viewed at 1:27 into this Yayoi Kusama overview video below published by NGV Melbourne, while Statue of Venus Obliterated is shown at 1:31.

Play Video

The Camachos first encountered Kusama artworks during the couple’s visit to Japan in 2004, or 22 years ago, when Kusama’s popularity was starting to peak. Upon the invitation of the Japanese government, they visited Tokyo, where there was a retrospective on Kusama at the National Museum of Modern Art.

Kim had not heard of Kusama prior to that, but she was wowed by her works of art.

“I was immediately attracted to her works because they were so different. There was something very original and fresh about them, and the retrospective showed how adept she was at different mediums: she started with very small watercolors, moving to acrylic on canvas and sculptural pieces, and eventually entire room installations. Her versatility, sense of fun, originality and uniqueness were just outstanding!” she said in an interview with Art Outreach, a Singapore-based nonprofit visual arts organization, published in 2021.

Upon his wife’s insistence, Lito said he made sure to also include in his itinerary a visit to the museum, spent an hour looking at Kusama’s work, and was “awed by Kusama’s art as Kim was,” he said in the same interview with Art Outreach.

Play Video

“You have to consider that she started her art back in the ’50s as a Japanese woman who had moved to New York, so she was an outsider, and yet she persisted. I also got a sense of her courage and strong conviction because she was not very successful in the early days. Even her works from the ’50s and ’60s remain as contemporary today, and that shows how significant and important her art is in history. I guess we just fell in love, and that was the start of our love affair with Kusama,” he said.

In 2005, when the Camachos moved to Singapore following a three-year stint in the Arroyo administration, they went to a Kusama exhibition in an art gallery, where they bought their first Kusama pieces. At that time, Lito said the “fairly small works” were still reasonably priced. In the city state, Lito joined investment bank and financial services firm Credit Suisse Singapore and became its CEO from 2007 to 2016.

Kim did more research on Kusama, and the couple decided to “buy as many pieces” as they could given the still reasonable prices. “They were about 10% of what her prices are now. In some cases, even 1%,” she said.

Lito said they “were buying Kusama works wherever we could find them,” and within five years, they “had built enough of a collection to hold our own exhibition.”

“Our Kusama collection continues to grow as we have decided we’d like to hold a major retrospective one day that covers the full spectrum of her works from early to late, small to very large, and all the different mediums, so we still try to fill any gaps we have,” he added.

The couple now has over 100 pieces of Kusama’s works.

Among the popular Kusama works the Camachos purchased were a polka-dotted 300-kilo yellow pumpkin called Great Gigantic Pumpkin, installed in their home in Makati, and a Ladder to Home installation, purchased in 2006, which had amazed Kim when she first saw it in 2004.

“It is mind-boggling when you look up and down and see the ladder going endlessly into infinity. At the Singapore Biennale in 2006, which was the first biennale of Singapore, the work was displayed inside a Hindu temple. I went to see it and was still so impressed, so I persisted in enquiring when one became available, and that is the one we have now,” Kim told Art Outreach.

The ladder is installed in the Camachos’ main living room.

Lito, in an interview with ICON Magazine Singapore, described their Kusama collection as “very studied” and “very deliberate.”

“It’s the whole perspective of Kusama, from the earliest to the latest, in all the medium that she has done,” he said.

“So, from her early drawings and watercolors to works of acrylic on canvas…we have the longest work of Kusama, which is 100 meters long in soft sculpture,” Kim added in the same interview.

In an interview in 2017 with CoBo, a content platform for art enthusiasts, the Camachos said they got to meet Kusama in her studio and spent two hours — instead of an expected 15-minute encounter — with the artist when she was 84 years old.

Play Video

“It was quite an experience; she’s almost childlike. You can tell there’s something very special about her,” Lito said. “We were warned before the visit that if we were able to get 10 or 15 minutes of her time, we’re doing very, very well…. So, we had expected to have a couple of photos, shake her hands, maybe have something signed, and that’s it.”

“I was so delighted with how warm she was to us. I thought she would be forbidding and like standoffish and impossible to touch. [But] no, she was so warm, allowed me to touch her hand,” Kim said. “She was very excited to be with us. She’s so nice.”

Lito was elected chairman of the board of Philippine mining firm Nickel Asia Corporation in June 2024. The couple have philanthropic work as representatives of Scholas Occurrentes, a non-profit organization founded by Pope Francis in 2013 with educational initiatives for young people.

Where to see Yayoi Kusama art in Japan

With Japan rising in popularity for Filipino tourists, the best place to see Kusama’s works is in her own five-story Yayoi Kusama Museum in 107 Bentencho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo, Japan.

DOTS. White polka dots dominate the façade of the Yayoi Kusama Museum in Tokyo, Japan, in this photo taken in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

I got a chance to visit the museum in November 2019, when one could visit even without a booking in advance and without a specified and limited time slot.

BALLOON. The lobby of the Yayoi Kusama Museum has bright red and white colors, with a small souvenir stand in this photo taken in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

There was a multi-color polka-dotted giant silver pumpkin on the top floor of the building.

RAINBOW. A multi-colored, polka-dotted giant silver pumpkin installed at the top floor of the Yayoi Kusama Museum in Tokyo, Japan, in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

It also had a Ladder to Heaven installation with the warning, “For the protection of the artwork and your own safety, make sure not to step on the circular mirror at the bottom of the artwork.”

INFINITY. A peek into Yayoi Kusama’s Ladder to Heaven art installation in her museum in Tokyo, Japan, in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

On what she aspired for in putting up the museum, Kusama said:

“I infused my eternal soul into this museum. I want you to be guided by my sincere desire: I wish for everyone to realize all the inspirations in my art.

RED. A portrait of Yayoi Kusama with red hair hangs in her Tokyo museum in this photo taken in November 2019. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

“The Museum will be a testament to my truth, that I have been living my life. Perhaps the museum can deliver love for all humanity, accompanying both life and death, seeking to attain the world’s supreme peace, having revealed out of all the love a hymn for humanity’s eternal life.

“This is my great hope in founding this museum.”

FREE. No need to pay entrance fees to get a selfie with Yayoi Kusama’s giant pumpkin in Yokohama Art Museum in Odori Park. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

For those traveling to Fukuoka, there’s a Great Gigantic Pumpkin installed outside the Fukuoka Art Museum at the popular tourist spot, Odori Park. It is a cheap and quick way to get a photo with Kusama’s iconic art piece. – Rappler.com

World.title: Nearly a year after Tindig Bulacan, sectoral groups march again vs corruption, reclamation
World.content:
Protesters hold banners calling for accountability over corruption and the protection of the environment in front of the Bulacan Provincial Capitol.

BULACAN, Philippines — Following five weeks of heavy rains, Bulakenyos took to the streets once more on Monday, August 31, demanding accountability and immediate action amid the worsening flooding here.

At the KILOS BULACAN! indignation rally in Malolos, two groups of protesters from student, agricultural, labor, and church organizations marched from the Malolos Crossing and Malolos Digital Amphitheatre before converging at the Bulacan Provincial Capitol Freedom Park. They called for an end to corruption, environmental destruction, and reclamation projects, particularly the New Manila International Airport (NMIA) project in Bulakan.

The Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office reported that 960,821 residents were directly affected by the recent floods, while damage to agriculture, fisheries, livestock, and poultry reached more than P130 million.

Bulacan has been one of the provinces dragged into the flood corruption scandal that blew up last year, with district engineers based in the province eventually getting charged in court for graft and corruption. The Commission on Audit uncovered various ghost and substandard flood control projects here.

A former district engineer had testified that at least 50 ghost flood projects were marked for the province’s first district alone.

From 2021 to 2024, Bulacan was awarded a total of P43.5 billion worth of flood control contracts. Governor Daniel Fernando’s now-viral claim that he had no knowledge of the projects came with an explanation during an August 26 press conference: the funds and projects were handled directly by the national government and agencies.

Fernando’s statement drew criticism among Bulakenyos.

“Hindi rin puwedeng ‘yung gobernador, walang alam. ‘Yung congressman, walang alam. So lahat sila dapat managot kasi kung wala silang alam, dapat magsipag-resign na sila sa puwesto nila. Kasi hindi naman nila pera ‘yan,” said David D’Angelo, environmental advocate and interim spokesperson of KILOS BULACAN! (How can it be that the governor was not aware of this? Even the congressman claims lack of knowledge of these projects. If none of them were aware, then they should just resign.)

PUNISH THE CORRUPT. A protester delivers a solidarity speech as groups from different sectors converge at the Capitol Freedom Park in Malolos.

The group will also hold consultations with sectors across Bulacan as it continues its campaign, D’Angelo said. “Hindi naman po ito dito matatapos kasi lahat ng organisasyon hihilingan natin na magsama-sama,” he added. The group plans to discuss reclamation, including the NMIA project, as well as nature-based solutions and other approaches to flood mitigation.

He said they have requested documents from the office of Vice Governor Alex Castro, including Bulacan’s comprehensive flood mitigation plan. The group plans to study the documents as it considers filing cases against those it holds accountable for environmental destruction. “‘Yung mga dokumento rin na ‘yon ay pag-aaralan natin para magsampa po tayo ng kaso sa mga dapat sampahan, lalong lalo na sa kalaban ng kalikasan at sa salot ng kalikasan na si P.I. Ramon Ang,” D’Angelo said.

Monday’s rally came nearly a year after the Tindig Bulacan movement began, which sparked a series of mobilizations across towns in the province calling for accountability over flood control projects and the use of public funds. – Rappler.com



Mark David Silencio is an Information Technology student at Bulacan State University in Plaridel, Bulacan. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, he is also the managing editor for Administration of Pacesetter.

World.title: EJ Obiena back to golden ways with victory in Germany
World.content:
EFFORT. The Philippines' Ernest John Obiena in action during the men's pole vault final of the 2026 Weltklasse Zurich in Switzerland.

EJ Obiena claims his ninth gold medal of the year by ruling the ISTAF Berlin in Germany

MANILA, Philippines – Another vault, another gold.

EJ Obiena claimed his ninth gold medal of the year after ruling the ISTAF Berlin at the Olympiastadion in Germany on Sunday, August 30 (Monday, August 31, Manila time).

The Filipino pole vault star cleared 5.82 meters in a single attempt as he rediscovered his winning ways after failing to crack the podium in his last three meets.

Play Video

Belgium’s Ylio Philtjens placed second with 5.72m, beating France’s Robin Emig for the silver via countback.

With the gold already in the bag, Obiena tried to eclipse his season best of 5.91m he achieved when he topped the Golden Sand in Poland earlier this August by going for 5.97m but to no avail as he exhausted all of his three tries.

Obiena’s recent form has allowed him to climb to No. 12 in the world rankings — two spots above his No. 14 standing in June.

Enjoying a career resurgence, the former world No. 2 is tagged as one of the Philippines’ best bets in the Asian Games, where he is expected to defend the title he won in the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China.

The upcoming Asian Games will be held in Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4. – Rappler.com

World.title: Pilandok maintains strength; monsoon rain in 3 areas due to ‘habagat’
World.content:
WEATHER. Tropical Depression Pilandok and southwest monsoon inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility as of August 31, 2026, 5:20 pm.

Tropical Depression Pilandok continues to meander over the Philippine Sea east of extreme Northern Luzon, says PAGASA

MANILA, Philippines – Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength on Monday afternoon, August 31, while monsoon rain has eased in some areas, with Ilocos Region, Abra, and Benguet bearing the brunt due to the enhanced southwest monsoon.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said in its 5 pm bulletin Monday that Pilandok was located 1,145 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon, moving north northwestward at 10 kilometers per hour with winds of 55 km/h and gustiness of up to 70 km/h.

Two tropical depressions outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) are enhancing the southwest monsoon.

Tropical Depression Saudel (formerly referred to as Obet), located 1,075 km west of extreme Northern Luzon, has winds of 45 km/h and gustiness of up to 75 km/h. PAGASA Weather Specialist Charmagne Varilla said Saudel could still reenter PAR and redevelop into a tropical storm, but it has a low likelihood of making landfall.

The other tropical depression, located 570 km west northwest of Itbayat, Batanes, has winds of 45 km/h and gustiness of up to 60 km/h. According to Varilla, this tropical depression could eventually be absorbed into Saudel’s circulation, or it could have a “looping track” along the northwestern part, enter PAR, then make landfall in Taiwan.

In either scenario, this tropical depression won’t have a direct effect on the country, but it will continue to enhance the southwest monsoon and bring rain to parts of Luzon and the western section of Visayas.

Another low pressure area being monitored outside PAR has a “medium” chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours. It could enter PAR but is less likely to make landfall and will not affect the country.

Meanwhile, Tropical Depression Pilandok may become almost stationary over the Philippine Sea east of extreme Northern Luzon for the next 36 hours before moving generally north northwestward. It is still less likely to make landfall and will remain far from the Philippine landmass.

Pilandok may intensify into a tropical storm by Tuesday, September 1, before it leaves PAR and moves toward southern Japan.

The enhanced southwest monsoon is bringing monsoon rain to Ilocos Region, Abra, and Benguet, and occasional rain to the rest of Cordillera Administrative Region, Batanes, Nueva Vizcaya, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, and Nueva Ecija.

It is also causing scattered rain and thunderstorms in Metro Manila, Calabarzon, the rest of Cagayan Valley, the rest of Central Luzon, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, Aklan, and Antique, and isolated rain showers or thunderstorms in the rest of Luzon, Negros Island Region, and the rest of Western Visayas.

Below is PAGASA’s latest heavy rainfall outlook for the next three days:

Monday afternoon, August 31, to Tuesday afternoon, September 1:

Heavy to intense rain (100-200 millimeters): Ilocos Sur, La Union, Abra, and Benguet

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Ilocos Norte, Pangasinan, Batanes, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Zambales, and Bataan
